data/story/intro_story.tres::awakening_l: Ugh... where am I? And while I'm asking, who am I?
I keep reaching for my name, or for how I got here, and there's nothing there at all.
I should get up. My legs have other ideas, and every part of me aches.
data/story/intro_story.tres::start.gate_: A cold draft rises out of the dark, smelling of old stone and older water. The stranger said the town lies on the other side. Go in?
data/story/intro_story.tres::prologue.re: Easy. Stay down a moment and get your breath back. After what they put you through, I'm amazed you're breathing at all.
And keep your voice low. We're not the only ones in these woods tonight.
data/story/intro_story.tres::prologue.wa: I don't know this place, and I don't know my own name. ...Who are you?
data/story/intro_story.tres::prologue.re: A friend. That's all I can tell you, and there isn't time for more.
Can you still draw on the Paths? Hold out your hand and let me see.
data/story/intro_story.tres::prologue.wa: ...I feel them. All four, faintly. Like voices through a wall.
data/story/intro_story.tres::prologue.re: Faint will have to do. The Path-ologists are already hunting us.
Tell me: which Path resonates within you?
That one, then. Hold on to it. The others will come back to you, in time.
The Forgotten Cave behind me is your escape. It comes out at {town}, and Elder Maren will be waiting for you there. Find her first.
Hear that? They're close, but they don't know about the cave. Hardly anyone remembers it now.
Go, and don't stop for anything. I'll draw them off the other way, and when I'm clear, I'll find you. I always do.
data/story/intro_story.tres::prologue.wa: She's gone, and she's taking the shouting with her. Whoever they are, I'd rather not meet them.
data/story/intro_story.tres::prologue.se: The trees are packed too tight to get through. The cave it is, then.
No point getting lost twice in one day. I'll head back up the path to the glowing arch.
Whatever is waiting for me, it's through that cave.
Whoever she was, she said help would be waiting on the other side. Whatever's in that cave, it has to be better than those Path-ologists.
data/story/intro_story.tres::tutorial.wa: ...Footsteps. It has been a long time since anything woke me.
No one has walked this way since the house fell silent. I have kept the door all the same.
Turn back. Only one may pass this door, and he is long dead.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Hollow: Then I will do what I was left here to do.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: The Warden Stirs
At half health the Warden wakes a little more: a Cave Echo rises beside it.
...That light in your hands. I know it. No. NO. You cannot be him. He is gone.
A Cave Echo rises beside the Warden.
data/story/intro_story.tres::tutorial.wa: ...The door knows your hand. I do not understand it, but I will not stand against it. Pass, and let the Paths guide you.
The light goes out of the Warden's eyes slowly, like a lamp turned down for the night.
Hmph. About time. {villain}'s soldiers have been up and down the road all day, and nobody has come out of that cave in ten years, so forgive me for staring.
And look at the state of you. I told her I'd help whoever she sent along. I never said I'd take in a half-drowned stray.
I didn't want any part of this, and I told her so. She went ahead anyway. She always does.
But you need a bed, and I've baked far too much pie, so I can hardly leave you out here on your own, can I?
I don't know who I am, or where this is. I don't even know the name of the woman who got me out.

Hm. If she didn't give you her name, she had a reason, and I won't be the one to spoil it. As for where you are: this is {town}. We settle most things here with cards, and I see you've already got a deck.
If your memory's really gone, you'll be here a while, so you'd best get to know people. Say hello to Sable, Tilly and Pip on the square, buy yourself a card from Sable, then come back to me.
data/story/intro_story.tres::start.tunne: A narrow gap in the old treeline - easy to miss, easy enough to slip through, if you're not afraid of a shortcut.
data/story/intro_story.tres::still.wake:: You wake in a forest clearing with leaves in your hair.
A faint glow of four colors fades from your hand, like a thought you almost had.
Someone in a hood is kneeling beside you, shaking your shoulder gently, then less gently. Their face stays in shadow.
data/story/intro_story.tres::equipment_v: Security Protocol One: assess the customer's gait. Adequate - you may approach at your current level of walking.
Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant TO the Regional Merchant. The TO is load-bearing.
Everything on this rack is inventoried and oiled under Security Protocol Seven. Protocol Seven is need-to-know. You do not need to know.
Do not reach for the drawer. Its contents are classified, and so is your interest in them.
A return customer strengthens the economy and my employee-of-the-month case file. Please look satisfied for the record.
Fact: the beets came in early this year, and the bear has been informed. We have an understanding. I do not ask why it is here, and it does not ask about the beets.
I still don't know what to make of you, dearie. But you need feeding more than you need questioning, so sit down a minute.
Have as much pie as you like. Just keep your eyes off the recipe; better people than you have tried.
That tune's stayed with you, hasn't it? I can see it on your face. Good. Keep it somewhere safe, dearie, even when it hurts.
Found any more answers out there? I keep telling myself it's none of my business, and I keep asking anyway.
Somebody in the square says you've a look of the old court about you. 'That's no prince,' I told them. 'That's a damp young man with good posture.'
When you find Wren in the Capital, tell her my pie is still the best thing in the kingdom. She'll argue, and she'll be wrong.
I have told you the worst of me. The rest is easy, by comparison.
Go on, dearie. The next road won't open itself, and if we left it to me, we'd be at it until the regime died of old age.
{prince}. I keep wanting to curtsy. My knees have voted against it.
Go on, then. The kingdom has waited ten years for you; the pie won't wait ten minutes.
{prince}. {villain} let it slip to you, didn't he, that smug man. I had hoped to tell you myself.
Sit down. The rest of your memories will come when they're ready, and I'll be right here when they do. With pie, obviously.
Up and walking. Good. I am Elder Maren, dearie, and this is {town}, where the four Paths used to meet, and argue, and borrow each other's pans.

Ten years ago {kingdom} was whole. Beefcakes kept the lights on, Gourmands fed us, Necrocrats minded the dead and Refusemancers turned rubbish into harvests. Everyone complained, and everything worked.

Then {villain}, the Minister of Improvements, took the Paths one by one and set his own people over them. Now every road out of town has a gatekeeper: a bridge, a barrier, a pantry door, a wall of thorns.
Beat a road's gatekeeper and that road opens. Before you try, buy a few cards from Sable and sort your deck at the Deck Station. Then come back to me for pie. Pie, mind. Not answers.
Four roads out of town, dearie: the Gainlands, the Buffet, the D.N.A. and the Dump. Pick one and see it through before you start the next.
For all I know, you're somebody's spy. I've been wrong about people before. Once, in 1987.
Still here, dearie? {villain} would like nothing better than you sitting by my fire forever, so don't give him the satisfaction. And give me back my chair.
The pie on the sill needs another hour, dearie. You don't. Off you go.
If you're looking for advice: eat something. If you're looking for more advice: eat something else.
I've given you all the answers you need for now, dearie. Further questions require fieldwork.
Mind the fountain, dearie. People throw wishes in it. Most of them are mine.
Off you go, dearie. I'll be here when you get back. Tortoises are very dependable, just not quickly.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.guard:: Hm. You came back. Wrote it in the notebook: 'came back.' Best two words I know.
Gate stays open. Always has. My girl's still up that road somewhere, and I'd hate for her to come home and find it shut.
Hm. That road goes to the Capital. You'll be wanting to know why nobody comes back from it.
Four Paths kept that city alive. Beefcakes ran the lights, Gourmands the kitchens, Necrocrats the graveyards, Refusemancers the bins. Then {villain} chained all four.
So now it's Blackout, Famine, Restless Dead and Clutter up there. Dark streets, slow legs, no food that heals, rubbish in your deck.
You could walk in today, but you wouldn't get far. Free the four zones first. Each one you free turns one of those services back on.
My girl Isla went up that road eight years ago. If you see her... tell her the gate is still open.
Hm. Services still broken up there. The board by the road keeps count, if you want to check.
Hm. Each zone you free turns another service back on, and the castle gets a little less frightening. My knees, sadly, are a local problem.
Hm. All four zones free. The lights are on up there. I can see them from here.
Go on, knock on that castle door, and knock hard. And if you see Isla up there... tell her I'm still watching the road.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.vendor: Well met, {wanderer}. Sable, darling: seller of cards, and of very good stories about cards.
Your deck's all plain neutral cards, darling: honest, dependable and dull. The power is in the Paths. Buy a few, then put them to work at the Deck Station.
Where do my cards come from? The past, darling. Next question. My prices are fair, more or less; {villain}'s taxes on them are not.
Back, darling? The cards are honest; the misprints simply have a more adventurous relationship with spelling.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.item_v: Hi! Hello! You look like you need supplies! Tilly Tonic! I'm teal today, which means the new batch works!
Everything here is one use in a fight! Equip what you buy on your Character screen, then use it on your turn!
Probably not on yourself! Unless it's a healing one! I tested the healing one! I'm fine! I'm green! I'm usually green!
First visit gets a freebie! Power Wraps! Wrap a unit, it gets tougher for the whole fight! I wrapped my own arm once! Still tough! Still a bit stuck!
Here's how! Press C, or Menu then Character! Find Items, the big shiny panel!
Click the Power Wraps, then click an empty slot! Done! Whatever's in a slot comes with you into every fight!
One wrap, one use, then it's gone! More on my shelf! I'm green again! Green means business is good!
Did you equip the Power Wraps yet? Press C! Items! Click the wraps, then an empty slot!
I'll wait! I'm bad at waiting! I'm turning yellow!
Back for more potions! Equip them on your Character screen before a fight! Maybe skip the orange one until I stop matching it!
data/story/intro_story.tres::storeroom.l: The door rattles. Something behind it is muttering about a receipt.
Whatever it is, it sounds like it has been on hold for a very long time.
data/story/intro_story.tres::storeroom.b: OooOOOooo. Who disturbs the store room? We are VERY busy haunting it.
Ninety years ago the three of us went halves - well, thirds - on one lantern, and it never worked. Tilly's great-grandmother said no receipt, no refund.
We waited, died, and kept waiting. Your haunting is very important to us.
data/story/intro_story.tres::storeroom.w: ...You're haunting a shop over a lantern.
data/story/intro_story.tres::storeroom.c: A FAULTY lantern, for four copper. We worked out ninety years' interest and it's still four copper. We had the time.
Nobody comes in until it's refunded, or until somebody beats us at cards. That's how everything gets settled round here, living or otherwise.
data/story/intro_story.tres::storeroom.a: ...Fine. FINE. You play like someone who kept the receipt.
We'll go. The chapel belfry has a lovely draught and nobody has complained about it in centuries.
Tell Tilly the lantern's on the top shelf, still broken after ninety years of nightly checks. We were thorough, if poorly lit.
Ha! No refund, no entry. Come back with a better deck. Or a receipt. Ideally both.
data/story/intro_story.tres::storeroom.c: Just shelves now. And one broken lantern on the top shelf, exactly where they said it would be.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.equipm: Halt. Security Protocol Two. Equipment is issued on referral only, and Elder Maren does the referring.
Bring Elder Maren's blessing. Better posture is appreciated but cannot be accepted in its place.
data/story/intro_story.tres::quest.armor: Elder Maren sent you; I could tell from your gait, which now says 'referred'. Congratulations. Your file is finally thick enough to be a file.
Before I issue gear, protocol requires exactly one thing: win a fight. Any fight counts, and I will know if you lie.
Fact: things roam the outskirts, on the lanes round the edge of town. They are rude, they are close, and they are not on my referral list.
Beat one. Then come back and I will hand you something pointy.
One fight won. That is the whole requirement. So far I count zero. I am very good at counting to zero.
Security Protocol Four: check the outskirts. Enemies roam the lanes round the edge of town, and any win counts.
I will be here, guarding the drawer. The drawer does not know. That is the point.
Security Protocol Nine: gear in a bag protects nobody. Equip it.
Press C, click the Weapon slot on the figure, choose the blade and press Equip. Four steps. I have written them down for you, in my head.
Unequipped gear will be noted in your file. Your file is already very thick.
The blade is still in the bag. I can see the bag. The bag can see me.
Menu. Character. Weapon slot. Equip. Security Protocol Nine does not repeat itself. I am repeating it for you as a courtesy.
One fight, won. Stamp. Stamp. Stamp. Three stamps is the correct number of stamps.
Security Protocol Twelve: report to Elder Maren. She decides where things get pointed.
Your Starter Blade. The first unit you play each battle hits a little harder. Do not run with it.
And all five equipment slots are yours now: helm, weapon, armor, boots, relic.
The good stuff is rarer, and you can only wear so much of it until you level up. Protocol. Fact: bears do not wear helms. Bears are wiser than us.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.hidden: You found the chest, so I suppose you've earned a look. Epic and Legendary goods, quiet prices.
{villain}'s tax collectors don't know this stall exists. Let's keep it that way. Shh.
A cellar hatch beside the old cottage, chained shut. Someone has scratched two little crossed swords into the wood.
Somewhere below, very faintly, someone is rehearsing the word CHAMPION. Not yet, apparently.
Word around the square: the abandoned cottage at the end of Champions' Road has started roaring at night.
From the cellar. Somebody brave should check the hatch. Somebody like you.
WELCOME TO THE UNDERCROFT, CHAMPION! I AM ANNOUNCER GRAND BELLOWS, KEEPER OF THE SAND! (normal voice) Mind the third stair. It's loose, and it holds a grudge.
For a thousand years the four Paths settled their rivalries in the old arena, until {villain} chained the doors. SO WE DUG.
Since you freed a zone, THE RING IS OPEN! Battles and puzzles, tiers one to three, with prizes: ring-exclusive gear, gold, essence!
First clears pay out. Repeats are for GLORY. And for snacks. I brought snacks.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Announ: IN THIS CORNER: A CHALLENGER! IN THAT CORNER: ME! (normal voice) Hello.
THE SAND IS HOT AND THE CEILING IS LOW! Pick a fight, champion - the crowd is mostly my echo, and he agrees with EVERYTHING!
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.alchem: The door of Auntie Alembic's is bolted. A note is pinned to it in green ink, in what looks like four handwritings at once:
'CLOSED UNTIL TWO ZONES ARE FREE. {villain} TOOK MY CAULDRON. I AM BREWING IN THE SINK. THE SINK IS COPING. - A.'
With two zones free, a cauldron bubbles to life in {town}. Auntie Alembic's is open! Bring essence. Bring courage. Bring a fire blanket.
Auntie Alembic, dear: alchemist, and keeper of some very nervous glassware. Don't touch anything. ...Oh, fine, touch that one. It likes you.
When you collect more copies of a card than you can carry, dear, the extras boil down into essence of that card's Path. Nothing goes to waste here.

Bring me six essence each of two Paths, plus 100 gold, and I'll brew you a card of BOTH. Which card is up to the cauldron, and now and then it's on fire. I only take what the brew needs; the rest stays in your jars.
Your jars hold eighteen of a Path. Past that it evaporates, and my ceiling gets a new colour.
They say there was one spring once, the Wellspring, that fed all four Paths. Everything mixed at the source, dear. That is the kingdom I brew for.
Six essence each of two Paths and 100 gold, dear, and the cauldron does the rest. Lower your voice near the red flask. It takes things personally.
Oh, and here. A starter jar of every Path, six of each. Enough for one brew of any two. Don't drink it. People drink it.
You do not have enough essence of two different Paths yet. Collect more duplicates, then come back. The cauldron will wait.
The cauldron is patient. Please don't confuse patience with having had lunch.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.object: {villain} rules the four Paths through his rulers. Beat each road's gatekeeper, then free its zone by beating the boss of its main dungeon.
The imperial road to the Capital is open from the start, but its broken services will flatten you. Free the zones first. Gatekeeper Brannoch can explain.
All four Paths are free. Buy cards, test yourself in the Undercroft, and brew something dangerous at the Alchemist's.
Something under the old cottage at the end of Champions' Road is open for business. Listen for the crowd.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.alchem: Auntie Alembic's, the Alchemist, is now open in {town}. Bring your leftovers.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.pack_v: Psst... hear that crinkle? That's possibility, with excellent packaging.
Foil Fenwick, Purveyor of Sealed Goods - packs only. Open one where the light's good; if I cry, I want to see what I'm crying about.
Here's how it works: whenever a Path's final dungeon falls, that Path sends me its pack. Don't ask how. There's a great deal of foil and no paperwork at all, which the Necrocrats find upsetting.
Free a zone and I'll stock its pack; until then it's just a rumour in a wrapper. Browse, sniff if you like. I won't judge. I sniff.
Browse, sniff, but don't shake the packs. ...A little, then; I'm a collector, not a strong person.
A repeat customer... shh, listen to that foil. You understand me, and I don't know what to do with that.
Fenwick pulls a curtain aside. "The back room. Prismatic packs: every Path in one wrapper.
They only exist because the Paths are talking to each other again. Terrible for my exclusivity. Wonderful for my sales."
data/story/intro_story.tres::pack.vendor: Crinkle! You've made a wrapper very happy.
No refunds on bad luck. Bad luck is non-transferable.
It wants to be opened. I'm trying to respect its wishes without getting involved.
Gold, friend. The foil does not accept good intentions.
Not enough gold. The wrapper can tell.
Not yet. That one is still a rumour in a wrapper.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.tailor: Look closely. Every stitch tells a story; the good ones tell it with a feather.
Hat! Hat. Marvellous head. Hold still: your left shoulder is a size braver than your right.
Pip Threadwell, Haberdasher and Hemmer! Everything in here is purely cosmetic. It will not make you stronger, braver or better at card games.
It will make you LOOK all three, which is eighty percent of the job. Try anything on in the little mirror first: hats up top, cloaks down the back, dye on both.
Free zones and climb levels, and I will find grander stock. I hear rumours of rarer pieces, too. People tell hatmakers everything.
Back to change your mind and your hat? Excellent - one of those I can fit properly.
My favourite head, in the nick of time! Brim, brooch or billowing - this could be a hem-ergency.
Oh, you have been busy. New fabrics arrived. Do not ask where from. Some of them were yelling.
Stock has grown! Freed zones send me their finest fashions. Slightly singed, mostly fabulous.
Between us: a crown made of living leaves is growing in a bin somewhere in the Verdant Dump. And a cloak that has survived more than you have is draped over a chest on a muscly island.
And the Capital's mantle... well. Someone must defeat its owner first. The mantle, frankly, is rooting for you.
data/story/intro_story.tres::tailor.boug: Gorgeous. Truly. You are going to turn heads, mostly in confusion.
Wear it out! A hat cannot have an entrance if you keep it in a bag!
Sold! Such a dramatic fit - the hat looks surprised to be wearing you.
data/story/intro_story.tres::tailor.poor: Gold, my dear head. Thread is not free, and neither is my charm.
A little more gold, my dear head. I can work wonders with fabric, but it insists on being paid for.
data/story/intro_story.tres::tailor.lock: Not yet. That one is still on the sewing table, and it is sulking.
data/story/intro_story.tres::tailor.equi: Hat! On the head, where hats belong. My work here is done. Briefly.
A classic. Wear it like you mean it, and tilt it a fraction left. Your left. No, my left. Perfect.
data/story/intro_story.tres::tailor.bare: No hat. Bold. Brave. Wrong, but brave.
The bare-head look! I shall lie down in the back for a moment. Carry on.
data/story/intro_story.tres::tailor.owne: You own that one already! Do introduce it to the outside world.
data/story/intro_story.tres::tailor.plai: The Plain Cloak, undyed! Classic. Humble. Secretly the best cut in the shop. I made it, so I would know.
data/story/intro_story.tres::tailor.dyed: A new colour! Hold still while the cloak gets used to it. Gasp. It suits you. It suits it.
Dyed and dried! Walk into the light. No, more light. There. Devastating.
data/story/intro_story.tres::tailor.cloa: Cloak! Over the shoulders, swishing on cue. Do turn around once. For me.
A cloak with a past. You will give it a future. Mind the hem on stairs.
data/story/intro_story.tres::pack.hint.p: Stocked once the Gainlands' final dungeon is cleared.
Stocked once the Endless Buffet's final dungeon is cleared.
Stocked once the Verdant Dump's final dungeon is cleared.
Stocked once the D.N.A.'s final dungeon is cleared.
data/story/intro_story.tres::pack.hint.g: Fig can only get these once the Gainlands are free.
Fig can only get these once the Endless Buffet is free.
Fig can only get these once the Verdant Dump is free.
Fig can only get these once the D.N.A. is free.
The back crates open at level 10, or once two zones are free, whichever comes first.
data/story/intro_story.tres::pack.card_v: Sable pats a stack of wrapped bundles. "Surprise packs, darling. Fresh from the crates, and I never ask a crate where it has been.
What's inside? The crate has declined to comment, darling, and I admire a professional."
Sable grins at you. "The back crates are open, darling - more cards, bigger surprises, the same discreet fainting policy."
data/story/intro_story.tres::pack.black_: Fig Sly taps a gold-edged wrapper. "Guaranteed good stuff. Do not ask where the guarantee comes from.
It is not legal. It is, however, very shiny."
data/story/intro_story.tres::pack.reward: The Path sends you its pack: %s.
Where every champion starts: loud, dusty and mostly forgiving.
The crowd has stopped laughing and started betting.
Only legends stand here. Only the sand remembers who fell.
data/story/intro_story.tres::arena.arena: Warm-Up Brawl
A rookie gladiator rattles inside oversized armor. Bring your own deck; the armor has enough room for its own audience.
Your own deck, full HP. Win the duel.
Lethal Lunch
The lunch rush has an enemy blocker, ten HP and no mercy. You have exactly one turn and just enough energy.
PUZZLE: win THIS turn. Preset board. If the turn ends and your opponent still stands, you lose.
The Neutral Mile
The Marshal's favorite warm-down: no Paths, no tricks, no excuses. Everyone fights with a borrowed gladiator's kit.
RESTRICTED DECK: you fight with the Gladiator's Kit (neutral cards), not your own deck.
Hold the Line
A stampeding squad charges across the sand before you can even take a breath. You only have to outlast them.
PUZZLE: survive 3 of the enemy's turns. Preset board; the enemy moves first. You win when the third enemy turn ends and you still stand.
Spells Only, Please
The Cardboard Colossus does not like being hit by anything with a heartbeat. Win without playing a single unit.
RESTRICTED DECK + RULE: you fight with the Spellslinger's Satchel and may NOT play unit cards this duel.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Getting Soggy
At half health the Colossus gets soggy: its units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
THE COLOSSUS IS... DAMP! (normal voice) Someone left the mop bucket out again.
The Colossus is soggy: its units get -1/-0.
data/story/intro_story.tres::arena.arena: The Four Fists
A champion who fights with every Path at once, and has a fist for each. Bring your best deck.
Your own deck, full HP. Win the duel.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: The Fourth Fist
At half health the Champion uses its fourth fist: its units get +1/+0 for the rest of the fight.
THE CHAMPION RAISES ITS FOURTH FIST! (normal voice) Nobody knows where it keeps it.
The Champion's units get +1/+0.
data/story/intro_story.tres::arena.arena: Zero to Hero
The Wall of Fame has two blockers and eleven HP. The crowd has already booked your funeral. Show them lethal.
PUZZLE: win THIS turn. Preset board, five energy, two blockers to deal with.
The Marshal
Announcer Grand Bellows steps onto the sand. He has not lost a bout in eleven years. He is smiling, and so is the moustache.
Your own deck, full HP. Win the duel. No excuses.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: THE CROWD GOES WILD
On his 3rd turn the crowd joins in: a 1/1 Rowdy Fan climbs into the ring.
Next turn: a fan climbs into the ring.
THE CROWD! GOES! WILD! (normal voice) Could the crowd please stay behind the rope? I put up a rope.
A 1/1 Rowdy Fan climbs into the ring.
INTERMISSION
At half health Bellows calls an intermission: he heals 2, and his units sit down through his next turn.
INTERMISSION! (normal voice) Everybody sit down a minute. I've brought a flask of soup, and my voice needs it more than I do.
Bellows heals 2; his units sit out his next turn.
data/story/intro_story.tres::arena.scree: The gates are chained until the first zone is free.
data/story/intro_story.tres::arena.won.f: VICTORY ON THE SAND - THE PRIZE IS YOURS! (normal voice) Mind your head on the way up to collect it. The ceiling doesn't celebrate.
data/story/intro_story.tres::arena.won.r: ANOTHER WIN FOR THE BOOKS! (normal voice) Here's a few coins from the crowd. The crowd is me, but I mean every one of them.
data/story/intro_story.tres::arena.lost:: NOT THIS TIME, CHAMPION! Come back whenever you're ready; the sand has yet to win a rematch.
data/story/intro_story.tres::arena.puzzl: PUZZLE SOLVED - THE CROWD GOES WILD! (normal voice) Lovely bit of thinking, that. I could hear the gears turning from the booth.
THE PUZZLE WINS THIS ROUND! (normal voice) Have a good long look at the board and try again. It's not going anywhere, and neither am I.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.subt: Rips while-you-wait. Tips accepted in protein.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.here: You are here. A Rip is stationed here.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.lock: No station yet. Walk into that town yourself and a cousin will turn up and rip one into the nearest wall.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.warn: Ripping out of a zone ends your visit: you arrive at full HP, and the roaming enemies there come back. Rips are free, and so is the spotting.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.oper: Rip Tearson (Cousin #4, the One Who Eats)
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.stat: The home station. A well-supported sky is a happy sky.
The elevator lobby, where a cousin ripped it into the wall beside the Out-Of-Order sign. It's the only thing in the building that works.
Between the hot tub and the protein stand, where the gains are public.
The Endless Buffet: The Grand Pantry
A short walk from the heavy meal table. The cousin ripped it open right by the napkins, so you'll never arrive without one.
The Verdant Dump: The Compost Grange
Right by the harvest table. The Rip on duty is slightly damp, but then so is everything else out there.
A rip into the hideout under the Capital. Don't ask how we found it; we followed the smell of Fig Sly's hot sauce straight through the fabric of space.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.intr: HNNNGH. SPOTTER! Spot me! No, not you, the other guy. ...Hello. Welcome to the Beefcake Rift Express.
We tear the world open so you don't have to walk, buddy. Two men hold the sky - that's our overhead.
The sky is heavier than it looks, buddy, so we never skip sky day. Do not look at the seam. It's working very hard and it's shy about it.
Reach a new town and we send a cousin to rip a station there. Every one of them is called Rip. Our mother found a name she liked and saw no reason to stop.
After that, you can rip between any two stations. Thank you for ripping with the Express. Please keep your elbows inside the sky.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.retu: Back for another rip, buddy? Say where and we'll tear it right open. Rips are free, same as always.
Spotting is free, buddy. Water, sadly, you'll have to bring yourself.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.intr: HNNNGH... Rip Tearson, Beefcake Rift Express, serving this exact spot. I'm a cousin; we hire entirely on relative strength.
We are all very proud of one another and rarely speak.
Say where, buddy. We will rip it.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.retu: Need a rip, brother? I've held this sky since breakfast, and I'd hate to put it down with no one through it.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.intr: Shhh. Keep it down, buddy, there's a Wrinkle asleep behind the crates. Rip Tearson, Cousin Number Seven, Rift Express. Allegedly.
They told me this place didn't exist, so I ripped a hole to it anyway. Sometimes you just have to believe in yourself. The sauce smell helped.
Grab the edges! On three! One!
Hold the sky, brother! Feel the burn! RRRRRIP!
Spot this whole dimension, brother! Lift with your LEGS! Nobody ever tore the sky open with their lower back!
Loosen the shoulders. Roll the neck. Tear a hole in the fabric of space. And never, ever skip leg day.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.arri: The rift folds shut behind you with a very satisfied pop. A nearby Beefcake flexes at the hole to say well done.
The rift drops you by the lobby elevator and pops shut. You catch a fluttering memo: YOU WERE NOT AUTHORIZED TO ARRIVE.
You turn the memo over, looking for an approved way to have arrived. There isn't one.
The rift spits you out next to the Swole Station. A passing brute gives you a thumbs-up, then another to himself, then one to the hole.
You land in the Pantry, and someone hands you a napkin before you've found your feet.
You arrive at the Grange in a whiff of ozone, mulch and gym sock, and the gym sock is definitely the Express.
The rift spits you out in the Crease. Somebody says shh. Somebody else says it was not them. The rift closes politely.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.unlo: A Beefcake cousin has ripped a Rift Station into this town. Fast travel unlocked.
Rift Station unlocked: the Department of Necrotic Affairs. A cousin ripped it in beside the Out-Of-Order sign. Fast travel to and from here is now open.
Rift Station unlocked: the Gainlands. Two cousins have ripped it in with their bare hands and are now doing a victory pose. Fast travel to and from here is now open.
Rift Station unlocked: the Endless Buffet. A cousin ripped it in, then asked if there were seconds. Fast travel to and from here is now open.
Rift Station unlocked: the Verdant Dump. A cousin ripped it in, then looked at his hands, then at the hole, then at his hands again. Fast travel to and from here is now open.
Rift Station unlocked: the Crease, the hideout under the Capital. A very quiet cousin ripped it in. Fast travel to and from here is now open.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.sign: Rips while-you-wait. Space torn to order. No refunds on the sky.
A cousin is on duty. Do not look at the seam.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.stat: A hasty rip between the trees where you first woke up. There's a hatch south of the clearing now that nobody remembers being there, and it smells like a hospital.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.intr: HNNNGH. Rip Tearson, Cousin Number Eight, rift technician and tree enthusiast. This is where I found the hatch, buddy, and no, I didn't open it.
Say the word and I'll rip you back to {town}. Or, if you're going down the hatch, I'll hold the sky open till you're back up.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.retu: Back to {town}, buddy, or down the hatch? Either way, I've been holding this sky since breakfast and it's ready when you are.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.arri: Forest station! Mind the roots. And the hatch. Mostly the hatch.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.fore: Spotter! Big news. You know that forest outside town, where you first turned up?

I went up there on my day off and saw some very interesting things. The brambles south of the clearing just... let go, and there's a path now, with a hatch at the end that was NOT there before. Glowing roots, and a hospital smell.
I did not open it. I have manners, and also I am scared. But I did put a rift station up there, so you can pop over whenever you like.
It is on the Express now. Come to any of my stations, say 'forest', and I will tear it right open.
Whatever is under that hatch, it is yours, I think. It feels like yours. Be careful, buddy.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.unlo: Rift Station unlocked: the forest outside {town}. Rip has torn it open where you first woke up. Fast travel to and from here is now open.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: Sable, Tilly and Pip, dearie, all three on the square. And buy a card from Sable while you're there. I'll not have you facing the roads with nothing but what a cave gave you.
Back already? Let me guess: Sable charmed you, Tilly turned a colour, and Pip measured you before you'd finished saying hello. That's {town}, dearie.
Here, have a trophy. Everybody gets one, so don't let it go to your head. I made it myself, and the handle comes off if you wave it about.
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::_first: Maren says a deck you never chose is a deck you'll lose with. Open a pack for some new cards, then make the deck your own at the Deck Station.
Menu (top right), then Packs - or press P
Open the Deck Station and save your deck to a slot
The Deck Station, on Champions' Road south of the square
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: Now, about that deck of yours. You didn't choose a single card in it, dearie, and a deck you never chose is a deck you'll lose with.
New cards first, so open a pack: the Menu at the top right, then Packs. Or press P, if you're the sort who presses things.
Then take it to the Deck Station, down Champions' Road south of the square. Swap in whatever you like, save it to a slot, and come and tell me how it went.
No packs at all? Here, dearie, have a General Pack. It's been sat on a little. Cards are cards, and these ones won't hold it against you.
Open the pack first, dearie: the Menu, then Packs. It won't open itself. I've asked it nicely.
The Deck Station is down Champions' Road, south of the square, dearie. Save it to a slot when you're done, or it doesn't count. I do check.
Sorted and saved, and every card in it your own choice. Good. Now when it loses, you've nobody to blame but yourself, which is how it ought to be.
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::_store: Tilly Tonic's store room has been rattling and moaning for a week, and nobody can get in. Maren wants it sorted, and so, very much, does Tilly.
Open the store room door beside Tilly Tonic's shop
The row house beside Tilly Tonic's Supplies, on the north side of the square
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: Now, a favour. Tilly's store room, the corner house beside her shop, has been moaning for a week. I don't mean Tilly, dearie. I mean the room.
Ghosts, I expect, and petty ones, which are the worst kind. Nobody's been able to get in for so much as a candle. Go and sort them out, gently if they'll let you.
The store room door is beside Tilly's shop, on the north side of the square. Ignore the rattling, dearie; that's just them being dramatic.
A refund? Ninety years of moaning, all over one broken lantern. I've had customers like that. I still have a few.
Well done, dearie. You've settled the ghosts, so now go and settle yourself somewhere dry before you catch a chill.
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::_armor: Maren says it's time you had something sharper than a deck. Bertram Beetsworth issues gear strictly by the book: report to his smithy, then win one fight to earn it.
Report to Bertram Beetsworth at his smithy
Bertram Beetsworth's Smithy, on the west side of Crosspath's square
Enemies roam the outskirts, on the lanes round the edge of Crosspath. Any win counts
Bertram Beetsworth's Smithy, on the west side of Crosspath's square
Equip your new blade: press C (Character), then the Weapon slot
Your Character page (Menu > Character): click the Weapon slot
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: Right, then. It's time you had something sharper than a deck. Bertram Beetsworth hands out gear from his smithy, on the west side of the square.
He is... thorough. Report to him, do what he asks, and do not touch his drawer.
Bertram's smithy is on the west side of the square. Win him one fight, any fight at all, and he'll stamp something for you. He lives to stamp things.
Armed now, are we? Good. Then it's time I pointed you somewhere. Start with {zone}, dearie. It's {path} country, and so, by the look of you, are you.
{vendor} sells more {path} cards out there than anyone in this town does, so take gold and a good big bag. And take my advice, for once.
Inside {zone}, your Path stands a little taller. {buff}: {buff_text}
The Paths quarrel, dearie: Beefcake against Necrocrat, Gourmand against Refusemancer. They always have. Once, they needed each other too much for it to matter.
So in {zone}, it's the {rival} side that gets the short end. {debuff}: {debuff_text} In {rival_zone}, it's the other way round, and you're the one who suffers.
{gatekeeper} holds the way in, and you'll have to win that fight before anything else. Then come back alive. I'll have a pie waiting, and I don't bake for people who don't come back.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: A gravedigger in a battered top hat leans on his shovel among the headstones, consulting a little black book.
Evening! Old Hob, at your service. I dig, mostly, though there's not been much call for it these ten years. Nobody's been collected, you see. Paperwork. Heh.
What are you writing?
Appointments. Let's have a look for you... hm. Not for a good long while yet. Lovely! That's what I like to see.
Mind the cairn at the end of the row. Something under it is still counting its turns, and it's rude to keep a thing like that waiting. Heh.
Still digging, slowly. Two particular graves, these ten years now. I like to take my time over the important ones. Heh.
What are you writing?
Appointments. Let's have a look for you... hm. Not for a good long while yet. Lovely! That's what I like to see.
Hm? You? Not on my list. Off you pop. Heh.
Small handling fee, mind. The shovel doesn't polish itself.
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::_under: {villain} is gone, but Rip found something in the forest where you first woke: a hatch that wasn't there before. Whatever is down there feels like yours, and so does someone.
Ask Rip at Crosspath's Rift Station what he found
The Rift Express station in Crosspath
Take the Rift Express to the forest where you woke
Any Rift Express station: choose the forest
Find the hatch at the end of the new path, south of the clearing
Down the new path south of the forest clearing
Below the hatch: the Cell Block branch
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::_alemb: Auntie Alembic's cauldron is bubbling again. She brews cards of two Paths at once out of essence, and she has a starter jar for you.
Auntie Alembic's, the alchemist's shop in Crosspath
Brew a card of two Paths at her cauldron
Auntie Alembic's cauldron: pick two Paths
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::_loose: {villain} is gone, but the kingdom is not quite done with you. A mountain nobody has climbed, a secret Rip has been keeping, and a crowd under Crosspath that wants a show.
Climb Mount Swolympus: Old Man Mountain at the Swole Station knows the way up
Old Man Mountain, in front of the gym hall in the Gainlands
Find out what is under the forest (Under the Forest)
Win a bout in the Arena, down the cellar hatch in Crosspath
The cellar hatch to the Undercroft, in Crosspath
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::_meet_: Elder Maren wants you fed, kitted out and known in town. Say hello to the shopkeepers on the square and buy yourself a card. There's a trophy in it, though everyone gets the trophy.
Say hello to Tilly Tonic at her supply shop
Tilly Tonic's Supplies, on the north side of Crosspath's square
Equip Tilly's Power Wraps: press C, pick them in Items, then an empty slot
Your Character page (Menu > Character): the Items panel
Say hello to Sable at her card shop
Sable's Cards, on the west side of Crosspath's square
Sable's Cards, on the west side of Crosspath's square
Say hello to Pip Threadwell at the hat shop
Threadwell's Hats & Hems, on the east side of Crosspath's square
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::_free_: {villain}'s Capital runs on four stolen services. Free each Path zone to break one, then storm the castle.
The castle on its hill, up the palace avenue
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::_zone_: zone main quest for an unknown zone %s
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Cracks in the Glass
Wren says one of the mirrors at the castle door has cracked from the inside, and it is still showing a kingdom that never was. Go and look.
Look into the cracked mirror at the castle door
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-ELDER.barks::0: Slow and steady, dearie. I invented that. The hare has never forgiven me.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-ELDER.barks::1: Kettle's on and the pie's cooling. Neither's for you, dearie. Well. Both are.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-GATEKEEPER.bark: Hm. Wrote you in the book. 'Stranger, damp.' I'll add a name when you've got one.
Hm. Gate's never locked. Somebody might come home late.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-SABLE.barks::0: Two typos and a misprint, darling. Such a small card, such a complicated past.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-SABLE.barks::1: Where's it from? The past, darling. Next question.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-TONIC.barks::0: Fresh tonics! I tested every one this morning, and I'm teal, so they work!
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-TONIC.barks::1: Emergency tonic! I keep inventing new emergencies just to test it on!
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-BEETSWORTH.barks:: Fact: bears cannot open the drawer. Neither can you. Security Protocol Three.
Assistant TO the Regional Merchant. The TO is load-bearing. Say it.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-THREADWELL.barks:: Hat! Your next adventure needs a dramatic opening! Preferably above the eyebrows!
Gossip: there's a cloak on a very muscly island. I've said too much. Hat!
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-FENWICK.barks::0: Shh. That crinkle? Foil. Please let it finish.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-FENWICK.barks::1: Free a road and its pack comes in. I'll be here, providing shelf esteem.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-ALEMBIC.barks::0: The flasks all bubbled when you passed, dear. Every colour. They never do that for me.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-ALEMBIC.barks::1: They say one spring once fed all four Paths. Mixed, dear. Like a good soup.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-BELLOWS.barks::: LADIES AND GENTLEMEN! ...Oh. Just you. Hi. THE ECHO SAYS HI TOO.
IN THIS CORNER: MY LUNCH! (normal voice) It's soup. The soup is winning.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-BRONSON.barks::: Never lift alone. An old man told me that. Haven't seen him in years. Huh.
Water, then a stretch. Sorry, was that an order? I meant we could do them together.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-PALLOR.barks::0: Stamp, stamp. Old habits die hard. Unlike me.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-PALLOR.barks::1: I own two stamps: DENIED and APPROVED. One of them is very well rested.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-GRAVOIS.barks::: Taste it. Go on. Somebody in this kingdom ought to taste something.
The pantry key is shaped like a ladle. Don't ask why. The answer is soup.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-MULLIGAN.barks:: ...the green is hungry... Oh! Sorry. Did I thorn at you? I thorn when nervous.
The raccoons are very good boys. Don't tell them. They'll get ideas.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-VILLAGER.barks:: Fresh bread! Flour in my whiskers again, but the rolls came out lovely. Want one?
I knead a holiday, but the dough won't hear of it. Busy, busy badger.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-TOWNSFOLK.barks: Say what you like about His Perfection, the wells are clean. Shh. Don't, actually.
The old cottage cheers at night now, from the cellar. I've decided to find it lovely.
The well hummed at me. Wells don't hum. I said thank you anyway.
Four plinths round the fountain, and nobody remembers what stood on them.
data/story/intro_story.tres::gate.beefca: You actually did it - Grandmaster Flex is out! First thing he did was make me stretch for forty minutes. I cried twice, but they were good tears. Stretchy ones.
The bridge stays down now, but I still oil the crank every morning. Maintenance is how I say sorry, and I've got a lot of sorry left to get through.
Want to spar? Gently, I mean. I'll spot you. I'm still a spotter, I just get to say it at a normal volume now, and honestly, it's a huge relief.
The bridge is drawn up on the far side of the gorge. Somebody very large is standing by the crank, shouting about hydration.
Brick Bronson cracks his knuckles, takes the crank in one hand and lowers the bridge with it, making very sure you're watching.
The planks thump down across the gorge, and the road into the Gainlands lies open.
data/story/intro_story.tres::beefcake_np: NOBODY CROSSES THE GORGE WITHOUT A SPOTTER. I AM THE SPOTTER.
THE BRIDGE STAYS UP BY ORDER OF CHANCELLOR CLENCH! ONLY IRON MATTERS! ...AND HYDRATION! (quieter) The regime is very big on hydration.
YOU WANT THE CRANK? EARN IT! TEN REPS, NO REST! I HAVE NOT SAT DOWN SINCE SPRING AND I FEEL FANTASTIC!
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Brick: SPOTTERS ONLY. I AM SPOTTERS. ...SPOTTER. I AM ONE SPOTTER.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: HYDRATION BREAK
At half health Brick stops to drink: he heals 3, and his units stand down through his next turn.
HYDRATION BREAK. NOBODY LIFTS DURING HYDRATION. THAT IS THE LAW. ...It is a good law.
Brick heals 3. His units are exhausted and miss his next turn.
data/story/intro_story.tres::beefcake_np: ...Oh no. Was I yelling? I was yelling, wasn't I. I'm so sorry - that was the pre-workout talking, and it doesn't know when to stop.
Chancellor Clench had Grandmaster Flex locked away under the House of Gains, ten years ago now. Folks still whisper that the old man never broke. I should've whispered with them instead of yelling.
The bridge is yours, friend. Stretch before you cross, though - a pulled hamstring is a terrible souvenir.
HA! THE PUMP IS STILL MINE! GO HOME AND HYDRATE! THAT IS AN ORDER, NOT CONCERN! ...IT IS A LITTLE BIT CONCERN.
COME BACK WHEN YOU CAN LIFT! THE BRIDGE STAYS UP, AND SO DO I! NEITHER OF US IS ALLOWED TO SIT DOWN!
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::ZONE_M: Raise the Bar
The bridge into the Gainlands is drawn up, and the very large man on the crank answers to the regime. Get across and find out who is running the Beefcakes now.
Out-muscle Brick Bronson at the gorge
The drawn-up gorge bridge, at the end of the meadow road
Cross the bridge into the Gainlands
The lowered bridge over the gorge
Spot the locals: finish a favour in the Gainlands
Foreman Gus, Old Man Mountain or Coach Brutus Benchley
Storm the House of Gains
The House of Gains, beyond the north rim
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::hud.obj: The Gainlands: the Swole Station is safe, mostly because the regime forgets it exists. HP doesn't come back after battles, so soak in the Cooldown Hot Tub or walk down to town. The House of Gains is on Leg Day Ridge.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::ui.mini: Three sets in a row. Your HP carries from one set to the next and nothing heals in between. Finish all three for a unique Beefcake card.
You already took the unique card from here. You can still lift for gold and XP. HP carries over; nothing heals in between.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::ui.exit: Leaving the Gainlands ends this visit. Town heals you fully; the regime's roaming brutes, golems and sprites will be back next time.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::fx.main: The House of Gains looms over you, all bare stone and floodlights. Above it the regime's flag snaps in the wind: a barbell with a red line through it.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::fx.heal: You sink into eucalyptus-scented water with an unmistakable base note of gym sock. HP restored; nose unconvinced.
You're already as rested as a Beefcake ever gets. The tub has done all it can for you.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::fx.hit:: ZAP! A regime sprite hits you right in the quads. (-2 HP)
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::fx.wake: You wake up in the Cooldown Hot Tub at the Swole Station. Old Man Mountain is holding a clipboard and a very small towel.
"You passed out mid-rep, lad. Happens to the best of us. Happened to me in the spring of... the spring of... well, it was a spring. Towel's on your tab.
Just don't tell the regime you had a lie-down. They fine people for resting, and I've only got the one towel."
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::fx.ches: Behind a rock you find a hidden stash, wrapped in an old gym towel so the regime wouldn't spot it.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::fx.land: You land. The ground takes most of the credit.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::fx.port: RRRRRIIIIIP! A portal, torn open by hand.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::fx.fall: You slip off the edge and come round at your last safe spot, bruised. Gravity has never spotted anyone in its life. (-1 HP)
Fell off %s - respawned at the last safe spot, 1 damage to zone HP.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::fx.lock: Not yet. Come back when you've done a few more reps.
Courtesy Chuck to %s: free, fast, no legroom required. Ready to be thrown?
Portal service: torn open by hand, no refunds. Step through to %s?
Pec Perch
Delt Deck
the far west meadow
the far east meadow
the Meadow Road
Calf Cove
the Ridge Road
Glute Garden
the east wheel yard
the west meadow
Brock cracks every knuckle he owns, then a few he borrowed. "Pec Perch? Great view.
Landing's a bit rough, mind. Tuck your elbows in and enjoy the view while you've got it."
Brock is always ready, and so is his throwing arm.
Rita flexes both hands like she's about to open a very stubborn jar. "Delt Deck? Easy. I rip the portal open, you walk through.
No tools and no spells, just bare hands and a lot of back."
Rita shakes her head. "Can't rip a thing with the grid this dry. Portals run on power, same as everything else up here.
Somebody has to run the big hamster wheel up the hill. Get it spinning, then come back and I'll have you through in no time."
Tobias hefts you like a sack of oats. "West meadow, cross-country. It's a long way, so I'm putting everything into this one.
You can tell me how it was once your thoughts catch up with you."
Tobias squints at you. "Cross-country chucks are for Gainers only. Show me a Gym Rat card and I'll send you clear across the Gainlands. Coach Brutus Benchley sells them."
Wanda is already warming up. "East meadow? Easy.
Say 'courtesy' for me. Louder. COURTESY!"
Wanda is always ready.
Bonnie waves a foam finger. "Heading down? Right.
Bend your knees on the way down. It'll look like you planned this."
Bonnie is always ready.
Shredna rolls her shoulders. "Calf Cove. Did the old yeti say hello? ...No, don't tell me, I don't care. Did he, though?
Old Man Mountain vouches for you, so Calf Cove's open. Mind the edges out there; the view drops off very suddenly."
Shredna crosses her arms. "Calf Cove stays shut till Old Man Mountain trusts you. Do his 'Spot Me!' favour, then come back and I'll rip it open."
Ripley is already shaking out her hands. "Back down to the Ridge? Sure.
I don't open doors. I take a very personal interest in a wall until it gives up."
Ripley is always ready.
Dmitri cracks his neck slowly, one way and then the other. "Glute Garden's a long throw. A very long throw.
I need you aerodynamic, so try not to think about it. Thinking adds drag."
Dmitri shakes his head slowly. "Long-haul throws are for Beefcakes who can handle the wilds. Beat two roaming enemies out there, then come see me."
Greta checks her watch. "Down to the east wheel yard? Say 'ready' on three.
One. Two. Actually, I'm already throwing."
Greta is always ready.
Raelynn tears a seam in the air with one grunt. "Heading home? Home's always open. Mind the gap on your way through; it bites."
Raelynn is always ready.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.hu: Hub of the Gainlands. Heal here. Brag here. Do NOT skip leg day here.
(Regime notice: all gatherings must be pre-approved cardio.)
Every light in the Gainlands runs on giant mills and colossal hamster wheels.
100% muscle. 0% coal. 110% quota, by order of the regime.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.ex: To {town}. Mind the gap; it has a very low opinion of shortcuts.
(Bridge lowered courtesy of Brick Bronson. He would like you to know he stretched first.)
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.he: Soak. Stretch. Do not drink the water. (Foreman Gus drank the water.)
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.pr: Results may vary. Please let the shake settle before you drink it, and your stomach settle after.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.fl: Check your form, your friend's form and the mirror's form. Someone here needs constructive reflection.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.ve: Protein, powder and cards, but mostly cards. The protein is optional; the yelling is not.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.mi: These giant mills grind everything: grain, tension, deadlines.
Pushed by hand, by Beefcakes, since forever. (The D.N.A. once asked for exact start times. We said "morning-ish".)
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.qu: Professor Pump asks 4 questions on Beefcake knowledge. Every answer is written on a sign somewhere in the Gainlands, so read as you go.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.st: Now taping: 'Pump It Up Past Midnight!'
Wear your legwarmers. Fashion may have moved on, but our calves have not.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.pu: Six hamster wheels, three machines. Each wheel feeds two machines (or naps).
Only five wheels may run at once. They get tired.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.wh: Run it to power the grid. There are no actual hamsters inside; the hamsters get breaks.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.gy: Equipment: boulders, logs and more boulders. A rock-solid selection.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.re: Every record set on this field, promptly crossed out by the next one. Personal bests are temporary; chalk is forever.
At the bottom, in chalk: DAY 1 OF NEVER SKIPPING. Day 1 has been crossed out forty times.
The Pump Shrine is spent. It flexes anyway, out of habit.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.sp: Gary is under there. Gary has been under there since lunch.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.th: Spotter mandatory. Landing not guaranteed. Dignity sold separately.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.ri: Bare hands only. No spells, no tools.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.th: East to west. A courtesy chuck, the long way. Gym Rat card required; Coach Benchley sells them.
West to east. A courtesy chuck, the long way. Free. Aim is a rumour.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.mi: Leg day. Every day. Bring chalk.
(Chalk sold at Benchley's, at a price he calls motivational.)
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.ma: The regime's stronghold. Authorized personnel only. Authorization takes exactly thirty seconds, and someone inside is timing you.
Leg Day is mandatory. It never ends.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.le: The House of Gains is closed to the public. Visitors will be given a pamphlet, a towel and a very long set of squats.
Weights are not available. Leg Day, however, is.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.en: Ask any Beefcake: they've got loads of it, and the regime takes most of it.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.be: Currently operating under new management. Nobody asked.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.pe: Population: one mirror. Please mind the edge; looking down on yourself is enough.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.de: Mind the edge. Delts are not wings.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.gl: Bend at the knees. Always bend at the knees.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.ed: There is no railing. There is no spotter. There is only gravity.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.ha: A hamster does not know it is the engine of a civilization.
The Beefcakes bring snacks. Civilization rests on the hamsters not finding out what a salary is.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::enemy.b: You see a regime enforcer flexing at nobody. He has held the pose since breakfast, because nobody has told him he can stop.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::enemy.g: A walking tub of confiscated protein powder rattles past, and it does not like the look of you.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::enemy.s: A sprite of pure mandatory pre-workout buzzes past, vibrating so hard it goes straight through a wall.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::npc.bre: Shh, keep it down - the regime has big ears up here. Welcome to the Gainlands. They call me Old Man Mountain. We Beefcakes keep the kingdom's lights on and its people moving... and if you're in a hurry, we throw you.

Ten years back, {villain}'s people put Chancellor Clench in charge - Grandmaster Flex's own star pupil, if you can believe it. They locked Flex under the House of Gains and took every weight. Every... every last plate.
We're tired, but we haven't crumbled. If you fall, I'll catch you: rule one, never lift alone. Rule two, never skip leg day. Rule three is... I've forgotten rule three. Two's plenty.
And that gate up on the overlook, past the ridge, won't budge for anybody. It opens when the kingdom is whole again, and not a day before. I asked it nicely. Twice.
Back again? Good. The only bad rep is the one nobody was there to spot.
You beat the regime and I'll buy the first round of shakes. Even the illegal flavour. Especially the illegal flavour... ah, I can nearly taste it.
The old king came up for the Lifting Festival every summer, and he brought his boy. The little fella tried my dumbbell once and sat down very hard on his royal behind.
He laughed about it, too, and his hands lit up four colours, plain as day. You've a look of him, you know... no, never mind me. Old man talk. Where was I?
That gate up on the overlook is still sealed. It opens when the kingdom is whole again, and not a day before. I check on it most mornings, just in case.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::npc.gus: Foreman Gus. I keep the wheels turning, the grid humming and the hamsters - sorry, the volunteers - fed. They put pre-workout in the water. So far I'm mostly feeling the water.
The regime wants a hundred and ten percent. The wheels only go to a hundred. The extra ten comes out of the crew, and nobody writes down where it went.
The crews on the city wheels up in the Capital have it worse. They're told it's cardio, for their own good. It's neither.
Grid's still humming. If it ever goes quiet, it means somebody sat down, and the regime takes that very personally.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::npc.ton: LET'S GO! A NEW RECRUIT! Coach Brutus Benchley - retired champion, current motivator, part-time merchant! Protein, powder and pasteboard! SUPPLEMENTS FOR YOUR DECK!
REGIME-APPROVED MERCHANDISE! Not actually approved, but these old cards have a GREAT ATTITUDE!
*whispering* Mind the loose floorboard behind the counter. There's nothing under it. Just some iron, which officially doesn't exist.
LET'S GO, RETURNING CUSTOMER! The cards are pumped and my whistle's been SAVING ITS BREATH for you!
*whispering* Nobody's mentioned the floorboard. I'd like to keep our relationship on that footing.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::npc.qui: Aha, a student! I'm Professor Pump, Beefcake scholar, and I lecture from this very log. I've written seventeen books, you know.
Fifteen of them concern the biceps. The other two were a history of the Lifting Festival, and when the regime burned those, I rewrote them from memory. You can't confiscate a well-trained brain-cep.
Four questions on the Beefcakes, their energy and their transport. Every answer is on a sign, a poster or a Beefcake's lips somewhere in the Gainlands.
Answer well for gold and glory. Answer poorly and receive a mild, scholarly sigh. I have practised the sigh. It is devastating.
Back for another set of questions? Splendid! Knowledge gains stay with you, even on your rest days.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::quiz.re: Zero, I'm afraid, and no reward this time. Still, it's a clean baseline, and all research has to begin somewhere.
Do read the signs before your next attempt. Let your eyes do the heavy lifting for once.
One. A twitch of knowledge, at least. Take this small pat on the back.
Two. Half-credit, graded on a bicep curve. In the Gainlands half a rep still counts, just not for very much.
Three! One shy of a clean sweep. Take your reward and flex responsibly.
FOUR! A perfect set! You may now call yourself a Certified Gainer, Class A. The reward is real; the certificate, sadly, is imaginary.
Another lap! The Gainlands pay a little less for repeat attendance. The regime calls it a 'processing fee', which sounds suspiciously like the D.N.A. to me.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::quiz.no: Not a pass yet, I'm afraid. Read the signs around the Gainlands and come back. We're training recall here, not regret.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::npc.min: *cue synthesizer* Welcome, welcome, WELCOME to PUMP IT UP PAST MIDNIGHT! I'm your host, Chet Thunderabs, and it is 3 A.M. somewhere, which is where I live!
You've seen the late-night tapes! 'Feel the burn!' But WAIT, there's MORE! My assistant is a legwarmer. My producer is ALSO a legwarmer.
The regime banned my show for 'unauthorized fun'! But these cameras are STILL ROLLING, because you can't confiscate a man's ENTHUSIASM! They tried! It came back!
Today's show: REP COUNTER! Eight reps, one beat. Hit the beat and I give you a shiny medallion of pure encouragement!
Rewards for performance, plus a one-time bonus on your very first set! Three easy payments of gold? NO! FREE! Operators are standing by! And one, and two...
Back again! My fans! Both of you! Hear that? That's the sound of Spandex, applauding.
Remember: the beat is your friend. The beat does not judge. The beat is judging, but quietly.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::reps.in: Eight reps. Watch the ring: press SPACE (or click) the moment it closes on the bar. Perfect, Good, OK or Miss.
The beat speeds up. Fewer misses, more stars.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::reps.wi: THAT'S THE WAY - THE CAMERA LOVES YOU! And the legwarmers, but they've been trying to get a solo shot ALL NIGHT!
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::reps.fi: Your first set on the show! Here's your Pump Medallion: a bonus, free, no obligation. Operators are still standing by.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::reps.lo: Not quite a set, champ! But WAIT - that wasn't a failure! That was a FREE TRIAL!
REHYDRATE AND TRY AGAIN! The beat is standing by! The legwarmers are standing by! I am STANDING BY, and my calves are SO ready!
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::npc.gar: Mmmph! Oh, thank goodness, a spotter! Hi, I'm Gary. Lovely to meet you. Sorry I can't shake hands.
I've been under this barbell since lunch. Possibly since the regime took over - it's hard to tell from down here. No rush. Bit of a rush.
It's the last barbell they didn't confiscate, so I got excited and loaded one more plate than my confidence.
It's fine. It's FINE. Could you give it a little push? Whenever you're ready. Now would be good.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::ambient: Gym's open! The weights aren't. The scales stayed, though - standard measures, sent up from the Capital. Say what you like about the Minister, those scales never lie.
Towels are ten gold now, because Clench taxes sweat.
House rule one: re-rack your weights. House rule two: we have no weights.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::npc.gar: Spotter, you're a hero! One day this barbell and I will rise to the occasion... with you watching, please.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::fx.spot: You grab the bar and heave. Gary slides out, gasping.
"You're a hero! Take this, I borrowed it from the gym.
It's not mine, so now it's yours. I think that's how borrowing works."
You find Gary under a different, lighter barbell. He has lowered the bar in every sense except the useful one.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::fx.whee: You jump into the Colossal Hamster Wheel and run until your legs burn. The grid hums, lights brighten across the Gainlands, and somewhere a portal ripper rolls up her sleeves.
The wheel's still spinning happily on its own. Let it coast; you've earned a snack.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::fx.shak: A banana-berry shake. Smooth, sweet, suspiciously good for you. +HP.
A legendary chocolate-peanut-butter shake. Even your muscles want the recipe. Big recovery!
Chalky, lumpy... you appear to be drinking an unfinished wall.
The cup has a coin at the bottom. The shake was just a front. +gold.
You receive an empty cup. Flavour: surprise.
The stand wants 10 gold. You have enthusiasm, which it does not accept.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::fx.flex: You flex. The mirror flexes back. You both nod. +1 HP.
You hit a double biceps, and you and the mirror gasp at the same moment. +1 HP.
You hit the most-muscular pose. The mirror applauds. +1 HP.
Your pump has peaked for this visit; come back next time. Even your reflection needs a cooldown.
You flex, the mirror flexes back, and there's nothing left to heal. You look great regardless.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: The Colossal Hamster Wheel, up the hill
The protein shake stand in the Swole Station
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Juice the Station
The Swole Station's lights are flickering. Foreman Gus needs somebody to run the Colossal Hamster Wheel and, frankly, drink something.
Run the Colossal Hamster Wheel up the hill
Buy a protein shake at the Station's stand
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::quest.g: The lights keep flickering because the regime pipes every watt up to the House of Gains. Run the Colossal Hamster Wheel up the hill and we'll keep a little for ourselves. Call it quiet resistance.
Then buy a shake at the protein stand in the Swole Station. It's for crew morale. Mostly mine.
Run the Colossal Hamster Wheel up the hill, then buy a shake at the protein stand in the Swole Station. Come and find me when you're done.
The Swole Station's lights are back on and the grid's humming. I'd make a speech, but all my energy went into the lights. Here, take your reward.
Don't let the hamsters hear you call them 'volunteers'. They're sensitive.
The grid's running smooth, and some of the power's even staying here for once. I'd hug you, but I'm a foreman, so I'll nod. ...That was a big nod, for me.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Gary, under a barbell again. Follow the groaning.
A Flex Mirror, at the Station or up on Pec Perch
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Spot Me!
Old Man Mountain's rule: nobody lifts alone. Start by spotting Gary. He is under a barbell again.
Spot Gary under his barbell
Flex at a Flex Mirror
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::quest.g: Which brings me back to rule one. Gary's stuck under a barbell again - follow the groaning and give him a spot. Then check your form at a Flex Mirror. The regime tried confiscating reflections once. It didn't take.
Do both and I'll have Shredna rip you a portal out to Calf Cove. Nobody's been out there in months, and the calves... well, you'll see.
Spot Gary at his barbell, then flex at a Flex Mirror: the one at the Station or the one up on Pec Perch. Spot first, flex second, brag third.
You spotted Gary and checked your form? Beautiful. Here, have a Pre-Workout Jitters, on the house.
Calf Cove's open to you now. Tell Shredna I said hello. She'll pretend she didn't miss me.
Calf Cove's yours now. Mind the edge out there - always mind the edge. I didn't, once, back in the spring of... never mind.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Brutes, golems and sprites roam the open ground
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Clear the Lanes
Benchley's protein deliveries keep getting 'inspected' by roaming brutes, golems and sprites. Beat three of them. Deliver the gains.
Beat roaming enemies in the Gainlands
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::quest.g: Regime brutes, golems and sprites keep EATING my deliveries! Beat any three roaming enemies in the Gainlands in card duels! THOSE SHAKES HAD MY NAME ON THEM! I WRITE IT ON EVERY LID!
I'll pay you in cards! STRONG cards! *whispering* Heavy ones. The kind the regime hasn't found yet.
Three roaming enemies out in the Gainlands, champ! The brutes flex! The golems rattle!
The sprites buzz! Pick your poison and GET OUT THERE!
THREE DOWN! Deliveries are BACK ON SCHEDULE! Here, take a Leg Day for your trouble, and do NOT skip it, champ! I mean that as a coach AND as a card dealer!
The lanes are clear! For about an hour! Then the regime fills them up again! BUT WHAT AN HOUR!
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::wheel.i: A control panel hums beside the wheels: six hamster wheels, three machines (the Lift, the Gate and the Mill), a switch for every wheel.
Each wheel is piped to TWO of the machines; its switch sends the power to one of them, or leaves it napping. Every machine needs its exact wattage. Only five wheels may run at once.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::wheel.s: Every machine settles at exactly the right wattage, and the Lift, the Gate and the Mill all hum together.
Somewhere a hamster sighs with relief, and a small, heavy parcel drops into the tray.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::wheel.a: The grid purrs. Nothing left to route.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::wheel.h: Start from the machine with the fewest options. The Mill needs 9, and only the wheels piped to it can supply it. Work out which wheel MUST feed the Gate.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.re: 1. Weights are confiscated for your safety.
2. Protein is a privilege, not a right.
3. Mandatory Cardio Compliance, 5 AM sharp. Lateness is punished with more cardio.
CHANCELLOR CLENCH SAYS: "A BEEFCAKE WITHOUT IRON IS JUST A CAKE."
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.mi: Grandmaster Flex. Ten years gone, dragged off to the House of Gains.
If found, do not lift him. He is probably tired.
The whole zone is on a permanent pump. Beefcakes feel it in their quads.
Everyone up here runs everywhere. A Necrocrat who tries to keep pace arrives winded and needs a minute to find the right form.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::ui.main: The regime's stronghold. Far below it, in the Iron-less Prison, the true leader has been held for ten years. HP carries in from the zone; only the shrines heal. Beat Chancellor Clench to free the Gainlands.
The House of Gains is quiet, and the doors are open. You can still run the halls for gold and XP. HP carries in from the zone; nothing heals except at the shrines.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: An old gravedigger is pacing out a hole beside the weight racks, counting under his breath.
Just measuring, don't mind me. Lovely broad shoulders up here - very roomy work, when it comes. Not that it's come lately. Heh.
What are you writing?
Appointments. Let's see, you're... hm. Not for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-BENCHLEY.barks::0: LET'S GO! Cards are protein for your deck! Regime-approved! (They are not.)
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-BENCHLEY.barks::1: Floorboard? WHAT floorboard? Do NOT stand on the floorboard! LET'S GO!
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-HURL.barks::0: Three... two... oh, I already threw someone. Sorry. Enthusiasm.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-HURL.barks::1: Never once missed. The landing is your part. I believe in your part.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-RIP.barks::0: HNNNGH. Thank you for ripping with the Express. Please don't look at the seam.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-RIP.barks::1: HNNNGH. Two hundred and twelfth shirt this year. Did you notice my form, buddy?
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-PUMP.barks::0: Pop quiz! Kidding. Unless... no. Even brain-ceps need a rest day.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-PUMP.barks::1: Read the signs, student. Every answer is there. Consider it a slow circuit of the gym.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-THUNDERABS.bark: But WAIT, there's MORE! Act now for a SECOND set of reps! Reps not included!
Operators are standing by! It's me! I tried sitting! LOST THE ENERGY!
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-MOUNTAIN.barks:: Rule one: never lift alone. Rule two... rule two is... where was I.
There was a boy at the Lifting Festival once. Four colours in his hands... hm.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-FLEX.barks::0: Breathe in. Hold. ...Now lift. The breath was the hard part.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-FLEX.barks::1: They took the iron, son. The iron was only ever a guest.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: The protein shake stand in the Swole Station
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::s: With Primm gone, Old Man Mountain will open the gate to Mount Swolympus. Only for the worthy. The worthy bring him a protein shake from the Station's stand.
Buy a protein shake at the Station's stand
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::quest.s: You beat {villain}, and the kingdom's whole again. Which means that gate on the overlook can finally open... Mount Swolympus. I never thought I'd live to see it.
Only the worthy reach the top, mind. In my experience the worthy bring water, or a protein shake. Fetch me one from the stand and the gate's yours.
A shake from the stand in the Station, any flavour. Not the illegal one. ...Oh, go on, then. The illegal one.
Ahh. Worthy. Very worthy. A bit lumpy, but worthy.
The gate's open and the ridge path is mended, mostly. Climb to the top and say hello to the Ancient Spotter - he's held that bar for a thousand years. Ask him about his back.
The Spotter's waiting at the summit. Don't keep him waiting another thousand years, lad.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: On a throne that is really a leg press, a Beefcake with thighs like mill wheels pushes a sled of plates up and down, up and down. He has not stood up in years.
'Nobody. Skips. Leg day.' He presses another rep. 'Not in my cave. Prove it. I won't get up.'
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Baron: Nobody. Skips. Leg day. (rep) In my cave.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Final Set
At half health the Baron starts his final set: his units get +1/+0 for the rest of the fight.
Nobody. Skips. Leg day. (rep) Final set. (rep) In my cave.
The Baron's units get +1/+0.
He Stands Up
Near the end the Baron stands for the first time in years: he heals 2, and wobbles (his units get -1/-0).
Standing. Huh. Wobbly. Like a first rep.
The Baron heals 2, but his units get -1/-0.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Baron Quadzilla racks the plates, stands, and wobbles. 'Huh,' he says, looking down. 'So those are my feet. Hello, feet.'
He hands you a sweaty ribbon. 'Leg day survivor. Wear it. Stretch. That order.'
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::dungeon: The gates swing open on a hall papered with posters of Chancellor Clench, and there isn't a single weight anywhere in it, not even a dumbbell.
Every rack along the walls stands empty, right down to the little pegs where the decorative plates used to hang.
Somewhere far beneath your feet, something is breathing, slow and even, as if it has been counting every breath for a very long time.
The Gates of Gains
Bare steel and floodlights under a banner reading MANDATORY CARDIO. Iron is banned here, and nobody has ever left through these gates.
The Regime Checkpoint
An enforcer searches your bag for weights while a clerk times him with a stopwatch. Minister Quota wants every search done in thirty seconds, and he's already at forty.
The Descent
A long stone stairway leads down into the Iron-less Prison.
The Cell Block
The prisoners keep very quiet and the guards are very loud, and it doesn't take long to work out which of them is afraid.
The Calisthenics Check
The prison has no iron, so it tests bodies. A guard demands to see your form.
The Iron-less Warden
The warden has never lifted a weight in his life, has never needed to, and is furious with everyone who has. (Elite)
The Last Cell
At the very bottom of the prison there is a single cell, and from inside it comes one long, slow breath.
The warden's keyring clatters to the floor. At the end of the corridor, behind a door with no handle, someone is doing a push-up so slow and controlled it seems to take a full minute.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Locker Room of Legends

Rows of lockers hold the old champions' gear, every strap labelled by weight class. A laminated sign reads LOCKER 13 IS A STATE OF MIND. One door hangs ajar, and something inside is humming a marching tune to itself.
Borrow the lucky towel
The towel is still warm and smells of eucalyptus and somebody else's victory. You feel sturdier with it round your neck, and very slightly watched.
Raid the gym bag
Inside are protein bars, a roll of gold and a note that says 'Spotter knows.' Somewhere down the hall a whistle blows, and you leave with the gold and a guilty conscience.
Do a set with the ghost of a champion
The ghost miscounts your reps on purpose, always upward, to be encouraging. You walk away standing taller, if not stronger, and he presses a Gym Bro's number into your hand.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/quo: Someone has built a barricade out of weight plates painted regulation red. Behind it, a ferret in a pinstriped suit is timing a guard's push-ups with a silver stopwatch.
Forty-one, forty-two, and stop. Eleven percent slower than yesterday, which we will discuss at your review.
And you walked in at a pace of seven out of ten. Disappointing, but at least it's measurable.
Who are you?
Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency. I designed the wheels, the schedules and the prison downstairs. The Chancellor does the shouting. I do the arithmetic.
Hold still while I measure you. Grip, low. Stride, uneven. Resolve... unusually high, and that is an inefficiency I intend to remove.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Vivien: You arrived four seconds late. I have already deducted it from you.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Efficiency Review
At half health Quota reviews her numbers: she draws a card.
Your performance: forty-one percent of acceptable. Mine is about to improve.
Quota draws a card.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/quo: Ninety-four seconds. You beat me in ninety-four seconds.
I'll note it, the way I note everything. The Chancellor is not going to enjoy this figure.
