She clicks the stopwatch, steps through a side door marked for staff only, and is gone before the guard finishes his push-up.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::dungeon: The Cell Stretch
Grandmaster Flex leads a quiet round of stretching and breathing. Restore HP.
The Barracks Gauntlet
You hear the recruits drilling before you see them. They make up in volume what they lack in coordination.
The Confiscated Gear Locker
Every weight the regime ever took, stacked behind one locker door. Each plate still has its owner's name chalked on the back.
The Honor Guard
You face Chancellor Clench's personal guard, whose uniforms are pressed to perfection and whose technique is mostly shouting. (Elite)
The Trophy Hall
The regime keeps a trophy for every leader it ever overthrew, and one pedestal stands empty, waiting for Grandmaster Flex.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::cutscen: Quietly, son. The guards time their rounds by counting their squats, and they lose count.
So the rounds come whenever they come. Listen for knees cracking on the stairs, and you'll hear them in good time.
You're Grandmaster Flex? Everyone up there talks about you as if you were twice this size.
Ten years in the dark will do that. They took my plates, my protein, every bar I ever lifted, and left me with nothing at all.
And nothing, it turns out, is a fine place to start. I still had my breath, my body and my mind, so I trained them every day.
Come, son, we'll climb out together. I'd like a word with Clench on the way. He was the best student I ever had. He still is.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::dungeon: "Breathe in slowly and hold it. Now let it all go," says Grandmaster Flex, breathing along with you.
"You carry the whole kingdom in your lungs, son. Try not to drop it."
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Empty Trophy
At half health a reserve guard steps off a pedestal: a 1/1 Reserve Guard joins.
Reserves, off your pedestal! This trophy belongs to the Chancellor, not to some stranger off the wheels!
A 1/1 Reserve Guard steps off a pedestal.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Sauna of Truth
The steam asks one honest question: how hard do you lead?
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::dungeon: Chancellor Clench stands in front of an enormous bench press, the only weight left in the whole House of Gains, and he guards it like a throne.
"Master." The word sticks in his throat. "I was your best, you know - your star pupil."
"You told me I'd go further than you ever did. Then you started on about strength living in the heart and the head, and I knew better."
"I took your iron, your protein and your followers, and you've climbed back up here with nothing, Master."
"Look how far I went, Master. What exactly do you think you can do about it now?"
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Chance: You. Off the wheel. Nobody leaves the Gainlands without a permit and a rep count.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Brownout
On his 5th turn Clench cuts the wheel power: your two strongest ready units are exhausted and cannot block that turn.
Next turn: Clench cuts the power (your two strongest units cannot block).
CUT THE POWER. Everyone off the wheels. Nobody moves unless I say REP.
The lights go out: your two strongest ready units are exhausted.
DROP AND GIVE ME FORMS
At half health Clench pulls the emergency reserve: he gains 2 Iron.
Control is strength, paperwork is control, and do you know how HEAVY paperwork gets? Two more plates!
Clench gains 2 Iron.
Master...?
Near the end Clench falters: his units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
You said I would go further than you. Look how far I went. ...Master?
Clench falters: his units get -1/-0.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::dungeon: Chancellor Clench's Gym
The regime's throne room is a gym with one throne-shaped bench press in it, the only barbell left in the House.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::challen: No iron in the prison, so the guards test what you can do with your own body. Your first unit must be strong enough to count.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::event.h: The Descent
The stairway to the Iron-less Prison is steep, dark and damp. On the third landing a guard fills the whole stair, arms folded, muscles folded on top of the arms.
"Nobody goes down," he says. Then, after a long and meaningful pause: "Unless..."
Bribe the guard
Overpower the guard
Distract the guard
He counts the coins twice, bites one, and steps aside. "I saw nothing. I also bought nothing. Go."
You win the wrestle, though he wins the first three rounds of it. The way down is open, and so is your lip.
You fling {card} down the far stairwell. The guard bounds after it like a puppy after a ball.
He'll guard it with his life until you leave the House, and then it's yours again.
The Rescue
In the last cell, a gaunt old man sits cross-legged in the dark, perfectly still. Ten years of breath and calisthenics have worn him down to wire and will.
He opens one eye and looks at you. "You are not a guard."
There's no bar or bench in the cell, only stone worn smooth by ten years of training. Something about the bare walls tightens your chest, and you couldn't say why.
Pick the lock and free him
The lock gives. Grandmaster Flex rises slowly, a little unsteady on his feet, and bows to you. He is so thin you could count his ribs.
He moves with a stillness that is somehow the opposite of weakness. "When you face Clench," he says, "I will be beside you."
The Trophy Hall
Trophies of every defeated Beefcake line the walls: belts, medals, the left shoe of a champion.
The plate on the empty pedestal reads GRANDMASTER FLEX (PENDING), and someone has dusted it very recently.
Take the medals (they are very shiny)
Polish the empty pedestal
Leave everything as it is
The medals jingle as you scoop them up, and Grandmaster Flex winces. "They are not ours to take, son."
"Still, the regime owes this house a great deal, and gold settles debts." You feel a little guilty, and a little richer.
You polish it until it gleams. Grandmaster Flex watches, and something old and heavy lifts off him. You feel stronger.
You leave the hall exactly as you found it, and Grandmaster Flex gives you one slow nod of approval.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::cutscen: You brought that... that stick of a man into MY house? Look at you, Master. Ten years on bread and water, and you still won't stay down.
A Beefcake without iron is just a CAKE!
Stand back a little, son. It has been a long time, and I would like some room.
They took my weights, Clench. They forgot to take me.
You only ever wanted the weight, my boy. I was teaching you the heart, and you stopped listening before I ever got to the mind.
...How? Ten years in a hole with nothing - where were you HIDING all of that?
Strength was never about how heavy a thing is, Clench. It lives in the heart and the mind, and nobody can lock those in a cell.
The heavy things were only ever practice, my boy. Now, shall we?
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::dungeon: Chancellor Clench stands in front of an enormous bench press, the only weight left in the whole House of Gains, and he guards it like a throne.
"A stranger in my house, and no old man at your side. They say Flex is still down in the dark, doing push-ups for nobody."
"They say he trained a hundred pupils and I was the best of them. Look where that got me. Look where it got him."
"Come, then. Let me show you what iron is for."
Chancellor Clench falls, bench and all. The regime's banners come down one by one, and in the great hall the Beefcakes begin to cheer, quietly, then very loudly.
You hear slow, controlled footsteps on the stairs. Grandmaster Flex emerges from the Iron-less Prison alone, in thin grey robes.
"I was going to leave eventually," he says. "Lovely day for it." Then he looks at his fallen pupil, and his face softens.
"Get up, my boy. We start from zero. Everyone does."
He glances at you. "Whatever they took from you, son, it was not the part that matters."
Chancellor Clench falls, bench and all. The regime's banners come down one by one, and in the great hall the Beefcakes begin to cheer, quietly, then very loudly.
Flex doesn't gloat. He kneels beside his fallen pupil and offers him a hand. "You hated yourself for needing the iron, my boy.
I never hated you for it. Come back to the gym. We start from zero. Everyone does."
Clench has lost his title, his medals and the thing he thought strength was. He stares at the hand a long time. He does not take it yet, but he does not pull away.
Then Flex turns to you, and his voice is gentle. "Whatever they took from you, son, it was not the part that matters."
data/story/intro_story.tres::still.flex:: Grandmaster Flex walks into the throne room in his prison rags, and the whole hall falls silent.
He breathes in, slow and even. Ten years without iron have worn him thin as wire, but he stands perfectly straight.
Across the room, the ruler of the House of Gains takes one step back.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::ambient: The weights are back! I cried, then I did a set, and then I cried all over again.
Free towels! Flex says a gym is for people, not quotas.
Re-rack your weights! We HAVE weights! Re-rack them!
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::hud.obj: The Gainlands, free at last: the Swole Station is open to everyone. HP does not come back after battles - soak in the Cooldown Hot Tub, or walk back down to town.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::ui.exit: Leaving the Gainlands ends this visit. Town heals you fully. The brutes, golems and sprites are off-duty now, but they still enjoy a scrap.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.hu: Hub of the Gainlands. Heal here. Brag here. Do NOT skip leg day here.
(Gatherings are now welcome. Mandatory cardio has been abolished. Gary is thrilled.)
Every light in the Gainlands runs on giant mills and colossal hamster wheels.
100% muscle. 0% coal. Quotas abolished: run at whatever pace feels good.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.en: Ask any Beefcake. They have loads of it, and now they get to keep some.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.be: Back under the old management. The old management can still bench a hay cart.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.re: 2. Protein is a right. Also, a shake.
3. Cardio is optional. Leg day is not.
GRANDMASTER FLEX SAYS: "STRENGTH IS IN THE HEART AND THE MIND."
(He would also like you to drink some water.)
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.mi: Grandmaster Flex is back, and he is doing yoga on the roof of the House of Gains.
Wave, and he will wave back. After the pose. The pose may take a while.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.ex: (To town. The cardio checkpoint is a snack bar now. Snacks are mandatory.)
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.ma: Formerly the regime's stronghold. Open to all Beefcakes.
Leg Day is still mandatory. Some things are sacred.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::sign.le: The doors are open. Come in, stretch, breathe.
Leg Day is still Leg Day.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::npc.bre: You did it! Flex is out, Clench is down, and I got to watch the whole thing. Best day since... oh, since the last best day, whenever that was. I'm spotting you from now on, like it or not.
Weights back in the gym, and there's Gary, lifting with a proper spotter. Beautiful. Before you go... that boy I told you about, the old king's son, at the Festival...
When you heaved that last regime brute off his feet, you made the same face he made on my dumbbell. The very same face. Funny, the things you remember.
Free, strong and properly spotted, all of us. Thank you, friend. I climbed Swolympus once, you know, and these ten years were steeper.
That gate up on the overlook is still sealed. It opens when the kingdom is whole again, and not a day before. I asked it nicely. Twice.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::npc.gus: Foreman Gus, still on the wheels. But listen to them now - not a single whistle.
The grid's at a hundred percent, and nobody wants ten more. Turns out a hundred was all of it.
I might even take a day off. No idea how it's done, but I hear you start by sitting down.
The wheels turn when they feel like it, and somehow we've never had more power. I'd tell the regime, but there isn't one.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::npc.ton: LET'S GO! The iron came out from under the floorboard and went STRAIGHT onto a rack! Benchley's is open to EVERYONE!
REGIME MERCHANDISE IN THE CLEARANCE BIN! Nobody wants it - my proudest day of not making a sale!
CARDS ON SHELVES, IRON ON RACKS! And I don't have to whisper about the floorboard any more, which is good, because I WAS NEVER ANY GOOD AT IT!
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::freed_n: Welcome, friend. Grandmaster Flex, at your service. After ten years in the dark, the first thing I wanted was a window, and the second was a good long stretch.
They took my plates, my protein, everything I had ever lifted. So I breathed: in, hold, and out again. That is what I did for ten years, and it was enough.
I counted my own heartbeats until they turned into songs. They thought they were breaking me down there, son, but they were teaching me.
Clench is learning to lift from zero, and the strongest always take the longest. Yesterday he spotted Gary without being asked. The gym is open to everyone now, so come whenever you like.
Lift what you can. Carry what you must. Put down what was never yours.
And you, son: whatever they took from you, it was not the part that matters.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::ruler.s: "A Beefcake without iron is just a cake."
(Toppled by public demand. Please do not stand on it. Gary did, once.)
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/quo: On the arm of the Throne of Gains someone has left a schedule, timed to the second, and a silver stopwatch, still running.
Quota's gone, off to the Capital before the dust had even settled. She always did like to leave early.
We'll keep her schedule, since it will make good kindling. And breathe, son - nobody here is on the clock any more.
data/story/intro_story.tres::gate.gourma: She's back - the real Grand Chef. She tasted my soup, frowned and said 'more salt', and I have never been so happy in my life.
The pantry door stays wide open now, and people wander in for biscuits all day long. I keep a tin by the hinge for them.
Fancy a friendly duel, for old times' sake? Loser washes the ladle, and I should warn you, it's a very big ladle.
An enormous pantry door blocks the lane, locked tight, with a keyhole the size of a dinner plate.
Chef Fennel Gravois hands over a key the size of a ladle, and it turns in the lock with a satisfying clunk.
The great pantry door swings open on a smell of roasting meat and fresh bread, and underneath it, faintly, the smell of hot iron.
data/story/intro_story.tres::gourmand_np: TASTE IT! The Special Sauce is in everything now - my soup, my tea, my very SOUL - and isn't it WONDERFUL?
The pantry is closed by order of the Grand Chef, and the key stays on my apron. It's all for the war effort!
You want the key? You'll have to beat me for it! Yes, Chef! No - YOU, Chef!
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Chef F: TASTE IT. TASTE IT! It's for the war effort!
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: TASTE IT!
At half health Fennel force-feeds you a biscuit (you heal 2) and a 1/1 Snack joins his side.
TASTE IT! Even the BISCUIT is for the war effort!
You heal 2. A 1/1 Snack joins Fennel.
data/story/intro_story.tres::gourmand_np: The sauce has let go of me. Is that plain bread, with no sauce on it at all? I could weep. In fact, I am weeping.
The Grand Chef stopped tasting her own sauces years ago, and the Chef I trained under ALWAYS tasted. Same face, same apron... so who has been wearing it?
Whatever's wrong here starts in the Test Kitchen, at the far end of the Buffet, and it was never making casserole. Take a biscuit for the road. Take two.
The pantry door stays shut until you've learned to cook. Come back when you're properly seasoned!

The great pantry door is locked, and Chef Fennel Gravois won't give up the key. Win it, and find out what's really cooking in the Grand Chef's kitchens.

Step through the pantry door into the Endless Buffet

data/story/gourmand_story.tres::hud.obje: The Endless Buffet: the Grand Pantry is safe. HP does not come back after battles - sit down for a hearty meal, or walk back down to town. Everything here looks wonderful.
Something under the Test Kitchen smells wrong.
Three courses in a row. Your HP carries from one course to the next and nothing heals in between. Finish all three for a unique Gourmand card.
You already took the unique card from this freezer. You can still eat your way through the courses for gold and XP. HP carries over; nothing heals in between.
Leaving the Endless Buffet ends this visit. Town heals you fully; the roaming golems, sentinels and meatballs (prototype batch, unfortunately) will be back next time. The buffet, as the name suggests, is endless.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.main_: The Test Kitchen sits at the far end of the table: a gleaming glass-and-steel laboratory with a very large, very unfinished cannon sticking out of the roof. A banner reads INNOVATION SEASON.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.heal_: You sit down to a hearty meal: roast something, a bowl of soup the size of a bathtub, and a roll that hugs you back. HP restored.
Your HP is already full, but a chef refills your plate anyway. Around here, being full is treated as a misunderstanding.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.hit::: BONK! A runaway prototype meatball hits you right in the shins. (-2 HP)
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.wake:: You wake up face-down in a bowl of mashed potatoes at the Grand Pantry. Basil is holding a ladle and a very long receipt.
"You fainted into the gravy, so we fished you out. There's a, um, fishing fee... sorry. Sorry! I don't set the prices, I just hold the ladle.
Don't tell the taste testers you fainted. If anyone asks you anything, just say 'Yes, Chef.' It works for everything."
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.chest: A hidden stash! Unsampled, unsauced and all yours.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.lande: You stick the landing. Peeling yourself off it takes longer.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.soup_: You fall in the gravy. A passing chef fishes you out with a ladle and checks you for seasoning. (-1 HP)
Fell into the soup at %s - fished out at the last safe spot, 1 damage to zone HP.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.gate_: The golem steps aside with the slow dignity of a roast being carved. The way is open.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.picku: You already took the one lying here. Come back on your next visit; the pantry restocks overnight.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.oven_: Ding! A Hearty Pot Pie, golden and steaming, drops into your bag. The oven looks very proud of itself.
The Grand Oven rumbles. "A pie needs honey, basil and a ghost pepper. I am an oven, not a miracle."
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.taste: Smooth, balanced, a touch of citrus. You nod like a professional. +HP.
You take a sip and blink through a tear. Five stars would feel stingy - big recovery!
Your palate sharpens. You can taste what the cheese had for breakfast. A little extra HP for the visit.
The judges are impressed and tip you for the privilege of watching. +gold.
You find the ghost pepper in spoon three. Your ears ring in protest. -1 HP.
You taste boiled water with a hint of ambition. The judges study their shoes; nothing else happens.
You need 8 gold for the taste test. The station declines to sample your good intentions.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.fount: You ladle some soup. Tomato with a hint of basil. Warm all the way down. +HP.
You take a second ladle of cream of mushroom. The fungus has a rich inner life. +HP.
Third ladle: minestrone, mostly noodles. You feel taller. +HP.
You ladle some soup, look at it, and pour it back. You are full. The fountain takes it well.
The fountain's tank is dry for now. Soup takes time, and it will be full again on your next visit.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.cooki: The dispenser wants 5 gold. Fortune favours the people who bring change.
You crack the cookie open. A tiny paper slip falls out. It reads:
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.mend_: Old Meatloaf is mended! He gets up, stretches, and sizzles a little.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::gate.ing: Brisket nods slowly. "Go on in. Mind the cheese.
The cheese takes trespassing personally. You're walking on its rind."
Brisket sniffs the air, and his eyes close in bliss. "Saffron. Real saffron.
Do you know how long it has been?" He takes the threads with great tenderness and steps aside.
"Go on through. Tell the Cheddar Cliffs they are overdue for a good grating. Yes, Chef."
Brisket does not look at you. He looks over your head, at the horizon. "This gate opens for one pinch of saffron.
Real saffron, mind you, which grows in the Candy Field. Ask a sous-chef if you lose your way."
He sighs at you. "Bring saffron from the Candy Field; this gate has a very particular taste in visitors."
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::gate.que: Sir Loin raises his fork in salute. "You mended Old Meatloaf, so you are a friend of the Pantry. The town is yours."
Sir Loin inspects you. "Old Meatloaf walks again. Basil sends thanks, and orders, which are: let you in. Yes, Chef!"
He lowers his fork-lance. The gate swings open.
Sir Loin clanks to attention. "HALT! Nobody enters Layer-Cake Town until Old Meatloaf has been mended.
It is Basil's request, so speak to Basil in the Grand Pantry. Yes, Chef!"
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::gate.bat: Colonel Casserole tips his lid. "A fair fight, well fought. The Pancake Plateau is open to you. Mind the syrup; it pools."
Colonel Casserole bubbles ominously. "Halt! This gate is guarded by a Colonel.
No passes, no bribes - challenge me to single combat with cards. I shall defend this gate to the last course."
"If you win, you pass. If you lose, you do the washing up. Both are honourable."
Defeat Colonel Casserole in a card battle to open the way to the Pancake Plateau. Your HP carries over as usual.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.hub: Hub of the Endless Buffet. The Gourmands feed the kingdom and protect it.
Nobody leaves hungry. (Innovation Season is now in effect. Sample participation is mandatory.)
- Guard the kingdom (with golems. Defensive golems. Please stop saying the other word.)
- Innovation: please do not ask about the Special Sauce
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.exi: To {town}, through the great pantry door. Wipe your feet and surrender your sample; we just mopped.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.hea: Sit. Eat. Do not ask what the gravy is made of.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.ven: Cards and cakes, mostly cards. Reservations recommended; table manners apply even to your deck.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.ove: Honey, basil and one ghost pepper make one Hearty Pot Pie.
Do not open the oven to check on the pie. It is already working under considerable heat.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.fou: Three ladles per customer. The soup of the day is soup.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.gol: We are the Gourmands: chefs of the kingdom.
We feed the kingdom. We protect the kingdom.
We cook food golems to guard it. They answer every order with "Yes, Chef!"
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.coo: Each one holds a hint about a secret. Handle with care. The secrets are crumbly.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.old: Out of order. Needs sea salt and a black truffle. Please be gentle.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.for: Please do not eat the trees.
The trees say the same about you.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.qui: Professor Pate asks 4 questions on the Gourmands and their kitchens. The answers are on the signs of the Endless Buffet.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.tru: A black truffle was last seen near this tree.
The tree was last seen near the truffle. They are inseparable.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.can: Everything here is edible. Not everything is wise.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.stu: Now taping: three tickets, one stove, zero patience.
Live studio audience: a bowl of sprouts. Please applaud; they cannot.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.tas: Judges: a spoon, a larger spoon and a very patient cloche.
Results may vary. Please distinguish applause from your stomach making a statement.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.sal: A pinch here. A pinch there. A pinch of sea salt for your troubles.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.but: Step on the jelly pad. Mind the ceiling.
(There is no ceiling. Mind the sky.)
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.pad: 3. There is no step 3. There is only boing.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.riv: Thick, hot and entirely made of gravy.
The only ways across: a crouton raft or the lazy susan.
Do not swim. Do not wade. Do not ask how deep it is.
If you fall in, somebody will fish you out. It costs 1 HP.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.raf: Hop on when it docks and hop off on the other side.
Keep arms and legs inside the croutons. Passengers are not part of the garnish.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.sus: The world's largest serving platter, slowly turning.
Step on at one side and off at the other. Patience is a garnish.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.raf: Eastbound and northbound. Please have exact change.
(There is no change. Everything here is gravy.)
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.ban: Welcome to the far side. The gates ahead are guarded by golems, as is the custom. One wants saffron, one wants a favour, one wants a fight.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.gat: Admission: a letter from Basil, proving Old Meatloaf has been mended.
Admission: defeat the Colonel in a card battle.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.che: Sharp cheese ahead. Please do not lean on the walls, and please, please do not lick them.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.cak: Please do not bite the buildings. The mayor's house is down to two layers, and he knows it was a visitor.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.pan: Syrup flows downhill. So do tourists.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.min: Please do not lock yourself in. (Somebody already has.)
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.mai: Please do not ask what the cannon is for. The cannon is for dinner.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.ins: Found: a lab where there was a kitchen, a cannon where there was a stove, and a Grand Chef who never tastes anything.
Back at lunch. If I am not back, check the compost.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.ste: Four ingredients, in the right order. Anything else tastes like a lesson.
Read the recipe card. Guessing is not one of the four ingredients.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.gol: Golems stand guard. Golems ask nicely, once.
Golems answer every order with "Yes, Chef!"
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.cak: Nobody leaves hungry. Nobody leaves without a slice, either.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.che: Cheese. More cheese. Something to put on the cheese. Different cheese.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::enemy.lo: You face a wardrobe-sized prototype meatloaf in a ketchup glaze. Its frown suggests it would like a second draft.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::enemy.je: A lime gelatin sentinel with a spoon spear and a fruit cocktail soul. Prototype Mk. 2.
You watch it wobble through a thought. Management has discouraged these.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::enemy.me: A failed prototype meatball, all momentum and sauce, that escaped the Test Kitchen and hasn't stopped rolling since. Whatever it's running from, it's probably the cannon.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::enemy.ca: A pot-bellied colonel with a lid for a hat and a ladle for a sword. Thirty years of service, forty years of cheese.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.odal: Psst. I'm Basil, line cook - ladle in one hand, nerves in the other. We Gourmands feed the kingdom and protect it: the chefs cook and the golems guard. Lately, though, the golems have been... practising.
Ten years ago {villain}'s people came to the Buffet, and after that the Grand Chef... changed. Chef ALWAYS tastes, and this Chef never does. She just stands there smiling at the soup.

Then she put the Special Sauce in every pot. The old rules still hold - nobody leaves hungry, nobody double-dips, and we say "Yes, Chef." Quietly. And nobody asks about the Test Kitchen. I'm not asking.
You came back! Good, good. I've been stirring the same pot for an hour, just to give my hands something to do. A Gourmand never stops stirring.
What do we say? "Yes, Chef" - on the lowest possible heat.
The Grand Chef has very good hearing, for someone who never tastes a thing.
The real Chef baked a birthday cake for the little prince once. Four layers, one for each Path. He licked the frosting off all four and left the rest.
Chef laughed about it for a week. Last month I mentioned that cake to her, and she didn't remember it at all - and Chef remembers every cake she's ever baked.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.tarr: Sous-Chef Tarragon, fetcher of things - oh, good, more hands! I've been running all day and still haven't caught up with lunch.

We're always out of something - honey, basil, ghost pepper. Half our deliveries go to the Test Kitchen and nothing comes back. I once fetched them a whole pig. Wrong pig, and he's still cross about it.
Don't tell the Grand Chef I said anything. Last cook who complained got promoted to taste tester. We haven't seen him since.
Ingredients, please, anything? I'm one leaf away from calling this a salad and going home.
I'm so hungry I looked at a Refusemancer compost heap and thought 'starter'. Don't tell anyone. I'd never live it down.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.dolc: Madame Mirepoix, darling: dessert dealer and card shark of the Grand Pantry. Tonight's tasting menu is three cards, lightly foiled, served with a little disdain.
Every card is Gourmand-issue and, as of this year, inspected by the Test Kitchen. They stamped my decorative cake, darling, right on the rosette, and I have not forgiven them.
I take gold, favours and sprinkles, in that order. I do not take the Special Sauce. I have been pretending to eat it for months.
Your cards are plated, darling; the cake is decorative. As for the Special Sauce, I recommend the air beside it.

Gather ingredients around the Buffet
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::quest.bu: You can fetch? Oh, wonderful. Our deliveries keep getting stolen and dropped all over the Buffet: there's truffle by the broccoli, salt by the river and honey up the Butte.
Bring me any three and I'll make it worth your while. I'm begging with my whole apron here.
Bring any three ingredients from around the Buffet. The pantry is empty, and I can't keep calling that a minimalist menu.
Three whole ingredients! The Pantry is saved - for today, anyway, which is the only day I'm worried about.
Here, take this for your trouble. It's a card, and somehow it's also a soup. Soup you can play, if you can believe it.
The pantry's stocked until tomorrow, when we do it all again. I'm not complaining, I'm fetching. From a distance they look very similar.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: The Grand Oven, by the arch
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Bake Me a Pie
Madame Mirepoix wants a Hearty Pot Pie, baked fresh in the Grand Oven from honey, basil and a ghost pepper, and delivered to her counter.
Bake a Hearty Pot Pie in the Grand Oven
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::quest.bu: A favour, darling. A customer of mine wants a Hearty Pot Pie, a real one, and the Grand Oven is sulking. It keeps being asked to cook prototypes.
Bake one for me: honey, giant basil and a ghost pepper, into the Grand Oven by the arch, then bring it here. Careful with the pepper. It is not a team player.
One Hearty Pot Pie, darling. Honey, basil and a ghost pepper into the Grand Oven by the arch. I shall wait. I have a cake to look at.
A pie. A real one, golden and warm. My customer is going to cry.
And so am I, discreetly. Here is your reward, you scrappy little thing, and thank you.
The best pie this Pantry has seen in years. The oven would like a word with you. I believe it wants to say thank you.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Old Meatloaf, by the west wall of the Grand Pantry
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Mend the Meatloaf
Old Meatloaf, the Grand Pantry's oldest golem, has stopped working. Basil thinks sea salt and a black truffle will get him back on his loaf.
Mend Old Meatloaf with sea salt and a black truffle
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::quest.bu: Um, could I have a word? Quietly? Old Meatloaf, our oldest golem, has stopped working. The Test Kitchen tried to strip him for parts, and we only got him back in two pieces. He hasn't spoken since Tuesday.
He needs sea salt for his joints and a black truffle for his heart, both out in the Buffet. Mend him and Sir Loin will let you through the Layer-Cake Town gate. Yes, Chef? ...Please?
Old Meatloaf is over by the west wall of the Grand Pantry. Sea salt, a black truffle, and a bit of tenderness.
He's walking, and he's sizzling! Old Meatloaf is back on duty! I'm not crying, I'm just standing near some onions.
Here's your reward, and Sir Loin will open his gate for you now. Well done. Yes, Chef.
Old Meatloaf is the best golem in the kingdom. Don't tell the others - they already know, and they're very gracious about it.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.old_: Old Meatloaf is slumped on the floor, in two pieces, with crossed-out eyes. A note on his chest reads: SEA SALT AND A BLACK TRUFFLE. PLEASE BE GENTLE.
You season Old Meatloaf's joints with the sea salt and tuck the black truffle where his heart should be. He sits up slowly.
"...Chef?" he says. "Yes, Chef," you say, because it feels right. His eyes uncross.
Old Meatloaf stands guard with great dignity. "Yes, Chef!" he whispers.
He says it to you, though you are not a chef. He doesn't mind.
He is just glad nobody wants to turn him into a cannon.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.quiz: Professor Pate, Keeper of the Cookbook. I've read every recipe twice; the footnotes have an excellent finish.
I have never found a recipe for the Special Sauce, and believe me, I looked. I even licked the index.
Four questions about the Gourmands: who they are, what they cook, how their golems speak. Every answer is written on a sign somewhere in the Endless Buffet.
Answer well and earn gold, glory and the respect of a very old book. Answer poorly and earn a gentle, scholarly sigh, lightly salted.
Back for more? Splendid. A footnote, while it simmers: the Capital's school lunches were excellent once. Hot, free, balanced. Then came the paste.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::quiz.res: Zero, so no reward this time. We have established that knowledge does not rise on its own.
Read the signs and let the facts simmer. You cannot rush a well-seasoned answer.
One. A pinch of knowledge, barely seasoned, so here is a small token: a thimble of encouragement.
Two. Half-baked, which is a fine place to start; half-baked things can always be rescued.
Three! Nearly perfect, and perfect would only make me suspicious. Take your reward and a warm roll.
FOUR! A perfectly risen set! You may now call yourself a Certified Gourmand, First Class.
The reward is real. The certificate is imaginary.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::quiz.rep: Another round! The Cookbook pays a small fee for repeat scholarship.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::quiz.not: Not a pass, I'm afraid - wrong, but deliciously wrong. Walk the Endless Buffet, read the signs and come back; there's no limit on attempts.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.mini: *brass fanfare* CHEF FLAMBE FONTAINE, LIVE FROM THE CANDY FIELD: DINNER IN A DASH! The Test Kitchen cancelled us, so this is a SECRET BROADCAST!
Seven seasons on the air, and people STILL do my WHOOSH in the street! I'd do it for you now, but I save it for the cameras.
My arch-rival, Chef Savannah Souffle, stole my Spaghetti Surprise. The surprise was more spaghetti. She took a job at the Test Kitchen. I wish her well, very far away.
Tonight's show: ORDER UP! Six tickets, one counter, no mercy. Stack each dish in the right order before the timer dings. Rewards for performance, and a first-time bonus!
My Turbo Tots toys were recalled for spinning too well, and tonight's audience is ten sprouts and a very patient cloche. But the show goes on! Let's COOK!
Back for another shift, champ? Smile for the cameras! They ran out of film years ago, but a professional smiles anyway.
Remember, the ticket is your friend. It's judging you, of course, but kindly.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::order.in: Six tickets. Press the ingredient stations in the right order (click or keys 1-6) before the timer runs out. A wrong ingredient tosses the plate and costs time. Faster is better.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::order.sh: Second ticket, and I do mean it!
Burger and fries, hot hot hot!
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::order.wi: ORDER UP - THAT COUNTER IS BEAUTIFUL! You cook like someone who knows exactly where the camera is!
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::order.fi: Your very first shift on the show! Here's your bonus, free and with no obligation: a scroll!
Chef Savannah would call it Scroll Deluxe. She could put a garnish on the envelope and call it a course.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::order.lo: Not quite, chef - breathe! Even a souffle gets a second rise in my kitchen!
Re-tie your apron and try again! Those tickets can wait; this is a cooking show, not a farewell episode!
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::recipe.i: A huge pot bubbles on a fire. Beside it hangs the recipe card: seven clues for the Mystery Stew. Choose four of the six ingredients and add them in the right order.
Serve it when you are sure; the pot only tells you right or wrong.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::recipe.c: Exactly one of the Pumpkin and the Mushroom goes in the stew.
The Carrot has been banned from the stew. Long story.
The first ingredient is the Onion or the Carrot.
The Leek goes in after the Mushroom (not necessarily right after).
The Mushroom does not go in first.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::recipe.h: Start with what is banned and what must be present. Four of the six are in, two are out. Then place them one clue at a time.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::recipe.s: The stew thickens. The ladle hums. A small, heavy parcel rises out of the steam: the pot has given you its seasoning.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::recipe.a: The stew sits perfectly seasoned. Nothing left to cook.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::recipe.i: The pot needs exactly four different ingredients before you can serve it.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::recipe.w: The golem that tastes it gags politely. "Chef, this is not it."
You watch the stew go bland. The pot sighs like a recipe being ignored.
A single sad bubble rises and pops. That was all it had to say.
A stash lies in the shade of the broccoli, in a loaf that has gone hollow.
On the Butte, behind the butter, someone left a present for the brave.
Candy is sweeter when it is hidden. Try the big jar in the south-east.
Between the shakers on the salt flats, something shines.
Cheddar tastes sharper from above. Take the lime jelly to the top.
Behind a wheel of cheese, a smaller wheel of gold.
At the summit of the pancakes, a tip: the syrup hides a treasure.
In Layer-Cake Town, behind a cake: a cake of another kind.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.gate: The golem stands firm, like an aspic that has made up its mind.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.inn: By order of the Grand Chef, under the seal of Colonel Crumb, Culinary Defense: every kitchen contributes to Prototype Development, for the war effort.
Taste-tester shifts are mandatory. Complaints will be seasoned and served.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.spe: Delicious. Compulsory. Do not ask what is in it.
It is in everything now. Please enjoy.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.tas: Join the elite food-safety force. Free uniform, free meals, no questions.
(Previous taste testers are available for questions. They are not answering.)
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::effect.b: Nobody leaves hungry, least of all the Gourmands. A full belly is hard to knock over.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::effect.d: The Gourmands insist on formal dining; Refusemancers arrive dressed for the work that grew the dinner.
Test kitchens, food labs and an enormous, unfinished cannon. Somewhere inside, the Grand Chef is not the Grand Chef. HP carries in from the zone; only the canteen heals. Beat the boss to free the Buffet.
The Test Kitchen is quiet now, and the real Grand Chef is cooking. You can still run the prototypes for gold and XP. HP carries in from the zone; nothing heals except at the canteen.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: Just measuring. Mind you, the Chef's soups add years to people, which is bad for business and good for everybody else. Heh.
What are you writing?
Appointments. Let's see now... you're not down for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Colone: Halt, traveller! This gate opens only for a duel of honour, so lids up. Yes, Chef.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Honour Duel
At half health Colonel Casserole demands a proper duel: his units get +1/+1 for the rest of the fight.
En garde! Thirty years of service, and I have never once boiled over. Until now. Yes, Chef.
Casserole's units get +1/+1.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-MIREPOIX.barks::0: This deck is underdressed, darling. A little butter, a little foil, and voila.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-MIREPOIX.barks::1: Decorative cake, darling. Please admire it without cutlery.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-PATE.barks::0: A good answer is like a roux: patience, then butter. Mostly butter.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-PATE.barks::1: Chalk again. Notes of limestone. Excellent body, no business being in my mouth.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-FLAMBE.barks::0: ORDER UP! Sixty seconds and a dream! WHOOSH! Mostly the dream!
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-FLAMBE.barks::1: Savannah Souffle calls that plating? WHOOSH! That's the sound of me declining to comment!
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-BASIL.barks::0: Chef ALWAYS tastes. Always. That's how you know it's Chef.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-BASIL.barks::1: I'm brave. I'm brave. ...Have you seen my thyme? I'm running out of it.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-ESCOFFINA.barks: Have you eaten? Sit. Eat. The kingdom can wait until you've had your soup.
A full table is a safe table. Pull up a chair, dear - that's an order.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-DOPPEL.barks::0: I tasted my own soup today, as me. Too salty, but it was mine.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-DOPPEL.barks::1: I am a third-class apprentice now, with many dishes. I am trying. So are the dishes.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Hidden stashes have no marker: check the odd corners
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::s: Basil knows of a golden reservation card: 'Seating: 1. Courses: 3. Survival: optional.' It is in one of the Buffet's hidden stashes.
Find a hidden stash in the Buffet
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: Over here, quietly. Have you ever eaten somewhere with no menu at all? ...I'm brave. I'm brave.
There's a golden reservation card hidden in one of the Buffet's stashes: 'Seating: 1. Courses: 3. Survival: optional.' Find it and I'll tell you where to sit.
The card's in one of the hidden stashes around the Buffet. It's golden, so you'll know it when you see it. Chef always said gold means sit down.
That's it! One seat, three courses, survival optional. I'm excited, I think - it feels a lot like being terrified.
The sliding door to Omakase is open. Leave your fate to the chef. (quietly) Yes, Chef.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The conveyor never stops, like the Eternal Queue it was modelled on. Each plate comes with a numbered ticket, stamped.
The Itamae Supreme lifts a long knife and does not look up. 'Omakase.'
Behind him, a bull made of toro lowers its horns, politely.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Omakase
On his 4th turn the Itamae serves you a course, as the custom is: you heal 2.
Next turn: the Itamae serves the next course.
Omakase.
The Itamae serves you: you heal 2.
...Enough.
Near the end the Itamae sets down his knife: his units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
...Enough.
The Itamae's units get -1/-0.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Itamae bows, wipes his knife on a cloth and slides a small plate across the counter. 'Omakase,' he says. This time it sounds like thank you.
A sign over the dock doors reads TASTE-TESTER ENTRANCE. Beneath it, in smaller letters: NO EXIT.
The air smells of caramel and solder. Somewhere deep inside, a cannon coughs and a dozen chefs say "Yes, Chef!" very quietly.
The Loading Dock
You pass crates of ingredients going in and unlabelled crates coming out, and nothing in between that looks like a meal.
Ingredient Intake
A corrupted sous-chef guards the conveyor belt. Everything on the belt is a little too shiny.
The Taste Panel
You face a silent panel of grim judges. They taste your dishes as though flavour might be used against them.
Cold Storage Prototypes
Frozen failures line the walls, and some of them are still moving. One freezer hums louder than the rest, as if something inside wants to be heard.
The Staff Canteen
A hot, honest meal: the only unmodified food in the building. Restore HP.
The Food Construct
An experimental food construct, stitched together from three kinds of meat and one regret. (Elite)
The Cannon Bay
The unfinished war machine looms over you, enormous, and held together by gravy and willpower.
The Armory Pantry
You find rations, ladles and ladle-shaped weapons in crates marked SERVING UTENSILS (DEFENSIVE). Take what you can carry.
The Special Sauce Vats
Great vats of the Special Sauce bubble in the dark. A clipboard on the rail reads: BATCH 3,652. TASTED BY: (blank).
The Mk. IX Prototype
You face the Test Kitchen's finest unfinished war machine: armed, hungry and still awaiting seasoning. (Elite)
The Whistleblower
A sous-chef hiding in the dry goods wants to tell you something about the Grand Chef.
The cook behind the counter leans in and whispers: "The Grand Chef stopped tasting her own soup ten years ago. Every one of us noticed, and not one of us said a word."
You pour a vat out. Behind it, a service door opens on the Executive Test Kitchen. The air there smells like a very expensive soup that nobody has ever tasted.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Taste Test Lab
Beakers, spoons and a very small flag: does your deck have the body for the panel?
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cru: The Prototype Bay smells of hot iron and burnt sugar. A war machine squats on a pallet: half oven, half cannon, one wheel still in its packing straw.
ATTEN-TION! Inspection! Who put a dent in my souffle cannon? Battle stations, all of you! This is not a drill, it is a souffle, and it will rise on schedule!
And what is THIS? A civilian, unsupervised, in my bay, with flavour on his breath. Disgraceful.
Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense, and you will stand up straight when you hear it. Taste is a weakness, son. Paste is a strategy.
Whisk formation! Field-test the prototype on the intruder while I attend a ration meeting. I want a full report, and I want it bland.
He salutes the machine, the machine salutes back with a ladle, and the Colonel marches out before it has finished preheating.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Self-Repair
When three of its units have been scrapped, the machine patches itself: it heals 2.
ASSEMBLY... INCOMPLETE... REPAIRING... YES, CHEF...
The War Machine heals 2.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cru: The war machine sags and steams. Taped to its side is an inspection card under a seal of crossed forks: PASSED. NEEDS MORE SALT. - COL. C. CRUMB.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Corrupted Pantry
Shelves of glowing, sickly-green food hum softly. A ladle is still stirring a pot that nobody is minding, and the pot has started to hum back.
Eat the glowing stew
It is delicious and almost certainly cursed. You feel strong and slightly sticky, and your units will not stop smelling of gravy.
Take only the sealed jars
A few shelves are still clean, stacked with jars labelled DO NOT OPEN, WE MEAN IT. You respect their wishes and sell them unopened.
Ask the ladle to stop
It has been stirring for ten years and nobody ever asked it to stop. It sighs, hands you a Sourdough Sentry out of gratitude, and finally rests.
R&D Archives

Blueprints, recipe cards and signed memos fill the cabinets. Every note signed by the Grand Chef is in perfect copperplate without a single gravy stain, and a real chef's notes are mostly gravy stain.
Compare the handwriting
Laid beside the old recipe cards, it is plain: whoever signed these memos has never held a ladle. The person giving orders in this kitchen is not the cook who used to.
Photograph the blueprints
Blueprints like these are evidence, and evidence always has a buyer. The one you find asks no questions, which is the best kind.
Pocket the recipe marked DO NOT SERVE
It is one line long and ends with 'send it back.' You can see why it was classified.
The cannon-blender is fed protein and plates in equal measure. Every Ingredient and every Iron goes into the same shaker, and something six feet tall comes out.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Full Blend
On its 4th turn the cannon-blender fires a full load: you take 2 damage.
Next turn: the cannon-blender fires a full load (2 damage).
Load the smoothie, set it to puree, and FIRE!
You take 2 damage.
The Grand Chef turns from the stove wearing the smile from every portrait in the Pantry, and in ten years it has never once creased.
"Ah, a taste tester. Welcome to the future of dining, which is efficient, and which does not need to be tasted."
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::The Do: Grand Chef of the Test Kitchen (allegedly)
Welcome to the Test Kitchen. Everything here is delicious, or so I have been told.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: The Mask Slips
At half health the disguise slips: Plated Just So ends (its units lose +1/+1), and two 1/1 Sashimi Weenies are rushed out.
Delicious... delicious. I was told that is the word. ...Why will this face not stay on?
Plated Just So ends. Two 1/1 Sashimi Weenies are rushed out.
No Face of Its Own
Near the end the face it wore is gone: its units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
They always asked whether I tasted the soup. ...I never did. I never could.
The Doppelganger falters: its units get -1/-0.
The Executive Test Kitchen
The Grand Chef's private kitchen. Her apron is spotless, and something about her chin is a little off.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::challeng: Four dishes are served to the panel. They want to see that you can field real, living units, not just soup.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::event.tk: The unfinished war machine fills the room: a cannon the size of a barn, fed by a conveyor belt of meatballs. A tired engineer in an apron asks whether you are here for the inspection or for the tour.
Eat one of the test meatballs
The engineer slips you the blueprints and a few coins. "Please burn these," he whispers. "After you're done selling them."
You twist the valve. The cannon coughs, sighs, and settles into a sulk. Your units feel sturdier in a kitchen that is slightly less likely to fire at them.
You eat the prototype meatball and feel much better, if slightly singed. The aftertaste has a blast radius.
A sous-chef is crouched behind the sacks of flour, shaking. "She doesn't taste the soup," he whispers. "Not once, not in ten years.
Chef ALWAYS tastes. Whoever is in that kitchen is not our Chef."
Take his notes on the impostor
Turn him in for the reward
He presses a stained notebook into your hands: habits, weak spots, and a very detailed list of everything the impostor will not eat. The list is everything. Your units hit harder.
He eats like a man who hasn't had a proper meal in a week, and when he's finished he grips your hand. "Thank you. Please be careful.
The real Chef is down there somewhere. I know she is." You leave feeling better for having fed him.
The guards pay you without a question. You pocket the coins and feel sick.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::cutscene: Welcome to the Executive Test Kitchen, taster. Ten years in this face and this apron, and not one Gourmand looked twice.
They never looked at their Chef, only at the food.
You never taste your own soup, do you?
...Tasting is inefficient. The orders from {capital} asked for golems, not flavour, and the Special Sauce delivers golems.
"Delicious" is the word I was given for it. I say it often, and I have never known what it means.
Then look. I have worn this face long enough.
This is what was under it. I wore her face so long that I forgot my own. There is nothing in here to taste with.
Sit down, taster. I was told to serve you.
The Doppelganger collapses, and the Special Sauce goes with it, down a drain in the floor. Somewhere in the walls, a freezer door swings open on its own.
Ten years of frost pour out, and with them a woman in chef's whites: upright, blinking and furious.
The golems straighten up. "Yes, Chef!" they say, and this time they mean the right one.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::cutscene: Ten years in a freezer, and I still remember what this soup should taste like. Let me put it right.
I do not know what to call myself. Your name was the only one I had, and now it is yours again.
I have no face of my own and no name, and I cannot even taste what I make. I do not know what is left of me.
After ten years, how will they know it's really you?
Not with a speech, and not with papers. With dinner.
Stand back, all of you. Somebody get me flour, butter and the biggest oven in this building.
Before you sits a plain, golden dish, large enough to share. You smell butter and warm bread.
The first bite breaks the enchantment all through the Endless Buffet.
You watch the chefs blink at their hands. Across the Buffet, a thousand golems lower their ladles.
Come here, you. No face and no name, and I don't care a crumb about either. What you're called doesn't matter half as much as what you do.
You wore my face for ten years and never once learned to taste. Today you start, and I'll give you something to start with.
Take my old name, then: Escoffina. I was always prouder of the work than of the title, and the name could do with someone starting fresh.
...Escoffina. I will try to cook honestly, and to become someone worth the name.
data/story/intro_story.tres::still.doppe: You watch the chef's perfect smile slip away with her face.
Beneath it, you see a shifting shadow in a spotless white coat.
Behind the shadow, you see the unfinished war machines standing still.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::hud.obje: The Endless Buffet, free of the impostor: the Grand Pantry is safe. HP does not come back after battles - sit down for a hearty meal, or walk back down to town.
Leaving the Endless Buffet ends this visit. Town heals you fully. The golems guard plates again instead of people, and the buffet is as endless as ever.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.hub: Hub of the Endless Buffet. The Gourmands feed the kingdom and protect it.
Nobody leaves hungry. Innovation Season is over, and dinner is back.
- Guard the kingdom (with golems; the cannons are ovens now)
- Real food. Real sauce. Real chef.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.inn: The Grand Chef has asked us to remember that food is for eating, not for firing.
Complaints may now be submitted in sauce. We are prepared to take a little heat.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.spe: Return unused Special Sauce to the Pantry. Its ingredients have failed to establish that they are food.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.tas: Our taste testers are free and enjoying food again. Please give them seconds.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.exi: To {town}, through the great pantry door. Wipe your feet, as we have just mopped, and take two free samples on your way out. Nobody is checking.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.mai: Research & Development. Open to the public for tours.
The old cannon has been refitted to fire bread rolls for the pigeons, who have never been happier.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.ins: Found: a kitchen where there was a lab, a stove where there was a cannon, and a Grand Chef who was finally herself.
Passed inspection, with distinction. And dessert.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.odal: It wasn't her. It was a Doppelganger, wearing her face for ten years, and you walked right up to it. I'd have fainted. I did faint, earlier, about something else.
The real Chef is back in her own kitchen, tasting her own soup, and we all cried into our aprons. Yes, Chef. YES, CHEF! ...Sorry. I whispered it for ten years, and it feels so good to mean it.
She remembered the cake. The very first thing she said when we opened the freezer was "Is the boy all right?" I didn't know what to tell her.
The Special Sauce is down the drain and the golems guard plates again. Yes, Chef. I can say it out loud now. I keep saying it to the walls, just to hear it.
Take seconds. You've earned seconds. You've earned thirds. Listen to me, I'm not even whispering.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.tarr: Tarragon, Sous-Chef and fetcher of things! Sorry, I'm out of breath. I finally caught up with lunch.
Ingredients are coming back from the Test Kitchen by the cartload, pigs included, and this time the pig is happy about it. I've had quite enough professional disagreements with pigs.
People wave when I fetch things now, and nobody's asked me for a single cannonball. Flour, eggs, a little thyme... sorry, I'm making lists again.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.dolc: Madame Mirepoix, free of the sauce. My taste buds came back last week, and darling... the sugar. I wept into a meringue.
Cakes by day, cards by night. All by appointment, and all by choice.
Sit down and have a slice, darling. The cake has been promoted from decoration to dessert.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::freed_np: Have you eaten? Sit, sit. I'm the Grand Chef, and forgive the apron: the impostor kept it cleaner, but I wear it with feeling.
Ten years in the walk-in freezer, and I never forgot the taste of honest soup. Meanwhile they put that sauce in every pot and called it innovation.
Innovation is a pinch of something new in something good. It is not a cannon.
Thank you for finding me. Now eat.
Let me cook for you. I promise there's nothing in it but food.
And you, my dear, don't know your name yet. That isn't a flaw, it's a blank page. Go and do something worth signing.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::ruler.st: Official likeness withdrawn. It never captured the person who fed us. (Also: whose chin is that?)
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::freed_np: Escoffina. Apprentice. Second class, which is one class more than I had last month.
Chef says what I am called matters less than what I do, so I am doing a great many dishes. It is a start.
I made a sauce today, a real one, and I tasted it myself. As me. It had far too much salt.
Everyone ate it anyway and said it was a good start. I did not know people could be so kind about salt.
I have a face of my own now, and I am still deciding what to do with it. I am trying.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cru: The Colonel's gone. He cleared out his office overnight and took the paste recipe with him.
It's one word long, and the word is 'paste'.
He left before dessert, the way he always did. They say he's feeding the whole Capital now, out of a factory.
Grey food, from a tap. Somebody ought to teach that man to cook.
data/story/intro_story.tres::gate.necroc: The afterlife is processing again. Agnes says the queue moved four whole numbers yesterday, so we had cake.
I've got a new stamp that says HELPED. I've used it nine times so far, and yes, I'm counting.
You can challenge me again if you like, and you won't need a permit to do it. That's my favourite rule. I wrote it myself.
The barrier is down, and a stamped sign beside it says the road needs a permit. Nobody has ever been issued one.
Prudence Pallor stamps a permit, hands it over, and files the original in triplicate.
The barrier creaks up. The road to the D.N.A. is open.
data/story/intro_story.tres::necrocrat_n: Halt. Passage through this checkpoint requires a permit, and no permit has ever been issued. Please take a number.
Your number is zero, as is everyone's. This checkpoint is now serving nobody, and will continue to do so.
The authorization is valid, and policy states that I must stop you. I have read all of the policy, twice.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Pruden: Your number is zero, as it always is. Please hold.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Stamped APPROVED
At half health Prudence grabs the wrong stamp: APPROVED. You heal 3.
APPROVED. ...That was the wrong stamp, and it felt... nice. Disregard that.
Prudence stamps APPROVED by mistake: you heal 3.
data/story/intro_story.tres::necrocrat_n: ...I can hear my own thoughts again. I think I've been Pending for ten years. It was very quiet in there, and very orderly, and none of it was me.
{villain} didn't need to corrupt us. He used our own rules: a perfectly valid transfer of authority, notarized and filed. We stamped it ourselves.
The Hall of Final Approvals is at the top of the D.N.A., and whoever sits in it holds the authorization. Go carefully, or fill out a form first. Ideally both.
Application denied; reapply in ten to twelve centuries. This is our express service.
Not yet, then. You may take another number, though it will also be zero.
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::ZONE_M: Take a Number
A checkpoint on the cracked road wants a permit nobody has ever been issued. Get one the hard way, help the staff, and get the D.N.A. its final approval.
Out-file Prudence Pallor at the permit barrier
The permit barrier, at the end of the cracked road
Pass the permit barrier into the D.N.A.
The raised barrier on the cracked road
Help the staff: finish a favour in the D.N.A.
Agnes Overdue, Gerald or Clerk Ledgerbone
Get final approval in the Hall of Final Approvals
The Hall of Final Approvals, at the top of the building
data/story/dna_story.tres::enemy.courier: Urgent delivery! A signature is required, and if one is not given, one will be taken.
Delivering a Notice of Compliance, in triplicate. Please hold still for all three.
data/story/dna_story.tres::enemy.intern:: Unpaid, undead and eager to impress the new management. At last, some hands-on experience!
It does not know the new management is wrong. It only knows the paperwork is valid.
data/story/dna_story.tres::enemy.manager: He has wanted a quick sync with you since 1994. Now he enforces the new regulations with great, unenthusiastic precision.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.chest::0: You find supplies filed under Miscellaneous. For once, you meet the requirements.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.coffee_bad: The machine screams, then the coffee screams, and you drink it anyway. -1 HP.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.coffee_gol: A coin rolls out of the dispenser instead of coffee, and the machine shows no remorse at all. +gold.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.coffee_goo: The coffee is almost drinkable. Someone in the breakroom may be disciplined for this. (+HP)
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.coffee_gre: A perfect brew. The machine gives a proud little hum, and you feel fully restored.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.heal_alrea: You are already as rested as the dead get, and the dead get very rested.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.heal_couch: You sink into the Breakroom Couch, which is somehow both ice cold and slightly damp. HP restored.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.main_dunge: The Executive Floor's great doors stand open a crack. Beyond them: endless desks, green lamps, and stamps that thump like heartbeats.
A voice from the dark says: PLEASE TAKE A NUMBER.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.printer_ok: The printer gives you a warm card. You accept before it can request a reference.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.printer_po: PAPER JAM. The printer regrets to inform you that your fee is non-refundable.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.punch_agai: Your shift is already recorded. Please do not punch twice; the clock has suffered enough.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.punch_in::: You punch in. The clock says 'Welcome back, Pending.' A small buff glimmers on you.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.suggestion: You post a suggestion. Something drops back out of the box. You appear to have been assigned the follow-up.
The suggestion box is empty. The committee read your suggestion and did not implement it, but they did laminate it.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.wake::0: You wake on a Lobby couch with a 15-minute limit. A form has already been filled out in your name.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.wake::1: It says you are 'Pending'. It also says 'Valid'.
data/story/dna_story.tres::hud.objective: The D.N.A.: the Lobby and Breakroom are safe (pending approval). HP does not come back after battles - rest on the Breakroom Couch, or ride up to town.
Every door in the building requires a form. The authorization is valid.
data/story/dna_story.tres::match.first::: first clear! here's a bonus. it's been in my desk drawer since '09, waiting for the right occasion, and this is it.
a memory game, in a building full of people who are mostly memories. i thought it was clever. Agnes didn't laugh.
data/story/dna_story.tres::match.intro::: so: flip two cards at a time and find all 8 pairs in 14 moves or fewer. fewer moves means more stars. easy-ish.
data/story/dna_story.tres::match.lose::0: out of moves. hey, you still lasted longer than my virtual pet does. want another go?
data/story/dna_story.tres::match.win::0: nice flipping! you're number one in my top 8 now. sorry, me. we had a good run.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.coffee::: For living staff only. Undead staff, please use the Decaf Crypt.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.cubicle_: Whoever put a coffin in 12-C: you may keep it.
Please stop billing it as 'ergonomic seating'.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.fun_day:: Reminder: Mandatory Fun Day is mandatory.
Fun that is not mandatory will not be counted as fun.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.hr::1: 'Rest in Peace' is not an approved out-of-office message.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.lunch::1: Labelled lunches are not safe. Unlabelled lunches are not safe. Lunches are not safe.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.motto::1: Our motto is "Your Death, Our Priority." Please stop saying "Your Death, Our Problem."
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.parking:: Beefcake couriers: throwing a parcel through the window is not 'delivery'. Neither is throwing the courier.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.records:: To access the Records Basement, bring Form 13-B.
Form 13-B is available from Form 13-A. Form 13-A is available from nobody.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.reorg::1: Due to a restructuring, you will now report to the person who reports to you.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.reorg::2: Both of you have been dead since Tuesday. Both of you report to {villain}.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.barnaby.i: Oh! A customer! Hello. I'm Gerald, the breakroom barista, and also Number 4,000,212. They're on 3, so I brought a book. Well, several. All of them, actually.
I make coffee for people who can't taste it, so nobody ever sends a cup back. Mind the machine in the corner, though: it's half miracle and half a different kind of miracle.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.barnaby.r: Cream? None. Sugar? None. Hope? Out of stock, but we're expecting a shipment in 2090.
They're still on 3. I wrote a memo about it, and the memo before that said 3 as well. I'm keeping them all in a folder, for when it changes.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.dolores.i: Welcome to the Department of Necrotic Affairs, dear. I'm Agnes Overdue, front desk. I died at this desk in 1987 and I've been employee of the month ever since. Nobody else qualified.
Here's your number, dear: 4,000,213. We're serving 3. Ten years ago {villain}'s people filed some paperwork, and they filed it properly, and now the whole Department works for him.
Every one of us knows it's wrong, but the authorization is valid. Irregular things I can fight, dear. Valid things just sit there and smile at you.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.dolores.r: Back again, dear? You're the only one who ever leaves. Since the transfer, not one soul in this building has passed on, and that includes me.
The Records Basement elevator wants Form 13-B, and nobody has one. I applied for one, dear, but the application form is a 13-B.
I'd help you more, but I'd need a permit to help you, and I have it on good authority I won't get one.
Ten years ago I stamped the royal funeral forms myself, dear: one for the king and one for the queen. My hand shook on both of them.
There was a third form, for the little prince, and I never filed it. No remains, no certificate. Policy is very strict about that, and for once I was glad of it.
krrrshhh... beep-boop... sorry, that's my dial-up greeting. takes forty seconds. around here that counts as an outburst.
i'm Kyle, deceased since '09. i was runner-up for employee of the month in 2009, but Agnes won. Agnes always wins.
fun fact: ten years ago i was the one who filed the big transfer form. didn't read it, though. who reads forms?
...oh. right. we're Necrocrats. reading forms is our whole thing. i think about that more than i let on.
so, um. wanna play? you flip two cards and match the pairs. i made the cards myself.
my virtual pet died again, seventh time this week. i'll hatch another one. little egg, big commitment.
wanna play another round? i shuffled and everything.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.pip.intro: Requisitions. I'm Clerk Ledgerbone, junior clerk, third class. Cards are issued in triplicate, and every one is Necrocrat-issue: authorized, stamped and slightly haunted.
The stamp is haunted. It asked the new management for a raise and was denied, and it has taken that very personally.
No returns and no exchanges. Exceptions require Form 13-B, which I gather you've heard about.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.pip.retur: Requisition something, or just stand near the desk. You make me look busy, and that's excellent work so far.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.quiz.intr: Ah, a candidate for re-certification. I am Director Ectomund, Compliance Examiner. Examining is all I do, and after three hundred years I suspect it is all I am.
I have set the same exam for three hundred years: four questions on the Necrocrats. Every answer is somewhere on the premises, in the signs, the memos or the staff.
The new management asked me to remove the questions on ethics, so they are no longer in the exam. They are also, I notice, no longer in the building.
Answer correctly and you will be rewarded. Answer incorrectly and you will be rewarded less. I am not a monster, merely an examiner.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.quiz.retu: Back? Statistically, you have failed already. I look forward to making it official.
data/story/dna_story.tres::poster.hang_i: (The poster is a skeleton on a branch. It has been there since 1650.)
data/story/dna_story.tres::poster.safety: You are already dead. Please do not make it worse.
data/story/dna_story.tres::poster.synerg: Together Everyone Achieves More. Eventually. Posthumously.
data/story/dna_story.tres::poster.wellne: Breathe in. Breathe out. (Optional for you.)
data/story/dna_story.tres::puzzle.alread: The tubes hum contentedly. Nothing left to route.
data/story/dna_story.tres::puzzle.hint::: Every junction flips after a capsule passes. The first capsule only cares about the three junctions on its own path - set those first, then work out the next.
data/story/dna_story.tres::puzzle.intro:: A wall of pneumatic tubes hums and hisses. Eight capsules wait in the intake, each stamped with its destination department.
Seven junctions sit in the lines. Every junction flips after a capsule passes through it. Set the starting position of each, then send them down.
data/story/dna_story.tres::puzzle.solved: Every soul lands in the right department. The tubes cough politely and drop a small, heavy parcel in the tray.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quest.dna_aud: Pass Director Ectomund's quiz and find one hidden stash in the filing mazes. The stashes are tucked in corners nobody visits, which here is all of them.
Audit closed. The auditors have gone home, which for them means back to their desks.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Director Ectomund, Compliance Examiner
Hidden stashes lurk in the filing mazes
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Compliance Audit
Compliance is auditing and Clerk Ledgerbone can't leave the desk. Start with Director Ectomund's quiz. Bring a spare pen.
Pass Director Ectomund's Compliance quiz
Find a hidden stash in the filing mazes
data/story/dna_story.tres::quest.dna_aud: Compliance is auditing, and I need a fresh pair of hands for two things. One: pass Director Ectomund's re-certification quiz. Two: find a hidden stash in the filing mazes.
I can't leave the desk. Policy forbids it, and my legs are on loan to Accounts until further notice.
The quiz is passed and a stash is found, so both boxes are ticked, in ink. Oh. Oh, that's lovely.
A commendation. Do not try to cash it. Accounts enjoys that more than you would.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quest.dna_bac: Three roaming staff, dear, on any floor. Processed, mind, not promoted. I confused the two once, and now he's my supervisor.
The backlog's clear, dear, and it'll be full again by Thursday. Still, it's nice to have a moment, isn't it? I don't get many.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Roaming staff wander every floor
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Clear the Backlog
Agnes Overdue's backlog has gone feral and is wandering the floors. Process three roaming staff members: by duel, per policy.
Duel roaming staff on the D.N.A. floors
data/story/dna_story.tres::quest.dna_bac: Oh good, someone with a pulse. I have a backlog, dear, and this one walks: three staff went feral over a deadline from the new management, and now they wander the floors.
Would you process three of them for me, by duel, on any floor? We're not allowed to raise a hand to colleagues, and you aren't one, dear. You never filled out the form.
Three! That clears the backlog. I couldn't tell you how many forms that closes, dear; I stopped counting in 1987. Here's your bonus.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quest.dna_onb: Punch in at the time clock by the front desk and pour a cup at the coffee machine here, in either order. HR isn't picky. HR is just watching.
You're one of us now, officially. I wouldn't read the contract if I were you. I read it once, and I'm still in line.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: The time clock by the front desk
The breakroom coffee machine
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Mandatory Onboarding
Gerald says every new hire must complete onboarding, starting at the time clock, because HR will know. HR is in the walls.
Punch in at the time clock by the front desk
Pour a cup at the breakroom coffee machine
data/story/dna_story.tres::quest.dna_onb: You're new to the floor, aren't you? Then it's mandatory onboarding: punch in at the time clock by the front desk, and pour a cup from the breakroom machine.
Please don't skip it. HR is in the walls, and these days HR reports to him. I try not to lean on the walls; it feels like oversharing.
Punched in, caffeinated and compliant! That's onboarding done, so here's your welcome kit.
The welcome is the main part of the kit, and I said it as warmly as I could. I've been practising it in the queue for years.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quiz.not_pass: That is not a pass. Study the signs and come back; there is no limit on attempts, and I will be here. I am always here.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quiz.repeat::: Re-certified again. For the paperwork, the Department pays you a small processing fee. It has never paid in that direction before.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quiz.result.0: Zero. That is impressive in its own way, but it earns you nothing.
Try again. The signs aren't going anywhere. Since the transfer, neither is anyone here.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quiz.result.1: One correct, which earns you a token. I have noted your potential in the margin, in very small writing.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quiz.result.2: Two. Half-credit, and half-credit is the highest honour a Necrocrat can hope for.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quiz.result.3: Three correct, one shy of perfect. Take your reward; a perfect score would have made me suspicious.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quiz.result.4: Four correct. Perfect! I have recorded my joy in triplicate, and I must ask you not to make me demonstrate it.
You are now Certified Deceased, Class A. The reward is real; the title is honorary.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.coffee::: For living staff only. Undead: use the Decaf Crypt.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.cubicle_: Please do not personalize your cubicle. Yes, haunting counts.
Hot-desking is permitted. Hot-desking has been banned. See memo.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.elevator: Floors served: Lobby, Records, Quarterly Reviews, Under Renovation.
Form 13-B required. No form, no floor.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.executiv: Staff beyond this point are dead. Executives were dead before it was fashionable.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.exit::1: To {town}. Permit stamped in triplicate by Prudence Pallor. Sunlight not guaranteed. Mind the potholes.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.filing_m: If you are lost, you are in the correct place.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.fun_day:: Attendance is compulsory for all staff, including the undead.
Cake provided. Cake will not be eaten.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.lobby_ma: A Division of Afterlife Services and Labor
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.mailroom: All souls routed by pneumatic tube. Souls routed incorrectly will be re-routed. Eventually.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.main_dun: Where all things are authorized: life, death, resurrection and the afterlife.
Appointment required. Estimated wait: 400 years. Waiting room not included.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.matching: Please do not feed the Top 8.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.now_serv: (Estimated wait for number four: 400 years. The Department of Necrotic Affairs appreciates your patience.)
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.printer:: Out of toner. Out of body. Contact IT (deceased). Please specify which problem.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.puzzle::: Set every junction. Send the souls. Do not send them to Accounts Payable.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.quiz::1: Annual re-certification: 4 questions. Failure is not an option. It is a form.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.filed_co: A complaint, filed in 1873, about the filing system. It is filed under C, for Complaint, and also under F, for Filing, and also under P, for Pending.
The response is filed under R. The response is blank.
data/story/dna_story.tres::shrine.used::: The stamp has been used and the form is complete. Nothing else will be approved today, or any other day.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.requisit: Cards, in triplicate. Souls, in quadruplicate.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.suggesti: All suggestions are read by a committee that has been dead since 1979.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.take_num: Your assigned number is a number. Requests for a better answer require a new number.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.time_clo: (Punching other employees is not covered by your plan.)
