data/story/dna_story.tres::ui.exit.body:: Leaving the D.N.A. ends this visit. Town heals you fully; defeated staff will be back next time. Exit permit 12-X has been auto-approved. This time.
data/story/dna_story.tres::ui.exit.title: Walk back to town?
data/story/dna_story.tres::ui.mini.body:: Three meetings in a row. Your HP carries from one to the next and nothing heals in between. Win all three for a unique Necrocrat card.
data/story/dna_story.tres::ui.mini.body_: You have already earned the unique card here. You can still sit through the meetings for gold and XP. HP carries over; nothing heals in between.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.authoriz: Form 1-A, submitted, reviewed, approved, notarized and filed. Authority over all Necrocrat government is hereby transferred to {villain}.
This transfer is valid. If you disagree, please submit Form 1-B. Form 1-B is available from the person who wrote the transfer.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.new_mana: By order of {villain}, all personnel are required to follow all rules, permits and procedures, including the new ones.
This is not oppression. This is policy.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.permit_t: Standing in a hallway for more than 30 seconds requires a Permit to Stand (Form 7-S).
Form 7-S requires a Permit to Fill in Forms (Form 7-F). Form 7-F requires a signature. The signature requires you to stand still.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.new_rule: Rule 40,001: All rules must be followed.
Rule 40,002: All rules include this rule.
data/story/dna_story.tres::effect.buff.f: Every Necrocrat here is properly stamped, countersigned and notarized. It makes them very hard to argue with.
data/story/dna_story.tres::effect.debuff: Beefcakes do things on the spot, which here requires a permit, in triplicate, and a fee. The fee is also a form.
data/story/dna_story.tres::ui.main.title: The Hall of Final Approvals
data/story/dna_story.tres::ui.main.body:: The Hall of Final Approvals governs life, death, resurrection and the afterlife. Its authority controls the Necrocrats. HP carries in from the zone; only the waiting room heals. Beat Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No, to free the D.N.A.
data/story/dna_story.tres::ui.main.body_: The Hall of Final Approvals is open and, somehow, more efficient. You can still walk the departments for gold and XP. HP carries in from the zone; nothing heals except in the waiting room.
data/story/dna_story.tres::ui.main.butto: Take a number and go in
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: Lovely building. Can't collect a single soul in it, mind. The paperwork won't let me past the lobby, and I've been sat here since the transfer.
I took a number, heh. Makes a change. Usually I'm the one calling them.
What are you writing?
Appointments. Let's see, you're... hm. Not for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-LEDGERBONE.barks:: Form 12-B for purchases. Filled in correctly? Oh. Oh, that's lovely.
The stamp wants a raise. I've given it the form, and it's thinking it over.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-ECTOMUND.barks:: Three hundred years, the same quiz. The answers have never been fresher.
The ethics questions were removed by management. Ethically, I object.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-KYLE.barks::0: is it still '09 out there? no? huh. brb, updating my away message.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-KYLE.barks::1: brb, haunting. been brb since '09. it's a long b.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-GERALD.barks::0: Four million two hundred and twelve. They're on three. Any minute now.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-GERALD.barks::1: Coffee? Nobody here can taste it, but I make it anyway. It's the thought.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-AGNES.barks::0: Employee of the month since 1987, dear. The plaque is getting heavy.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-AGNES.barks::1: Appeal forty thousand and one, denied. I'm starting to take it personally, dear.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-MORTIMER.barks:: Number four million two hundred and fourteen. I have begun to understand Gerald.
I have filed my impatience in triplicate. It is still being processed.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Roaming staff wander every floor
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::s: Gerald is Number 4,000,212 and they are on 3. Thin out the queue to the Waiting Room of Eternity: process two roaming staff.
Duel roaming staff on the D.N.A. floors
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: Number 4,000,212? That's me, and they're on 3. I don't suppose you could help?
The queue for the Waiting Room of Eternity is stuck. If you process two of the roaming staff on the D.N.A. floors, I can get you in. I'll wait. I'm very good at it.
Two roaming staff on the D.N.A. floors, if you can. The queue won't move itself; I've given it a very fair chance.
Two fewer, and the queue moved! Only slightly, but I felt it in my ticket.
The Waiting Room of Eternity will see you now. Do take a number, just not mine. We've been through so much together.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: A single desk under a single green lamp, buried in forms. Betty Bones looks up through cat-eye glasses, very slowly, and sighs the sigh of the long deceased.
'Forms A through F,' she says. 'Then we'll talk. We won't, but still.'
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Betty: Take a number. I won't be calling it. Take it anyway.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Forms A Through F
At half health Betty hands over forms A through F: she gains 2 Contracts and a 1/1 Zombie Temp files in.
Forms A through F. Then we'll talk. We won't, but still.
Betty gains 2 Contracts; a 1/1 Zombie Temp files in.
Out to Lunch
On her 5th turn Betty takes her lunch break: her units stand down (exhausted) for that turn, because nothing gets done on lunch.
Next turn: Betty goes on lunch (her units stand down for a turn).
I'm on lunch, and nothing happens on lunch. That includes me.
Betty is on lunch: her units are exhausted this turn.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Betty stamps one last form with a bony flourish. 'Fine. Number 4,000,212 is approved. Don't make it a thing.'
Far down the line, a ghost with a crumpled ticket begins, very quietly, to cheer.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_lo: You step through the doors and a small grey machine hands you a ticket: 4,000,213. The display above the desk says NOW SERVING: 3.
A clerk looks up, sighs, and says, in a voice like a filing cabinet closing: "The authorization is valid. Please wait."
A cavernous reception hall under a single sign: ALL THINGS REQUIRE AUTHORIZATION. THIS INCLUDES THE SIGN.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_nu: A small silvery ghost is already in the queue, hugging an enormous stack of appeals tied with three kinds of ribbon. "Number 4,000,213. There you are, dear.
Gerald in the breakroom is 4,000,212, so you two will be neighbours. He's a lovely man, and he's been waiting a very long while.
I'm Agnes Overdue. I work the front desk, and on my lunch hour I'm an appellant: forty thousand appeals, every one denied. They've started decorating the stamps.
Follow me; I know where the departments hide. And a word of advice: the authorization is valid. That's what makes it so terrible."
You are number 4,000,213 and they're serving number 3. It's a very long queue, and it's the only way forward.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_in: An intake clerk demands to see your paperwork, and the inspection turns out to be mostly a fight.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_nu: A small silvery ghost waves from the queue, the ribboned stack of appeals under one arm. "Number 4,000,213. I saved your place, dear. Nobody noticed, but then nobody ever does.
Gerald in the breakroom is 4,000,212, so you two will be neighbours. He's a lovely man, and he's been waiting a very long while.
I spent my lunch hour on appeal forty thousand and one, and it came back denied with a very nice stamp. I'm starting to take it personally.
Follow me; I know where the departments hide. And a word of advice: the authorization is valid. That's what makes it so terrible."
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Take-a-Number Kiosk
A small grey machine offers you ticket 4,000,213 while the display above says NOW SERVING 3. A polite ghost behind you coughs, then apologises for coughing.
Take a number and wait
You wait, and then you wait some more, until a vending machine takes pity on you and dispenses one sad cookie.
Take every number
The machine jams, apologises and coughs up coins and a written warning. You are now marked 'Difficult.'
Skip the queue
Nobody dares object, at least not yet, and somewhere down the queue they have started whispering about Number 4,000,213.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_wa: A very comfortable waiting room, whose magazines are 600 years old. Restore HP.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_au: An auditor examines your deck for compliance. Three cards will be weighed on the Scale of Approved Expenditures.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_ma: Souls arrive here by pneumatic tube when nobody knows where else to put them. They are not happy about it.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_lo: A counter piled high with misfiled belongings. A sign: IF YOU FIND SOMETHING, YOU MAY KEEP IT. IF YOU LOSE SOMETHING, SEE A CLERK.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_co: The department that enforces the rules that enforce the rules. Their officer is perfectly polite. (Elite)
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_ap: A judge in an old powdered wig weighs your case. The scales are made of paperwork.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_no: Every important document in the Hall is stamped, signed and witnessed here, the transfer of authority included. The notary is still finding blue-green feathers.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Waiting Room of Eternity
Row after row of chairs stretches into the distance. Can your deck outwait the line?
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_wa: You wait until your legs ache. You check the clock above the door: four minutes.
The clock is lying, and from the look of it, somebody ordered it to.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_co: The officer folds his clipboard and, with a courteous nod, points you toward the Appeals Department.
"You may appeal," he says. "You will lose. But you may appeal."
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_re: The Records Labyrinth is a canyon of filing cabinets that goes down further than it goes up. At its heart, under glass, lies the original transfer: the Necrocrat Path, signed over to {villain}.
It's flawless: submitted, reviewed, approved, notarized and filed, without a single box left empty.
Agnes reads over your shoulder and stops at one clause. Under HEIR OF THE FORMER SOVEREIGN it says: "Deceased (presumed). Remains: not on file."
"Irregular," says Agnes, very quietly, and looks at it for a long time. "A presumed death with no remains on file is an incomplete form.
Someone should look into it, dear, because this form doesn't tell us what happened to the boy."
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: In Triplicate
At half health the Wraith notarizes a Red Tape for itself.
Signed, witnessed and notarized in triplicate. One copy is for you, but you may not keep it.
The Notary Wraith gains a Red Tape.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_fo: Two aisles over, Agnes is filling in a form with a very stubby pencil. "Form 27-C, third attempt. It needs a 27-B, which needs a 27-C.
They keep stamping it DENIED and writing Irregular in the margin. Don't mind me, dear. I've filed worse and kept the receipts."
A counter with a very long sign: FORM 13-B REQUIRES FORM 13-A. FORM 13-A REQUIRES FORM 13-B. PLEASE SEE A CLERK.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_du: Every form here has a twin, and every twin has a twin of its own. The clerks are undead and, understandably, a bit short.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Form 27-B Office
Form 27-B requires Form 27-C, which requires a stamp from the office you are standing in. A clerk slides a pen across the counter without looking up.
Fill out the forms
Everything is in order. A boon is granted and a small tax is levied, in that order, by two different departments.
Forge the stamp
It works, mostly. Something in the ceiling disapproves loudly, with a stapler.
Ask the clerk what Form 27-C is
The clerk looks up for the first time in decades. Nobody has ever asked. She slides you a Pink Slip 'for personal use' and, you swear, winks.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_cl: Undersecretary Vellum squares his papers and does not look up. "Noted. You wish to challenge the transfer of authority.
The authorization remains valid. It was submitted, reviewed, approved, notarized and filed. You may appeal in triplicate."
"Mr. Grimsby has asked me to hold the Court until his schedule opens. I will hold it very, very well. Noted."
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Noted.
At half health Vellum files an objection: he gains a Contract.
Noted. ...Noted?
Vellum gains a Contract.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_cl: The Appeals Court's Undersecretary Vellum, Mortimer's deputy, defends the transfer of authority to the last paragraph. He has never once been thanked. (Elite)
Vellum squares his papers with great care. "Noted," he says, very quietly. "The authorization remains valid."
For the first time, it sounds like a question.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Shredding Room
Rows of paper shredders chew through the day's denied appeals. A sign reads: SHRED ONE THING, RECEIVE ONE THING. Another, in smaller letters, reads: THINGS INCLUDE YOU.
Shred a spare appeal
The shredder hums happily and pays out in coins. It says 'denied' in a voice like a kettle.
Shred your own number
Nothing is left of Number 4,000,213. You feel lighter and slightly nonexistent as the machine files you under 'Resolved.'
Reach in for what it ate
You pull out half of a lost appeal, which is technically a weapon, and the machine takes a bite of you in exchange.
The elevator is hand-cranked by a Beefcake on loan from the wheels. Every floor needs a permit and a rep. Iron turns the crank; Red Tape keeps the doors shut.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_bo: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No, looks up from an endless pile of paperwork, his face as smooth as a blank form and his stamp the size of a tombstone.
"You do not have an appointment. That is irregular. However, the authorization is valid, and under it every visitor is entitled to a hearing.
The answer is no. The question is irrelevant, but you may state your case anyway.
You have, according to the clock, four hundred years."
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Mortim: The answer is no. The question is irrelevant, but you may state your case anyway.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Mortimer Files a Form
On his 4th turn Mortimer files Form 27-B: a 1/1 Filing Clerk is hired to process it.
Next turn: Mortimer files Form 27-B (a clerk is hired).
Your appeal has been received, reviewed and denied. It was a very good appeal.
A 1/1 Filing Clerk is hired.
Filed on a Tuesday
Late in the fight Mortimer finds a note under his own form: FILED ON A TUESDAY. His units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
The authorization is valid. It was filed on a Tuesday. ...We do not file on Tuesdays.
Mortimer hesitates over the form: his units get -1/-0.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_bo: A vast office with a single desk, a single stamp, and one very patient authority.
data/story/dna_story.tres::challenge.ha_: The auditor lays three cards on the Scale of Approved Expenditures. A reasonable total will be stamped. An unreasonable one will be fined.
data/story/dna_story.tres::event.ha_take: You hold ticket 4,000,213. The display says NOW SERVING: 3. The queue snakes through the lobby, up the stairs and out of a window.
A clerk offers you a form, a coffee and a pitying look.
Wait your turn (it will be a while)
You wait for a very long time, until a clerk takes pity and the polite ghost ahead of you shares a biscuit, apologising that it's stale.
You are called in, eventually, rested and a little richer. Waiting, in the Hall, is a kind of work.
The Expedite Fee is an official fee with an official receipt. A tiny clerk stamps your ticket, a door opens, and you feel oddly refreshed.
You cut in line, and forty thousand undead clerks turn to glare. You're processed immediately, and a little roughly.
data/story/dna_story.tres::event.ha_form: Form 13-B
To pass the counter you need Form 13-B. The clerk says Form 13-B requires a Form 13-A, which she will gladly give you, once you have submitted Form 13-B.
Ask for Form 13-A
Pay the clerk 25 gold to look the other way
"Form 13-A," she says. "Certainly. It requires a Form 12-F, which requires a strong cup of tea."
She doesn't look the other way. She looks at the gold, and the gold is accepted.
She stamps something you cannot read, and the way ahead opens.
Form 12-F
Form 12-F is available at the Counter of Form 12-F. The Counter of Form 12-F is closed until Form 13-B has been filed.
Ask for Form 11-D
Argue
"Form 11-D," she says. "A simple form. It requires only your signature, in blood.
Please don't worry, the blood is optional. The signature is not."
You argue until a tiny stamp appears from nowhere and hits you, which hurts a little.
The clerk says: "That was a warning. The authorization is valid."
Form 11-D
Form 11-D is the last form in the chain. It is one line long: "I, the undersigned, request Form 13-B." You sign.
A stamp thunders. Forms 13-B, 13-A and 12-F all appear at once, in perfect order.
Submit all the forms and claim the reward
Rest in the clerk's break room instead
Every form passes. A bureaucrat's tear of joy lands on the ink. You receive a stamped Form 13-B, a small refund and a commendation you cannot read.
The clerk's break room is the most efficient room in the Hall. You are given a cup of tea, a biscuit and a lovely, quiet chair. You feel ready for the next department.
data/story/dna_story.tres::event.ha_nota: A very old notary sits behind a very high counter, a seal in one hand and a very large quill in the other. "Everything in the Hall," he says, "must be notarized.
Lie down in the notary's cot
Sell the notary a spare seal
The seal comes down with a THUMP. You are, officially, a person. Your units feel more legitimate, and hit a little harder for it.
The cot is small, hard and incredibly comfortable. You sleep for a very official ten minutes, and wake refreshed, with the notary's seal printed on one cheek.
He pays in cash, takes no receipt, and tells you he never saw you. You have never felt more notarized.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_bo: The stamp falls from Mortimer's hand, and the paperwork goes still.
At the very bottom of the pile, under every form, every stamp and every signature, is a small note in a trembling hand: FILED ON A TUESDAY.
"...Oh," says Mortimer. "Oh, no. Tuesday is not a business day in this building.
The authorization was valid, and it was always valid. But the office is now vacant, and policy is policy."
data/story/dna_story.tres::cutscene.vaca: The CE-No has been removed from office, and by policy the vacancy passes to the senior-most applicant on file. One moment while I look it up.
...The senior-most applicant is a ghost. It is, for the record, you, Ms. Overdue.
Me? Oh, for pity's sake. I filed more appeals than anyone alive or dead, and this is how they reward it?
I only ever wanted to leave.
The procedure is clear: the office passes to you. You cannot appeal it, Ms. Overdue. I would only have to deny it, and I find I do not want to.
...Then I'll stay, Mortimer, though not for you. I'll stay until nobody has to wait as long as I did.
Everyone in that queue was somebody, and the dead deserve to be treated as people. Helping the lost is the whole job. It always was.
No order outranks that, Mortimer, not his and not yours. From today we treat everyone with respect.
...That is not in the handbook. I find myself wondering why it never was.
Then we'll write a new one. Take a number and wait with the others, Mortimer. You're right behind Gerald, and he'll show you how it's done.
data/story/intro_story.tres::still.appro: You hear the great DENIED stamp crack. For the first time in the Department's long afterlife, it does not come down.
Forms rise around you. Across the Department, a thousand clerks look up from their desks.
Somewhere nearby, you hear a pen stop scratching.
the queue moved. it actually moved. agnes called my number at 3am and i was away from my desk, so she called it again. nobody's ever called me twice.
wanna play one more round before i pass on? kidding. probably.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.quiz.retu: Back again, I see. The ethics questions have been returned to the building, though not yet to the exam. One reform at a time.
Statistically, you will still fail a question, and statistically I will still enjoy it. That is not corruption. That is personality.
data/story/dna_story.tres::hud.objective: The D.N.A., liberated on a technicality: the Lobby and Breakroom are safe. HP does not come back after battles - rest on the Breakroom Couch, or ride up to town.
Leaving the D.N.A. ends this visit. Town heals you fully, and you no longer need an exit permit. Nobody does, though we're all still a little scared of the pen.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.lobby_ma: A Division of Afterlife Services and Labor
Authority Restored (Authorization Revoked on a Technicality)
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.authoriz: Form 1-A has been found to be filed on a Tuesday. Tuesday is not a business day in this building.
The transfer is void. Thank you for your patience. Please ignore the previous notice, the notice before that, and the notice about the notices.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.new_mana: Back from retirement, and delighted to be here. Rules and procedures have been reduced from 40,000 to a more reasonable 39,000.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.permit_t: Standing, sitting and lying down are now permitted. Please choose for yourself. We realise this may take practice.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.now_serv: (The number machine has been switched off. Please just come in.)
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.main_dun: Formerly where all things were authorized. The doors are now open, and the form is optional.
Estimated wait: some minutes. Waiting room included, with magazines.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.dolores.i: I'm head of the whole Department now, and I'm still on the front desk. They gave me a big office, dear, but nobody waits in a big office. They wait here.
Mortimer's in the Waiting Room as number 4,000,214, learning to wait. It's going about as well as you'd expect.
That unfiled form. I kept it in my drawer for ten years, just in case. I think I'll keep it there a little longer. Something tells me it won't be needed.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.dolores.r: The authorization is still valid, dear, but there's a rule above it now: everyone who comes through that door is treated as a person.
Prudence is my deputy. She's much nicer than she used to be, and so, I'm told, am I.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.barnaby.i: Oh, it's you! Gerald, barista, and as of this morning Number 4,000,212: CALLED. I didn't know what to do with my hands, so I made coffee.
Agnes switched the queue machines off and called every number herself, one by one. It took all night. She never sat down.
Have a cup. It's free. The machine is feeling generous, and so am I.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.barnaby.r: No cream and no sugar, I'm afraid. None at all. But hope's back in stock, and I'm trying not to use it all at once.
My number's been called. I'm only here because I like the coffee.
Mortimer's Number 4,000,214 now, and you were 213, right between us. Don't mention it to him, though. He goes very quiet.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.pip.intro: Clerk Ledgerbone, Requisitions. The stamp has stopped haunting the place now that it got its raise.
It doesn't know what to do with itself, and neither do I. Cards, in triplicate, as always.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.pip.retur: Apparently I am allowed to be unbusy now. I keep reaching for the stamp to certify it.
I've been practising. I just stood here for a whole minute and filed nothing at all. It was exhilarating.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.new_rule: Rules 40,001 through 40,003 have been repealed. Please allow a moment for the notices to catch up.
data/story/dna_story.tres::poster.compli: (Freedom is also fine. Choose what you like.)
data/story/dna_story.tres::freed_npc.agn: Agnes Overdue, head of the D.N.A. Yes, me. The office goes to the senior-most applicant, and I filed more appeals than anyone. I have never been so annoyed to win.
I only ever wanted to leave, and I will, soon. But first I'm putting this place right, so nobody else waits as long as I did.
Everyone in that queue was somebody, dear, and the dead deserve to be treated as people. No order outranks that, not his and not anyone's.
And you, dear. You were a number in somebody's file once, weren't you? I can see it in how you hold your shoulders.
Never let anyone file you under 'subject' again.
data/story/dna_story.tres::ruler.statue:: Statue pending approval. Do not look at it until it has been approved.
(Authorization revoked. The statue has been asked to leave. It has taken a number.)
data/story/dna_story.tres::freed_npc.pru: Prudence Pallor, Deputy Head of the Department. Yes, I stamped DENIED on everything. I was tired, the paperwork was valid, and I am sorry.
{villain} did not corrupt us, you know. He used our own rules. Now I stamp APPROVED on things that deserve it.
The stamp is lighter than I remembered. Do you have anything I can approve?
data/story/dna_story.tres::freed_npc.mor: Mortimer Grimsby, formerly CE-No, currently number 4,000,214 in the Waiting Room of Eternity. Gerald was 4,000,212, and he has been very patient with me.
You had 4,000,213, and you did not wait. I keep thinking about that.
I made others wait far longer than you, and every one of them was a person. It is worse, knowing that now.
The authorization was valid. I have begun to wonder whether that was ever the right question.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: Intake's moving again! Agnes waved me straight through. First time in ten years nobody's asked me for Form 27-B, and my appointment book is filling up nicely.
data/story/intro_story.tres::gate.refuse: Archdruid Compostella is herself again, and she hugged me! She smells like rain and a little bit like compost, which is exactly how an Archdruid ought to smell.
Most of the thorns are gone; I keep one in a pot. It's behaving, but I'm not ready to let it meet the curtains.
Fancy a practice round? I'll try very hard not to thorn at you. The raccoons have come to watch, so let's both be on our best behaviour.
A wall of thorns has swallowed the forest path. It looks like it is breathing.
Moss Mulligan lays a hand on the thorns. They sigh, brown, and crumble into leaf mould.
The forest path to the Verdant Dump is open.
data/story/intro_story.tres::refusemance: ...the green is hungry... the green is HUNGRY... nothing goes to waste...
...this path belongs to the Rotheart now... turn back... before the green decides you would make good compost...
...if you won't leave, the green will keep you... it keeps everything now... nothing it holds is ever allowed to go...
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Moss M: ...the green is hungry... stay... stay and be fed...
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Did I Thorn at You?
At half health the real Moss breaks through for a moment: the thorns loosen and you heal 3.
...grow... GROW... (small) Did I thorn at you? I'm sorry, I can't make it stop...
The thorns loosen: you heal 3.
data/story/intro_story.tres::refusemance: Oh no, did I thorn at you? I'm so sorry. The Rot talks very softly in your head, right up until the moment it's doing all the talking.

The Rot took Archdruid Compostella first, down at the Rotheart in the deepest part of the Verdant Dump. Everything grew out from there, and it got into me the day a very tidy lady with shears came calling.
The path's clear now. Go gently in there, and if you meet a raccoon, say hello for me. They're very good boys, whatever anyone tells you.
...the green is patient... nothing ends here any more... come back when you're ready to stay...
...come back... the green can wait... it has forgotten how to do anything else...
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::ZONE_M: Root Cause
A wall of thorns has swallowed the forest path, and the druid guarding it sounds very wrong. Clear the way and find what is making the Dump sick.
Uproot Moss Mulligan at the thorn wall
The thorn wall across the forest path
Walk the forest path into the Verdant Dump
The withered thorn wall on the forest path
Lend a hand: finish a favour in the Verdant Dump
Billie Muckfoot, Granny Gristle or Brother Bramble
Descend into the Rotheart
The way down into the Rotheart, at the bottom of the Dump
The Verdant Dump: the Compost Grange is safe, though the vines keep trying the door. HP does not come back after battles - sit down to a fresh harvest meal, or walk back down to town. The Rotheart festers somewhere to the north.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::ui.m: Three levels down, one after another. Your HP carries from one level to the next and nothing heals in between. Reach the bottom for a unique Refusemancer card.
You already took the unique card from the landfill. You can still dig for gold and XP. HP carries over; nothing heals in between.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::ui.e: Leaving the Verdant Dump ends this visit. Town heals you fully; the roaming golems, scarecrows and gulls (all a little too alive) will be back next time, and so will the garbage.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.m: The way to the Rotheart runs through a tunnel of living roots, and the air down here is warm, wet and humming.
Somewhere underneath you, something very large is breathing slowly, the way a sleeper does when the dream is a bad one.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.h: You eat roast roots and a pie with a crust like a fence post, washed down with a mug that's mostly apple, while a goat watches every bite. HP restored.
Your HP is already full, but Granny Gristle offers you a third helping anyway: one very small turnip.
SCREEEE! A mutant junk gull dive-bombs you and steals your dignity. (-2 HP)
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.w: You wake face-down in a haybale at the Compost Grange. Granny Gristle is leaning on a pitchfork, chewing a stalk of something.
"Went down in the muck, dearie, so we rolled you out. Mucking-out fee is yours, mind. I call it a soil charge. Heh!
The haybale was free, though it's started growing, so best get up before you put down roots."
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.c: You find a treasure chest among the rubbish. For once, sorting pays.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.p: You already took the one lying here. Come back next visit; these days the Dump restocks itself overnight, whether anyone asks it to or not.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.c: The bin burps, steams and hands you a warm Compost Cocktail that smells faintly of promise, and you feel sturdier. (+1 max HP this visit)
The Compost Bin needs two piles of good junk, and you have fewer than two. It sits there, patient and faintly steaming.
The bin has given all the cocktails it can for this visit. Come back next time, once it has had a chance to ferment.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.s: You kneel, and a seed in the shrine splits and blooms. A druid's voice, soft as moss, says: "Grow."
You feel taller. (+1 max HP this visit, and a little healing)
The shrine has blessed you this visit. Give the seed a chance to enjoy being a flower.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.t: The animals fall on the junk, chew it thoughtfully, and spit out a coin. Gold!
The trough is empty and every animal in the pen is staring at you. Bring them a pile of good junk.
The animals are full, and one goat is lying on its back to prove it. Come back next visit.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.c: You need a sack of fertilizer to plant a crop. The soil has standards. Low, fragrant standards.
You plant a crop and pat the soil, which wriggles a little under your hand. Come back in a while and it will be ready.
The crop is still growing. A sprout waves at you, and you leave it to get on with things.
A ripe harvest! Pumpkins, melons, one suspicious turnip.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.h: The goat looks at you, looks at the pen, looks at the sign it was eating, and trots home. Round one: you.
The pig is exactly where you expected, in the only puddle. A little shoving and it waddles home, offended.
The raccoon walks to the pen on its hind legs, tin can held like a briefcase. You appear to be its next appointment.
That one is already back in the pen, sulking. It will get over it eventually.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.b: The vine bridge sways and creaks cheerfully under you, held together by vines, goodwill and a great deal of compost.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.g: The seed cracks. The soil heaves. Green shoots race into the air, twisting and knotting...
It has grown! Already you can't quite picture the spot without it, and the druids look very pleased with themselves.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.c: You climb the beanstalk, hand over hand. The leaves are big enough to sit on. Do not sit on them.
You slide down the beanstalk. Leaf, leaf, leaf, ground. It is faster than the chute and much less dignified.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.m: You swing up onto the saddle. Faster, and it can smash junk barricades. Press Q to dismount.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.d: You hop off and the animal trots back to its stable, snorting.
You can't dismount out here; the scree would eat your boots. Find a flat spot first.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.b: This barricade of junk is far too heavy to push on foot, but something fast and stubborn could charge straight through it.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.s: KA-RASH! Tyres fly, doors fly, and a very surprised hubcap lands in the pen. The way is open.
KA-SPLOOSH! The dam bursts and the recycling stream flows free, along with half a mattress.
You land in a pile of leaves. You decide not to examine the softer bits.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.h: You fall in! Someone fishes you out with a pitchfork and leaves you dripping on dry ground. (-1 HP)
Fell into %s - fished out at the last safe spot, 1 damage to zone HP.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::bark: Mind the edge. The river's lovely to look at and a nightmare to climb out of.
Compost doesn't sort itself. Well, lately it tries, and that's the whole problem.
If a raccoon in a crown asks for your lunch, say no. He'll cry. Still no.
Built these stairs last week, and they've grown two more steps overnight. Same climb, only longer.
The Buffet calls us garbage eaters. Half our garbage is their souffle, barely touched.
The beans came up purple again. I've stopped asking the beans.
Those purple trees were green last spring. Nobody's talking about it.
Stall's open! Patched awnings, patched prices. The holes are free.
Mind the vine ladders in the wind. They hold. Mostly.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::grow: Moss Mulligan hops up from the bank. "You got Billie's herd home? The goat, the pig AND the raccoon? Then the stream owes you a bridge."
She plants her staff in the bank, whispers to it, and the vines begin to climb.
Moss Mulligan tucks her hands behind her back. "Sorry! I only grow bridges for people who have helped the herd, and Billie Muckfoot's animals have got out again.
Round them up for Billie, then come back to me, and I will grow you a way across. No thorns. Promise."
A sprout mound, freshly turned. You press a Magic Bean into the soil and step back.
A sprout mound with a sign: PLANT A MAGIC BEAN HERE. You don't have one, but beans lie around the Dump, one per field each visit.
Another sprout mound. You press a Magic Bean into the soil and step back.
A sprout mound with a sign: PLANT A MAGIC BEAN HERE. You do not have a bean.
A sprout mound at the foot of Mount Scrapmore. You plant a Magic Bean. Something deep in the junk begins to rumble.
A sprout mound at the foot of the junk mountain. It wants a Magic Bean, and you are fresh out.
A sprout mound at the foot of Rust Peak. You plant a Magic Bean and wait, and somewhere above you a hubcap starts to spin.
A sprout mound at the foot of Rust Peak. It wants a Magic Bean. Beans are the currency of the Dump.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::sign: THE COMPOST GRANGE
Hub of the Verdant Dump. The Refusemancers handle waste removal and agriculture.
Nothing goes to waste. Everything, lately, goes to the Rot. Please keep the doors shut.
TODAY'S COMPOST
- Waste removal (by goat)
- Agriculture (by magic)
- Nothing goes to waste. Not even the menu.
- Do not water anything. It is already awake.
THE FOREST PATH
To {town}, past Moss Mulligan's thorn wall. Sort your boots. Check for vines; they will claim to be laces.
THE HARVEST MEAL
Sit. Eat. Do not ask where the carrots were last Tuesday.
GRANNY GRISTLE'S SWAP SHED
One person's trash is another person's starting hand. Please shuffle outdoors.
THE COMPOST BIN
Two piles of good junk make one Compost Cocktail.
Do not drink the compost. Do drink the Cocktail.
THE DRUID SHRINE
Kneel. Be blessed. Do not step on the seedlings. They are listening.
FEEDING TROUGH
Please do not feed the goats (they will eat the sign).
A pile of good junk, however, is welcome.
BORIS THE GIANT BOAR
Fast, loyal and entirely unbothered by fences. They bother him once, briefly.
Ride him. Dismount with Q.
THE REFUSEMANCER'S OATH
We are the Refusemancers, druids of the kingdom.
We summon animals to eat its garbage and turn it into fertilizer.
We use our magic to help the crops grow. Nothing goes to waste.
THE PATCHWORK FIELDS
Every patch grows something different. Every patch is fertilized by the same goat.
PLANT A CROP
A sack of fertilizer and a little time make a harvest, ready before you leave. It grows faster if nobody stares at it.
THE APPLIANCE GROVE
A druid circle of old fridges and washing machines. The spirits of dishwashers are strong here.
Druid Thistlewick keeps the Dump's questions.
THE COUNTY FAIR GROUNDS
Blue ribbons for the best pumpkin, the best pie and the best pile.
Judge: Recycle Rhonda. Do not argue with the judge.
SORT IT OUT! - TODAY ONLY
Compost, metal, glass or paper. Twenty pieces, one conveyor.
The belt does not slow down for anyone. It has been asked.
MOUNT SCRAPMORE
A junk mountain, overgrown with moss and ambition.
Plant a bean at the mound to climb. Slide down the chute to leave.
BEANSTALK RULES
1. Plant bean.
2. Wait.
3. Climb. Do not look down, do not look up, do not look at the cow.
THE RECYCLING STREAM
Everything the kingdom threw away ends up here, rinsed.
Crossing: vine bridges only.
WARNING: STREAM
Do not swim, wade or ask what is in it.
If you fall in, somebody will fish you out. It costs 1 HP.
WEST BRIDGE
Not grown yet? Plant a Magic Bean at the mound beside it.
CENTRE BRIDGE
Moss Mulligan grows this one for anyone who helps Billie Muckfoot round up the herd.
EAST BRIDGE
Not grown yet? Plant a Magic Bean at the mound beside it.
THE NORTH BANK
Welcome to the far side. The wall of tyres ahead has three gaps. One has been plugged with junk.
THE JUNK DAM
Somebody has dumped half a landfill across the feeder channel.
Needs a charging mount. Brother Bramble will pay.
GIDEON THE GIANT GOAT
Eats anything. Climbs anything. Rams anything.
Do not feed him the sign.
JUNK BARRICADE
A pile of tyres, doors and one very stubborn wardrobe across the gap.
The Landfill Depths are beyond. Bring something that charges.
RUST PEAK YARDS
The finest rust in the kingdom. Small batch. Very slow finish.
THE LANDFILL DEPTHS
Three levels. Mandatory. Bring a nose peg.
Do not dig deeper than the raccoons. They will consider it competitive.
THE ROTHEART
The source of the sickness. Do not enter. Do not breathe deeply. Do not lick anything.
The deeper you go, the more it grows.
NOTE FROM A DRUID
The door is warm because something behind it is thriving, very hard, and lately it seems to be thriving in our direction. Please don't open it.
THE SEED SHRINE
Plant a seed in a plot and it flips that plot and its four neighbours.
Bring every plot into bloom to wake the great beanstalk.
THE SCREE FIELDS
Loose rubble, jagged tin and thistles. Impassable on foot.
Mounts only. Boots are not covered.
SCREE RULES
No walking. No dismounting. No dropping your lunch.
The scree will find it.
TODAY'S JUNK
Tyres, fridges, one (1) piano.
Nothing goes to waste. Everything goes to the Dump.
NOTE
Good stuff in the hollow log. If you can read this, kindly take one step back from my retirement.
- a raccoon
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::enem: A trash golem towers over you, moss coating its fridge body and shoots sprouting from its ears. Inside, the little light is still on.
A scarecrow druid faces you with a cabbage growing where its heart should be. There isn't a crow in sight; the garden has bigger problems now.
Four junk gulls guard a stolen can, shrieking over its crop of mushrooms. You have interrupted a very small turf war.
Welcome to the Compost Grange. I'm Brother Bramble, Warden of the Stream. Would you close the door behind you, and lock it, and maybe check the window? The vines keep trying it.

We're the Refusemancers, druids of waste removal and agriculture: our animals turn the kingdom's garbage into fertilizer for its crops. The Buffet calls us garbage eaters, and then they eat our carrots.
Our magic runs through nature itself, and {villain} turned it against us. Our Archdruid, Compostella, went down to tend the deep roots and never came back up, and nothing has been right since.
Now nothing rots, so nothing feeds the soil. Everything is too alive and the whole Dump is sick with growing, and on top of all that, SOMEBODY has eaten the compost AGAIN.
Back at the Grange? Do sort your boots at the door - compost, metal, glass, paper - and check them for tendrils. We have quite enough houseplants already.
The Archdruid planted a tree for every royal birthday, and there's a row of them past the stream. Eleven trees, and then nothing.
I water the twelfth spot anyway. I couldn't tell you why, except that it feels as if somebody is still coming.
Not long ago, somebody carried a sleeping young man through these woods in the dead of night. He was glowing faintly, in four colours. I've never seen anything like it.
The raccoons saw it too. Raccoons see everything; they just won't tell you about it.
Granny Gristle, junk-trader! Born in a haybale, raised in a barn and retired to a shed, and this is the shed. It's started growing, mind. There's a window in the back I never put in. Heh!
Everything here's Refusemancer-issue: grown, composted and well rinsed. Found, not stolen, dearie. The raccoon found it, and I just held on to it very tightly.
Cards grown strong and rinsed clean, with a faint smell of earth. Hear them humming? Well, I never promised you a silent auction. Heh!
Back again, dearie! Turnips are a day old. A lovely vintage, if you're a turnip.
The turnips are looking at me again. I like a root vegetable that minds its own business, I do. Heh!
Oh good, a pair of legs! I'm Billie Muckfoot, animal handler, and I speak fluent goat, which is mostly screaming. Lately the screaming's about the plants: the fields keep trying to eat my herd.
The boar and goat in the stables will carry you. Ask nicely or ask rudely; they ignore both the same. Good, sensible animals.
Any luck with the herd? Look for the goat first; it'll be eating something it shouldn't. If the something is eating it back, shout for me.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Escaped animals graze out in the fields
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Round Up the Herd
Three of Billie Muckfoot's animals got out: a goat, a pig and a raccoon with a briefcase. Shoo each one back to the pen before the Rot gets them.
Shoo escaped animals back to the pen
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::ques: Three of my animals got out: a goat, a pig and a raccoon with a briefcase. The Rot's in the fields and they're wandering right into it.
Find each one out in the Dump and get it back to the pen before dark. Don't chase them. Walk up firmly and make eye contact.
Animals respect eye contact. Raccoons consider it the start of negotiations.
Three escapees, all out in the fields: the goat's eating something, the pig's found a puddle, and the raccoon is probably writing me a strongly worded letter.
All three home, and the pen's never looked so full! Here, you've earned this.
A goat card. You can play this one without having to catch it afterwards.
The herd's home and already plotting the next escape. Thank you! Moss Mulligan will grow you a crossing at the centre bridge now. Tell her I sent you.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Try the fields, the east edge and across the stream
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Fertilizer Run
Granny Gristle is out of fertilizer and the crops are sulking. Gather three sacks from around the Dump, and hold your nose while you do.
Gather fertilizer sacks around the Dump
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::ques: Now then, fertilizer. The crops are sulking and the soil's gone strange, and good clean fertilizer is the one thing the Rot can't grow in.
I need three sacks from around the Dump, lying wherever the animals left them. Don't ask me how they got bagged up, dearie. I never have. Heh!
Three sacks of fertilizer, dearie. Try the fields, the east edge and the far side of the stream. Follow your nose. Then apologise to it.
Three whole sacks! The crops'll be singing by morning, and I mean that more than I'd like to.
Here's your reward. Found, not stolen, and only a little bit damp. Heh!
The fields are fed, dearie. Plant your own with a sack of fertilizer and a little patience. I'd sell you the patience too, but nobody ever stays long enough to buy it. Heh!
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: The stables: borrow a mount, then charge the dam
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Unblock the Stream
Somebody dumped a junk dam across the feeder channel on the north bank. Borrow a mount from the stables and charge it. Brother Bramble's compost boots are the prize.
Ride a mount into the junk dam on the north bank
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::ques: Somebody has dumped a dam of junk across the feeder channel on the north bank, and the stream can't breathe. Borrow a mount from the stables and charge it, and my compost boots are yours.
It's the junk dam on the north bank. Take Gideon the goat from the north stable and charge it at full tilt. He's never slowed down for anything, and I'd hate for him to start now.
The stream's flowing again, practically dancing! Here are the compost boots, still warm. They squelch, but it's a proud sort of squelch.
The stream's clear, for now. The kingdom will have it full again by the end of the week, but that's what we're here for.
Ah, a visitor. I am Druid Thistlewick, Keeper of the Dump's Questions, and I have sat in this ring of old appliances for forty years.
The dishwasher and I have an understanding, though lately it has started talking back. Forty years, and NOW it wants to clear the air.
Four questions about the Refusemancers, their work and their oath. Every answer is written on a sign somewhere in the Verdant Dump.
Sort your thoughts as you would your bins: compost, recycling, regret. Answer well and there is gold and seed in it for you; answer poorly and you will receive a gentle, rustling sigh.
Back to improve your score? Good. A druid is just a student who never left the garden.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::quiz: Zero. We have found room for growth, rather a lot of it, I'm afraid. No reward this time.
The signs are patient. I am slightly less so. The dishwasher is not patient at all.
One. A single seed, but every garden starts with one. Plant it, water it, and try again.
Two. Half-grown. Keep tending those thoughts; we are not harvesting excuses.
Three! Nearly in bloom. Take your reward and a sprig of mint.
FOUR! A perfect harvest! You may now call yourself a Certified Refusemancer, First Class.
Your reward is real. The certificate is compostable. When you tire of showing it off, let it become something humble.
Another round! The Dump pays a small fee for repeat scholarship.
Not a pass. Walk the Verdant Dump, read the signs, and come back. There is no limit on attempts.
Step RIGHT up to the County Fair's own SORT IT OUT! I'm Recycle Rhonda: fair judge, pie inspector, and the finest dumpster-diver in three counties!
I was the voice of Captain Compost Badger and his Sorting Squad at every harvest puppet show for twenty years! Nobody knew! All that fame went to a badger in a cape!
The Rot cancelled the pumpkin contest. It can't cancel ME! Today's show: twenty pieces of junk, one conveyor, four bins. Compost, metal, glass or paper!
Send each piece to the right bin before it falls off the end. Rewards by performance, plus a first-time bonus. Gloves on!
Back for another run, champ? The conveyor's hungry, the bins are ready, and I've got pie for afterwards!
Remember: one person's trash is another person's blue ribbon. Sort fast. Sort true. Sort with a smile!
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::sort: Twenty pieces of junk ride the conveyor. Send the front piece to the right bin (click a bin, or keys 1-4 or the arrow keys) before it reaches the end. A wrong bin or a miss breaks your streak. A long streak scores more.
Feel the rhythm of the belt!
Compost left, metal down, glass up, paper right!
No hesitation! Give that rubbish somewhere to be!
BLUE RIBBON sorting! Reduce! Reuse! Refuse to quit! All three goats in the crowd are cheering. Or hungry.
Your very first run at the fair! Here's your first-timer's bonus, no strings attached: a jar of compost salve!
Rub it in, champ! The salve, I mean, not the victory. Nobody loves a gloater!
Not quite a run, champ. That's fine. The belt isn't going anywhere.
Unlike the jam jar. The jam jar went everywhere.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::grow: Twenty-five plots of garden sit in a five-by-five square, some bare and some in bloom. Plant a seed in a plot and that plot and its four neighbours flip between bare and bloom. Bring every plot into bloom to wake the great beanstalk.
Work from the top row down: if the plot above a bare plot is bare, plant right below it. Then fix the last row with the first row. Count your seeds; there are only four solutions.
Every plot blooms at once. The beanstalk rises, shakes out a seed pouch the size of a satchel, and hands it down with a leaf. It is still warm.
The garden is in full bloom. Nothing left to plant.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::sign: WARNING: THE ROT
Plants here are unnaturally alive. Fungi mutate. Roots invade structures, hands, and lunch.
Do not feed anything. Do not name anything. Do not turn your back on the zucchini.
THE CORRUPTION SPREADS FROM THE NORTH
Whatever our Archdruid has become, it is feeding the whole Dump.
Follow the dying fields. Then follow the living ones. They are worse.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::effe: The Dump is alive in all the wrong ways, but its own druids know how to make the best of it.
Everything delicate rots fast in the Dump. Gourmand food does not keep. Gourmand golems keep even less.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::ui.m: At the Rotheart, the Archdruid is joined to the Dump through its corrupted roots. HP carries in from the zone; only clean soil heals you. Beat the Archdruid to free the Verdant Dump.
The Rotheart is silent, and the roots are only roots. You can still wander the tunnels for gold and XP. HP carries in from the zone; nothing heals except on the clean soil.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: Nothing's died in this valley in ten years, not so much as a beetle or a leaf. Unnatural, that.
Gives a fellow a lot of free time. I've taken up knitting. Heh.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-GRISTLE.barks::0: Found, not stolen, dearie! The raccoon found it. I just held on tight. Heh!
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-GRISTLE.barks::1: Shed grew another room, dearie. At last, a growing business I don't have to water. Heh!
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-THISTLEWICK.bar: Every thought has a bin. Most of mine go in compost. That is not a complaint.
The dishwasher talks back. I listen. Wisdom sometimes arrives with a rinse cycle.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-RHONDA.barks::0: Reduce! Reuse! And rinse your jars, folks - a sticky jar is a sad jar!
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-RHONDA.barks::1: Captain Compost Badger says: rinse first! ...Who says I do the voice?
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-BRAMBLE.barks::: The vines have started whispering. Also, SOMEBODY ate the compost AGAIN.
Eleven little trees in a row, one per birthday. Then nobody came for the twelfth.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-COMPOSTELLA.bar: Everything goes back to the soil in the end, child. That's what lets it grow.
About the barn, child... I'll help mend it. The goat would rather I started elsewhere.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Scavengers prowl the junk heaps
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::s: Little paw prints, a tiny crown, and no compost. Drive off two scavengers to follow the trail.
Drive off scavengers in the Dump
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: SOMEBODY has been eating ALL the compost. There are little paw prints everywhere, and next to the bin I found... a tiny crown.
Chase off two of the scavengers in the Dump and their trail should lead you to the big dumpster. Gently, please - they're only hungry. And GUILTY.
Two scavengers out in the Dump, please. Follow the fresh paw prints; it's a trail of evidence with TERRIBLE table manners.
The paw prints lead to the big dumpster. I knew it. I KNEW it.
Under the tipped-over dumpster there's a gate made from an old bicycle wheel, and that's the way to the Trash Panda Throne. Do bring a peg for your nose.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Courtier collects the crusts the kingdom leaves behind and serves them back, warmed, as a royal tasting menu.
The Throne of Lids creaks. On it sits a very large raccoon in a very small crown, sweating profusely.
'WE DID NOT EAT THE COMPOST. We... sampled it.' His Majesty grips the throne. 'The royal tasting is not open to questions.'
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::His Ma: Sovereign of the Throne of Lids
Kneel before the Throne of Lids. Or crouch. Crouching is also acceptable.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: The Royal Bins
At half health the royal guard of bins rallies: a 1/1 Rat joins and he gains a Garbage.
WE DID NOT EAT THE COMPOST. We... audited it. Orally. GUARDS!
A 1/1 Rat joins; His Majesty gains a Garbage.
Sweating Profusely
Near the end His Majesty starts to sweat: his units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
We were only testing the compost on the realm's behalf. Very thoroughly. ...Is it warm in here? It is very warm in here.
His Majesty's units get -1/-0.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: His Majesty abdicates with great dignity and a crust of pizza. The crown rolls under the throne.
'Compost is for the kingdom,' he says. 'We are the kingdom. We fail to see the problem. Do not point at the crumbs.'
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::dung: The vines part for you slowly, and it doesn't feel like being let in. It feels like being drawn deeper.
Behind you, the gate closes with a soft, wet sound. Somewhere ahead, something very large breathes in, and the whole tunnel breathes with it.
The Withered Gate
A cracked archway wrapped in black-green vines that tighten a little as you pass beneath them.
The Overgrown Outskirts
Ordinary plants at first glance, only a shade too green, and every leaf turns very slightly to follow you.
The Mutant Grove
Mushrooms the size of garden sheds crowd the path, and a few of them tilt their caps to watch you go by.
The Whispering Mushrooms
A ring of pale mushrooms murmurs as you pass. They seem to know your name, though they can't think how.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Strangled Greenhouse
The vines are choosing who gets through, and they're reading your deck very closely before they decide.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cli: Roots as thick as a cart grip the mill wheel. Someone has trimmed them, very neatly, into the shape of a smiling man in a circlet.
Do mind the topiary, dear. That's His Perfection, seen from the left - the right side is still filling in.
Hortensia Clipwell, Royal Groundskeeper. I'm the one who outlawed composting. All that rot lying about in heaps, being honest with everybody - so untidy.
Nothing rots down here any more, and the whole place feels wrong for it.
Isn't it lovely? I brought the Archdruid a little seed as a gift - life that never ends. She was so very sad, and now nothing ever has to go.
And now, dear, I'm afraid I have a weed to remove.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Horten: Such a pretty little weed, and such a shame. Do hold still, dear, this won't take a moment.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Regulation Topiary
At half health Clipwell trims two topiaries into guards: two 1/1 Topiaries join her (Prize Topiary makes them 2/2).
Gentlemen, if you would? He's grown well over regulation height.
Two Topiaries join Clipwell.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cli: Well. You've made a dreadful mess of my hedges, and I shall be sending a note.
She opens a wide green umbrella, steps neatly over the roots and walks away up the ravine toward the Capital road, not one hair out of place.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::dung: Nothing here has rotted in ten years. The pool is full of leaves that stay green, fruit that never softens, and a smell like a held breath.
Brother Bramble's notes are pinned to a root in a worried hand: 'Nothing rots, so nothing feeds the soil, and the soil is STARVING.'
Underneath, pressed much harder: 'Everything down here is far TOO alive. And WHO has been eating the COMPOST?'
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Weeping Compost Pool
The pool is the colour of a bruise, and it's sobbing very quietly around a boot that bobs in the middle of it.
Drink from the pool
It tastes of rain and old boots. You feel hardier, and a little poisoned.
Bottle some of it
Somebody will pay good gold for a bottle of this. Down here, that somebody is usually a hedgehog.
Comfort the pool
You tell it that it's doing very well. It sobs harder, then gives you a very old Mulch Mole it was keeping safe, along with a little of its warmth.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::dung: A Patch of Clean Soil
One small patch of the ordinary, honest dirt the Refusemancers love. Restore HP.
The Spore Gauntlet
A tunnel of drifting spores. A well-built deck walks straight through, but a loose one starts to sprout.
The Strangler Thicket
A tangle of vines that remembers the shape of everything that has ever walked through it.
The Seed Vault
The Refusemancers' seed bank, long since overrun. Some of the seeds are still good, and some of them have opinions.
The Rootbound Golem
A golem with a ribcage of roots and a head of moss. The whole tunnel is part of its body. (Elite)
The Root Tunnels
The roots have grown into the walls, the ceiling, the floor. Whatever lives here has eaten the light.
The Pulsing Wall
The wall pulses with warm, wet light. It is not entirely a wall.
The Heartwood Treant
The oldest tree in the Dump, grown into the Rotheart. It doesn't recognize you, or anything else, any more. (Elite)
You sit on the clean soil and breathe. A thread of clear water runs through it, the only clean water you have seen down here.
It smells of rain and old compost, and somewhere beneath you a worm is working through the loose soil. Your shoulders drop for the first time in hours.
The golem folds back into the floor, and the tunnel ahead turns smoother and warmer, with a pulse running through it.
You can hear it now: a vast, slow heartbeat, shaking the walls.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The mutant bees have learned farming. What the rot throws away they turn into honey, and what they make they feed back to the rot.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: The Hive Swarms
When two of its units have died, the hive swarms: two 1/1 Mutant Bees with Flying buzz in.
BZZZZZZZ.
Two 1/1 flying Mutant Bees buzz in.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Something lifts in the Rot Tunnel. Every scrap of Garbage it finds becomes a rep, and every rep becomes Iron.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::dung: Every tendril in the Dump runs to this one place. At its center, wrapped in roots and humming, hangs a seed the size of a fist.
A tag hangs from it in very tidy handwriting: PROPERTY OF THE PATH-OLOGISTS - LIFE THAT NEVER DIES.
The tendrils feed on the seed, and the seed feeds on grief. Cut them, and the Rotheart will weaken.
But the seed won't let go of her, and she won't let go of it.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Heart Roots
Thick, pulsing roots run from every wall into the chamber beyond: the Rotheart's lifelines. You could cut them, and it would hurt her far more than you.
Sever the Heart Roots
The roots shriek and let go. Whatever waits ahead will be weaker for it.
Leave them be
The roots keep pulsing, and the Rotheart keeps its strength.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::dung: At the heart of the Rotheart stands Archdruid Compostella, half woman and half tree. Roots run from her arms into the floor and out into every plant in the Dump.
Her eyes are open, but whatever is looking out of them isn't her.
"I... am... THE... DUMP," she says in many voices at once, grieving and furious. "I am WHAT YOU THROW AWAY... I am what GROWS BACK... and I am HUNGRY."
Beneath the many voices, one small one: "Please. The tree. I could not let her go."
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Compos: I AM what you throw away... I AM what grows back... and I am so... HUNGRY...
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: The Roots Spread
At half health the roots spread: two 1/1 Sporelings sprout and her units get +0/+1.
...I am the bin you never empty... nothing leaves... I am HUNGRY...
Two Sporelings sprout; her units get +0/+1.
Please. The Tree.
Near the end a small voice breaks through: her units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
(small) Please. The tree. I could not let her go.
The hungry green falters: her units get -1/-0.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::dung: The Rotheart
The corrupted core of the Verdant Dump: a vast, throbbing knot of root and rot, and, at its center, a figure that was once the Archdruid.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::chal: Five cards drift through the spores. If enough of them are infrastructure they'll hold you steady; if not, the spores will settle sweetly in your lungs.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::even: The Whispering Mushrooms
A ring of pale mushrooms murmurs as you pass. "Stay," they say in a thousand tiny voices, "and eat."
"Listen," they add, softer. "Join us."
Taste a cap
Listen to what they have to say
Pick a few and sell them
It tastes like rain, soil and tiny, tiny regrets. You feel strangely rested, and your tongue is a little bit blue.
They tell you where the roots run, where the Rot wears thin and where the Archdruid used to walk, and you hold on to as much as you can.
It helps, though some of what you now know doesn't feel like your own thought.
The mushrooms scream very quietly as you pick them, and you pretend not to hear. A passing trader is delighted and pays well.
The Pulsing Wall
The wall ahead pulses with a slow, wet heartbeat, and warm light leaks through a seam down its middle.
A voice inside says: "Come. Be held."
Press your hands into the wall
Wait beside it and breathe
Cut a piece of it free
The wall takes your hands, warm and wet. It hurts for a moment, and then it doesn't.
Fine roots creep along your arms and then let go, and oddly you feel steadier on your feet than you have in days.
You breathe in time with the wall, and it quiets. A small bit of warmth moves from the roots into you. You feel mended, and a little ashamed.
It bleeds sap and fury, and a glittering stone drops out of the cut. It'll fetch good gold, though it costs you a long scrape down one arm.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::dung: The Archdruid sinks to her knees. The Rotheart lets out a long, shuddering breath, and across the whole Dump a thousand vines unclench.
Overhead the vines settle, and for a moment nothing moves beneath your feet.
"...What a terrible dream," Compostella whispers. "The seed is still in my roots, child. It won't die, and I can't make it."
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::cuts: It's the seed, {villain}'s gift - life that never dies. I grew up beneath a great tree, child, and when she fell, I couldn't bear it.
I planted the seed where she had stood, and it took. It's been feeding on my grief for ten years. Nothing here rots, and that's my doing.
Something that can never die isn't a gift. It's a grief that never gets to end. Let it rot.
Everything I ever loved, I gave back to the soil when its time came. Everything except her.
...Then we let it die, together. Hold on to me while it goes.
I have never let go of anything so large.
...It's rotting. Honest compost, the first in ten years. Oh, I can hear the soil again.
I can hear the stream. I can hear the goat.
And I can hear her, a little, in all of it. She did not go away. She went into everything.
To grow, I had to let her go. ...I think she has been waiting ten years for me to say so.
data/story/intro_story.tres::still.rothe: Light pours through the splitting Rotheart.
Before you, the purple vines wither. At the heart of the wound, the Archdruid kneels, free and breathing.
Wildflowers follow the light outward, field by field, through the Dump.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::bark: River's still lovely, and still a nightmare to climb out of. Healing only goes so far.
Compost's rotting down the normal way again - slowly, with help, the way it should.
The raccoon in the crown says thank you. He'd also like your lunch. I've told him no.
Same climb as ever, but the view's worth stopping for now.
Every terrace is a little greener now, and the top one most of all.
Archdruid's back on her rounds. Waters the weeds too - says they've had a hard ten years.
Trees went back to their proper green overnight. Folk keep stopping just to look.
Stall's open! Patched awnings, honest prices, and nothing purple unless you ask for it.
Funny thing - the flowers smell like flowers again. I'd forgotten they had a smell.
The Verdant Dump, healing: the Compost Grange is safe. HP does not come back after battles - sit down to a fresh harvest meal, or walk back down to town.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::ui.e: Leaving the Verdant Dump ends this visit. Town heals you fully; the roaming golems, scarecrows and gulls have calmed down a lot, and so has the garbage.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::sign: THE COMPOST GRANGE
Hub of the Verdant Dump. The Refusemancers handle waste removal and agriculture.
Nothing goes to waste. The Rot is gone, and the doors may be opened again.
TODAY'S COMPOST
- Waste removal (by goat)
- Agriculture (by magic)
- Nothing goes to waste. Not even the menu.
- Water the plants. They're only plants again, and they like it.
THE ROT: CURED
The plants here are only naturally alive, mostly. The zucchini has been spoken to.
THE ARCHDRUID IS BACK
Archdruid Compostella is recovering. She asks that you not call her "the Rotheart Archdruid" at breakfast.
THE FOREST PATH
To {town}. Moss Mulligan's thorn wall is mulch now, and she says sorry again. The vines are just vines, but please still sort your boots.
THE ROTHEART
Source of the sickness, now closed for healing. The vines are only vines (mostly), and visitors are welcome.
NOTE FROM A DRUID
The door is warm because the compost is happy. The compost was always happy. We just forgot what that looked like.
I never thought I'd get to say it, but the Dump is healing. The vines are only vines, the mushrooms are only mushrooms, and the Archdruid is herself again. She's terribly embarrassed.
Go on, breathe in. You can breathe deeply down here now, and that smell is HONEST COMPOST. Isn't it wonderful?
This morning Compostella walked straight to the row of royal trees and planted a twelfth. She didn't say why, and I didn't like to ask.
She only smiled at you on her way past. I've been wondering about that all morning.
The stream's clean, the fields are calm and the zucchini has gone back to being a zucchini. We owe you a great deal more than compost.
Though NOBODY has explained who ate the compost. The raccoons have suddenly become excellent listeners.
Granny Gristle, junk-trader, back in business! The shed's just a shed again, dearie, and the turnips are only turnips.
I had a little cry, then I went and planted a whole field. Shop's open, dearie, and every bit of it was thrown out by somebody who was wrong. Heh!
Day-old turnips, dearie, and not one of them looking at anybody. Finally, produce with manners. Heh!
Billie Muckfoot, animal handler! The whole herd's home, and the goat's already eating a sign.
And the sign isn't eating him back this time. I've never been so happy to watch a goat ruin something.
Every animal's home and not one of them mutated. I could cry, honestly, and I might.
Into a bucket, though. The plants could use it.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::free: Archdruid Compostella, child, and yes, I've been told about the barn. I don't remember doing it, but I gather the barn remembers me, so I'll be helping to put it right.
The Rot sat in my roots for ten years and spoke so quietly. It told me I was needed, and that the whole world was waiting on me to grow.
It was my own grief all along, dressed up as a seed. Thank you for helping me let it rot.
The Dump will heal, though the goat may take a little longer to trust me. Plant something, child. Anything at all. It'll be glad of you.
You're carrying a loss you can't name yet, child. When you find its name, don't shut it away in a jar the way I did. Death is not the end of them.
Let it be the start of something in you.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::rule: It looks like the Archdruid, and it's still growing. Please do not water it.
This used to be the Rot-Idol. It's only topiary now, but please still do not water it.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cli: The Groundskeeper's gone. She packed her shears and left for the Capital the very moment the Archdruid woke.
She left one pair behind in a compost heap, and Granny Gristle has kept them. 'Found, not stolen,' she told me, twice, before I'd even asked.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: Hear that? Things rotting properly again. Lovely sound, that - it means something's about to grow.
data/story/intro_story.tres::zone.comple: Chancellor Clench is down, Grandmaster Flex is back, and the weights are in the gym. The mills turn at a sensible pace; Gary lifts with a spotter.
The Doppelganger is exposed, the Special Sauce is recalled, and the real Grand Chef is back in her own kitchen with the golems guarding plates again. Nobody leaves hungry.

Mortimer Grimsby is removed from office, and the vacancy passes by policy to the senior-most applicant on file: Agnes Overdue. The Department of Necrotic Affairs belongs to itself again, and it is terrified by the freedom.
The Rotheart has gone silent and the vines are only vines again. The Archdruid is herself once more, deeply apologetic about the barn, and slowly the land begins to heal.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: The intake's open again, did you hear? Busy week. Gerald's number finally came up, lovely chap, and he brought his own mug for the journey.
Agnes stayed on, of course. Somebody has to fix the forms, and I've pencilled her in for later. Much later. Heh.
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::_fragm: Every zone you free seems to shake something loose in your memory. Each time it happens, go and tell Elder Maren; she'll want to hear it.
%s: free a zone, then see Elder Maren
Elder Maren's home, up the Gate Road from Crosspath's square
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-HOB.barks::0: Checked my book. You're not in it, not for a good long while. Heh.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-HOB.barks::1: Business has been ever so slow these ten years. Paperwork, not me. Heh.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.1.in: You've gone pale as flour. Sit down, sit. Something's come back to you, hasn't it?
Tell me all of it, however small it seems. The small things are usually the ones that matter.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.1.fr: There's light, four colors of it, warm as bathwater, spilling across a ceiling I can't quite see.
A woman is humming a tune with no words, and it rises and falls like someone breathing in their sleep.
A hand rests on my head, gentle and certain, and it smells of lavender and woodsmoke.
Then the light thins, like breath on glass, and I am back.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.1.af: ...A lullaby. That tune is from the old days, from the court, and there are very few left who remember it. Fewer still who'd hum it.
Have some pie. And don't ask me why my eyes are wet, because I won't tell you.
And look at you. With one zone free, the corruption's grip on the land is slipping, and it's slipping off you along with it.
You ought to be able to carry a second Path now. Go to the Deck Station and try building a deck with two; I'd like to hear how it feels.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.1.an: With the first zone free, the corruption smothering your gift has weakened. Your decks may now use two Paths, and dual-Path cards can finally be played.
Decks may now use two Paths.
One zone free and you're back for pie already. Fine, but it's one slice per zone from now on, dearie. I've just made that rule.
Three roads are still shut. I'd see to them myself, dearie, but at my pace I'd arrive next spring.
The square sang last night, and badly. It was the best thing I've heard in ten years, so don't you dare tell them.
One zone free. Hm. And the old cottage at the end of Champions' Road has started cheering at night, from somewhere down in the cellar. I've decided not to ask.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cav: Someone is sitting on a rock at the mouth of the Forgotten Cave, hood up, sharpening a pencil with a scalpel.
You freed a whole Path on your own, with a deck you've only had for a week.
Let me see your hands. Steadier than they were. Good. That's the first thing I've been able to tick off my list in a long time.
Who are you?
A friend. That's still all I can tell you, and I'm sorry it isn't more.
I'm not coming into town. The old woman with the shell looks at me like I owe her something, and she's probably right.
Keep going. I'll know when the next one falls, because the woods go quiet whenever a Path comes loose.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.2.in: Another one, is it? Don't hide behind your teacup, dearie. Just say it.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.2.fr: White rooms, and a white light that never changes, whatever the hour.
Glass on every side, and faces behind it in white coats, taking notes.
No one there ever uses my name. They call me 'the Subject', and whatever I do, they only say 'again.'
I wasn't lost. I was kept.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.2.af: Glass, and white coats, and 'again.' So that's where you've been all this time.
You've earned some truth from me, so here's the first piece of it: I'm not just an old tortoise who bakes.
There's a resistance in this kingdom, and I'm its contact here in {town}. A woman called Wren leads it, from a hideout in the Capital.
I wasn't sure of you before. I am now, near enough, and I don't say that about many people.
Two zones free, and the square's louder for it. I complain about the noise every morning and don't mean a word of it.
Halfway, dearie. I'd say I'm proud of you, but then you'd stop trying.
Auntie Alembic keeps asking after you. I tell her you're busy, and for once it's even true.
Two zones free, and Auntie Alembic has opened the Alchemist's on the square. She brews cards from two Paths at once, if you can stand the steam.
She's been asking for your leftovers. From her, that's a compliment.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cav: The hooded figure is back at the cave mouth with two cups of something hot. She hands you one without asking.
Two Paths free, and I could hear the town singing from all the way out here. Badly, but singing.
You knew I'd come back here.
You always came back to the same places. Even when you were...
Drink your tea. It's for the shaking.
Even when I was what?
Even when you were somewhere you weren't allowed to leave. Ask me something easier.
Favourite colour?
Four of them. Next question.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.3.in: You're shaking. Sit down, slowly now. Here, take my hand.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.3.fr: A throne room at night, the candles guttering under banners with four colors woven into one.
A man in white and gold kneels before the king and speaks in a soft voice. Then he rises, and his soft voice is the last soft thing in the room.
Two pairs of hands are on my shoulders, pushing me behind them, toward the dark.
I know that man's face, and I think I have always known it. {villain}.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.3.af: A man in white and gold, kneeling and then standing. And before that, those rooms with glass on every side.
I know that glass, because I helped to blow it. Long ago I founded the study of the Paths, and I did it for the best of reasons.
{villain} took my work and made a cage of it, and my best student kept the lab running for him. And I ran.
I've been hiding here ever since, with my hands in pie dough, where nobody would think to ask what else those hands had made.
That's my secret. Now you're holding it, the same way I've been holding yours.
One Path left under {villain}'s thumb, and the whole town's holding its breath. I can hold mine for a week, being a tortoise. They can't.
Three zones free, dearie. Do finish the fourth before this pie goes stale; I'd give it about a week.
You walk like somebody with somewhere to be these days. I liked the damp young man better. He visited more.
Three zones free. Only one Path is left under {villain}'s thumb now, and I won't tell you what I'm feeling about it, except that it's a great deal.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cav: She is waiting at the cave mouth again with her hood down, as if she forgot it was up. Her eyes are tired and very sure.
Three. At first I told myself you just reminded me of someone. Someone I lost when we were kids. Now I'm starting to think...
No, not until I'm certain. Too many people around here say things before they're sure, and I won't be one of them.
You knew me before all this.
I knew a boy who fell on his behind trying to lift a dumbbell, and who ate the frosting off every layer of his cake.
You'd have liked him. He was terrible at hiding things.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.4.in: There's something in your face today, the look of someone who's just been handed a key. Tell me what it opens.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.4.fr: A boy of eleven stands in a coat too fine for the cold. Someone calls across a courtyard: '{prince}!'
I turn toward a woman's voice, and then a man's, and on every door is the {royal_house} crest: four signs in a ring.
{prince_full}, son of the king and queen. The whole kingdom believes he died ten years ago.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.4.af: {prince}. {prince} {royal_house}. I met a boy once at court, hiding behind his mother's cloak, who asked me why tortoises carry their houses.
I told him, 'So we are never far from home.'
