I knew, you see. The Warden opens that tunnel for one family only, and I knew it the moment you walked out of it. I was too frightened to say so.
Four signs in a ring, the same as the ones carved on my stick. I've carried it for ten years and never told a soul why.
And my lab, my life's work, was used on that boy. On you. Forgive me if you ever can. I'd understand if you couldn't.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.4.re: There's nothing to forgive. You gave me a bed and pie when you still thought I might be a spy.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.4.af: ...Then let us make the kingdom a home again, {prince}.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.4.in: You've the look of someone who was told something he didn't want to hear. Was it {villain}?
Sit down and tell me what he said. All of it.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.4.af: So he knew you from the very first. He told you who you are, and you've come to me for the rest of it.
I knew too. The Warden opens that tunnel for one family only, and I knew it the moment you came out of it. I was just too frightened to say so.
So hear it from someone who held your hand at court: you are {prince_full}, and I'm so sorry for what was done to you with the things I built.
All four Paths free, and {villain} still sitting in his castle as if nothing's changed. Go and knock, dearie. Loudly.
The roads are open, and even I've been using them. I passed a hare this morning; he's asked for a recount.
Eat something first, then go to the castle. Nobody ever toppled a tyrant properly on an empty stomach.
All four Paths are free, and {kingdom} is whole again, or nearly. Up in his castle, {villain} will be counting what he has left.
Get some rest. Then we finish this, together.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cav: The cave mouth is quiet. This time she is standing, cloak fastened, a satchel of four-coloured vials over her shoulder, ready to go somewhere.
All four. Can you hear it? The kingdom's breathing again, like voices through a wall, except now the wall's coming down.
There's only the Capital left. Only him.
Come with me.
I'll be at the castle gate when you get there. Somebody has to watch the door while you knock it down.
And when it's over, I'll tell you everything. My name first. I promise.
data/story/old_well_story.json::beats.vi: You touch the stone. It is cold, and then it is not. Far below, something moves that has not moved in years: water, or the memory of it.
...Four streams. One spring. They drank together, once.
...The water went down when they stopped sharing. Not all of it. Listen for what is left.
Two hums answer, faint as a wet finger round a glass. One is on the Verdant Dump's highest terrace, where its river starts to fall.
The other is in the Endless Buffet, by a little pond under the broccoli.
The townsfolk say the well doesn't talk. I'm not going to be the one who tells them.
data/story/old_well_story.json::beats.to: ...Listen. What is left of the water still hums.
One hum is high in the Verdant Dump, on its highest terrace, where the river starts to fall.
One hum is in the Endless Buffet, by the little gravy pond in the Broccoli Forest.
data/story/old_well_story.json::beats.fi: At the head of the falls, under a lip of roots and old junk, a thread of water comes up clear. The cleanest water in the Dump starts in its dirtiest corner.
Someone has thrown a boot in the spring. The water has gone politely round it.
For a blink you see four streams leaving one spring: red, blue, purple and green. This one was green. It fed the fields, and the fields fed everyone.
A whisper, from very far away: 'One stream remembers.'
The pond is gravy, like everything here. Under the gravy, ringed with old stones, is a basin far older than the Buffet: the first stockpot, built round a spring.
Every Gourmand recipe still begins with the same two words: first, water. Somebody has added 'and salt' here. Twice.
For a blink you see four streams leaving one spring. This one was blue. It went into the first pot, and the first pot fed a kingdom.
A whisper, from very far away: 'One stream remembers.'
Far away in {town}, the Old Well hums a little louder. One more stream to find.
Far away in {town}, the Old Well hums like a full kettle. Both streams have answered, and the well is calling you back.
data/story/old_well_story.json::beats.to: The well is full. Not of water: of light, every colour of the four Paths at once, turning slowly, like something stirred.
...Both streams remember. Now the spring will see who is asking.
data/story/old_well_story.json::beats.ec: ...I am what is left when the water goes. Every Path's voice, in one throat.
Hold all four, and I will run again. Hold fewer, and I will show you what the others were for.
...Not yet. The spring is patient. It has had ten years of practice.
The light sinks back into the stone. It will rise again when you touch the well.
The light sinks into the stone, and for a moment the well is a mirror. In it you see a spring under the whole kingdom: under the town, under the vault, under everything.
...Once there was one spring. Four peoples drank from it and gave it four names.
They argued about the name for a thousand years. The water did not mind.
Where it rose, they built a town to argue in. Over its source they built a vault, and the four Paths locked it together, so no one Path could own the water.
It ran while the four shared it, and while one house held them together.
Ten years ago the house went quiet. The streams stopped speaking. The spring went down to wait.
The little spring at the end of the old royal tunnel went to dust. This one nearly did.
Good new wells were dug all over the kingdom, clean and straight. The water did not come. It never comes when it is told.
...It does not run for one shape. It runs for many, held together, and it has waited ten years for a hand that can hold all four.
It hums when you touch it. Take a little with you. It remembers the way home.
A well with opinions. I'm keeping the bottle anyway.
data/story/old_well_story.json::text.que: The Old Well remembers a spring that once fed all four Paths. Two hums still answer it, one in the Verdant Dump and one in the Endless Buffet. Find both.
Find what hums in the Verdant Dump
Find what hums in the Endless Buffet
Go back to the Old Well and face what answers
The Dump's highest terrace, where its river starts to fall: something there hums like the well
The little gravy pond in the Buffet's Broccoli Forest: something there hums like the well
The Old Well in {town}, in its yard off the west market street
data/story/old_well_story.json::text.tou: The Old Well hums, low and steady, like a kettle kept warm for whoever comes home.
data/story/old_well_story.json::text.con: The Echo duels with all four Paths at once. It is a hard fight. Lose, and nothing is lost: the well will wait.
data/story/old_well_story.json::text.toa: Both streams remember. Go back to the Old Well.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::The We: ...you came back... the water remembers the shape of you...
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Ripples
At half health the water answers: two 1/1 Ripples rise on the Echo's side.
...you were here... you were small... the water remembers the shape of you...
Two 1/1 Ripples rise from the well.
Still Water
Near the end the spring gathers itself: the Echo heals 3.
...not yet... the spring runs once more...
The Echo heals 3.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: A four-coloured core hums at the heart of the vault, four marks set in a ring. Beside it a clockwork guardian unfolds, with a sound like a very old clock remembering the hour.
'Tick. Identify,' it says. 'The Old Kingdom's banner is not for just anyone.'
data/story/intro_story.tres::graveyard_i: The stones here were stacked by hands that stopped moving a long time ago.
Something under the cairn is still keeping count of its turns. It has been keeping count since before {villain} came.
Touch it, and it will not stop counting until one of you does.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::The Re: The stones count. One. Two. The dead are counting with them.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: The Count Pauses
At half health the dead lose count: their units stand still through their next turn.
The counting stops. Somewhere under the stones, someone has lost their place.
The dead stand still: their units miss their next turn.
The Cairn Remembers
Near the end the dead hesitate: their units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
The dead stop. They look at your hands as if they have seen them before.
The dead hesitate: their units get -1/-0.
data/story/intro_story.tres::graveyard_v: Whatever was keeping time down there has nothing left to spend it on.
The stones are just stones again. Take what it was guarding.
data/story/intro_story.tres::graveyard_d: Come back when you have more turns to spare than it does.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: A hidden chest in one of Crosspath's odd corners
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::s: Elder Maren says the door under the Old Well has been locked since before she was born. Its key is in a hidden chest somewhere in Crosspath.
Find the hidden chest in Crosspath
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: There is a door under the old well that has been locked since before I was born.
I always thought the key was lost, but it wasn't, dearie. Somebody hid it in a chest right here in town. Find it, and we'll see what the door is for.
The key's in a hidden chest somewhere in town. Look in the odd corners, dearie; this town has never quite managed a straight one.
You found it. Look at the bow: four little carvings in a ring. Hm. Never mind that. I'm too old for stairs, dearie, and you're not.
The door's the iron hatch beside the well. Go on down. Whatever's under it belonged to the Old Kingdom, not to me, so mind the stairs.
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::_oldes: The Oldest Trick in the Book
That giant chest was too good to be true. Someone is conning travellers with chests like it, and he's taken your gold. Find the rest of the chests, and you'll find him.
Face the Master of the Oldest Trick
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::_four_: Somewhere far off, a great lock has ground open. Each Path zone hides a lever that answers a seal near Crosspath. Find all four.
Find the hidden lever in each Path zone
The Four-Seal Vault, in the hills north of Crosspath
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Automaton clicks, whirs and lowers one knee. In its outstretched hand, folded neatly, is the Old Kingdom's banner.
'Tick. ...Recognised. Four Paths. One kingdom. Carry it well.'
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Shiro: You found me! Nobody finds me, which can only mean this is a trick. Mine, obviously.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::The Wa: Four seals, four Paths, one hand. Show me the hand.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: SMOKE BOMB!!!
At half health Shiro throws a smoke bomb: your strongest ready unit is exhausted and misses your next turn.
SMOKE BOMB!!! The oldest trick in the book. Page one. I wrote page one.
Your strongest ready unit is lost in the smoke until after your next turn.
Body Double
Near the end Shiro swaps places with a log: the next 4 damage to him is absorbed.
You hit a log. A very convincing log. I gave it my eyebrows.
Shiro's log absorbs the next 4 damage.
The Seal of Iron Breaks
At half health the first seal breaks and the Warden gathers the pieces: the next 3 damage to it is absorbed.
One seal for one Path, and the hand is real. Show me the rest of it.
The Warden gathers the broken seal: the next 3 damage is absorbed.
The Last Seal
Near the end the last seal opens: the Warden's units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
The last seal opens. The four Paths agreed to bury this, and they agreed that one day you might come for it.
The Warden's units get -1/-0.
Recalibrate
At half health the Automaton recalibrates: the next 3 damage to it is absorbed.
Tick. Damage noted. Tick. Recalibrating.
The Automaton absorbs the next 3 damage.
Recognised
Near the end the Automaton hesitates: its units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
Four colours. One thread. Tick. ...Recognised.
The Automaton hesitates: its units get -1/-0.
data/story/capital_story.tres::hud.objec: The Capital: the walls are up and the Approved Gate is the only way in. Pass Captain Spotless's entry examination (a card battle), or find another way.
HP does not come back after battles; rifts hurt; the hideout heals. {villain}'s Castle waits at the far end of the city.

Find the Wrinkles' hideout: knock at the manhole near the gate. Help them with one quest for each Path, seal the rifts, and reach {villain}'s Castle at the north end. Each Path you free mends a broken city service.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ui.exit.t: Walk back down the road to {town}?
data/story/capital_story.tres::ui.exit.b: Leaving the Capital ends this visit. Town heals you fully. The Approved Gate stays open for you, but every roaming officer, inspector and Tidy-Bot will be back next time, and so will the rifts.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ui.gate.b: Captain Spotless measures you against the Approved Visitor Standard: a hard card battle, his deck fair to nobody. Your HP carries in from the zone and nothing heals in between. Lose, and you wake outside, a little poorer.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ui.main.b: The great doors stand open, which is worse than closed. Twenty-odd rooms of portraits and good intentions, then {villain} himself. HP carries in; nothing heals except at the shrines. Your zone's broken-service debuffs apply to every duel.

{villain} is gone. The castle is just a very large, very tidy building now, and the portraits have started to peel. You may walk through it again for the memories (and the gold). HP carries in; nothing heals except at the shrines.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.main_d: You see your worried face in the gold handles of {villain}'s Castle. Beyond the doors, you smell floor wax and hear someone humming.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.galler: The glass is cracked from the inside, and behind it the castle's halls go on in silver, too clean to be real. Wren would want to hear about this.
Behind the cracked glass the castle's halls go on in silver: every frame holds someone you beat, perfect and cold, waiting for you.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: The cracked mirror beside the castle door
data/story/capital_story.tres::quest.cra: Before you go. The mirrors in his castle are still showing a kingdom that never was. Straight streets, smiling people, nobody hungry.
One of them, by the castle door, cracked from the inside last night. I don't like what I saw behind it. Will you go and look?
The mirror by the castle door, the one cracked from the inside. Go and look into it, and come back and tell me I imagined it.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.heal_c: Nurse Hesper hands you a cup of the Tea of Dissent. It is strong, bitter and entirely unapproved. HP restored.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.heal_a: You are already at full HP. Nurse Hesper hands you a cup anyway. 'Dissent,' she says, 'is good for the circulation.'
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.hit::0: The Capital catches you hard, the way it catches everyone. (-HP)
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.hit_ri: A rift tears at you as you pass. The Capital has no record of it. (-%d HP)
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.hit_ro: %s knocks you flat. Please remain orderly. (-%d HP)
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.wake::: You wake up on a cot in the Crease. Nurse Hesper Dray is writing on a clipboard that, you notice, is blank on purpose.
'I dragged you in by the collar, and the correction fee comes out of your purse. Drink. Then we can talk about this habit you have of arriving unconscious.'
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.wake_o: You wake in the dust outside the Approved Gate. A guard leans over you, measuring your height with a long stick.
'Falling down in the approved queue area is a minor offence, and the fine is payable now. Up you get, citizen. I cannot measure you while you are lying along the ground.'
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.chest:: A hidden stash! Someone hid this where {villain}'s inspectors would not look: behind something untidy.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.inside: You're through the walls. Somewhere above you a loudspeaker clears its throat, and you are now, officially, a Visitor in {capital}, the Capital of {kingdom}.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.no_tra: The service-tunnel network is down. The wheels that once turned the shaft lifts have spent ten years lighting the facade instead. 'No travel,' says a Wrinkle's note on the hatch.
'Free the Gainlands and we will get the lifts turning.'
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.shaft:: You drop down the shaft, ride the lift through the dark and climb out somewhere else, smelling of rust.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.ladder: You climb the ladder and push the manhole open. The Capital's cold light falls in.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.tunnel: You crawl out through the old tunnel and shove the rubble aside, and you're back in the Outskirts, a long way from anybody's approved queue.
You squeeze back down the collapsed shaft and follow the old tunnel in the dark.
Past the rubble and a toppled statue, a flight of stairs leads down to an old plaque: 'THE OLD JOINT WORKS. BUILT BY ALL FOUR PATHS, TOGETHER.'
The tunnel runs under the wall, under the gate and under every one of {villain}'s checkpoints, and you walk beneath them all without being measured once. It's the best moment you've had all day.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.manhol: You knock three times. The manhole opens to a hand and a tired voice: 'Down you come.'
There's a manhole by the wall with a scratch on its lid, like a tiny wrinkle. You knock three times, for no reason you can name.
After a pause the lid lifts and a hand beckons you down. 'Wrinkle?' a voice mutters, and you decide that, yes, you probably are.
Down a ladder, along a brick tunnel, into a warm room full of mismatched furniture and people who are all, visibly, not ironed.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.deface: You draw a moustache on {villain_title}'s portrait. A small coin drops from the frame: the Wrinkles' bounty for this improvement.
Someone has already improved this one. With the moustache he looks, for the first time, like a person.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.compla: You post a complaint. A coin drops from a slot with a note: 'Compensation for your inconvenience. Please use it to have less inconvenience.'
You post a complaint. A hatch opens and a warm cup of tea is pushed out, still steaming. 'We value your concern,' says a note. You feel a little better.
You post a complaint. 'Noted,' says the box, gently, and after a long wait you understand that this was the whole service.
You post a complaint, and a klaxon sounds. A Perfection Inspector appears from nowhere, measures your frown, writes you up and walks off.
'Thank you for your feedback,' says the box.
The box rattles, full to the slot. It has had quite enough of your feedback for one visit.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.seal::: You set the rift-stone and say the old word: close. The tear shudders, folds in on itself like a letter, and is gone. The air smells of rain. Sealed!
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.seal_g: The rift-stone will not take while the rift's guardian still stands. Whatever it spat out has to go first.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.seal_d: The rift is sealed. Where it was there is a scorch mark and the memory of a very bad idea.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.seal_c: This one is too big to seal. It runs all the way up into the castle, and it will only close when he does.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.pickup: A real recipe, written by hand, with a stain of actual sauce on the corner! Flour: some. Salt: enough. Time: until it smells right. It is wonderfully imprecise. You tuck it away.
A banished compost heap is hiding in a cellar where it was never allowed to be, still warm and still very much alive.
It steams, very slightly, with gratitude. Rescued!
You unwrap a handkerchief and find a worn rubber stamp: FINAL APPROVAL. Someone hid it here, ready for the day it was needed.
An old glass jar holds a single seed, glowing very faintly green. Nobody has planted anything in the Capital for ten years, and the seed hasn't given up.
You already took the one lying here.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.wheel_: The crew of the first wheel keeps running while you talk, because stopping is not permitted. 'Cardio,' pants a woman, 'is mandatory.' You find the brake lever under a pile of notices.
The wheel groans, slows and stops. The crew sit on the floor and laugh and cry at the same time.
The second wheel has been turning since some of its runners were too small to reach the pedals. A foreman's whistle hangs on a hook nearby, and you pocket it.
The wheel winds down. 'We were told,' says a man, 'that this was how you got strong.'
The third wheel's crew are children in school caps. 'It is a school activity,' says a banner, but nobody has rung the bell in years.
You pull the lever and lift them down one by one. They're very small and very proud, and they keep asking, 'Did Rollo send you?'
This crew is free. They're lying on their backs looking up at the sky, and it's the best they've felt in ten years.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.cable:: You cut the big black cable that feeds the facade's lights from the wheels. A spark; a silence. Far off, the perfect lamps flicker, stutter and come back on: {villain} keeps a very small private generator, just for himself.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.cable_: The cable is cut. The wires twitch occasionally, out of habit.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.paste:: You pull the lever and ask the Perfect Nutrient Paste Dispenser for a refund. It chokes, burps and covers itself in a bright green foam that smells, fatally, of actual cabbage. A paste machine is not supposed to remember cabbage.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.paste_: The dispenser is spoiled and sulking. The foam is still fizzing a little.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.plot::: With the Stamp of Final Approval pressed to the form, the grave plot's little iron gate unlocks. A line of mourners, who have waited three years outside, file in.
You watch the neighbourhood carry Mr. Pell to his grave. Nobody holds a permit to sing, so they sing very quietly. Nobody stops them.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.plot_a: The Pell plot is tended and quiet, with fresh flowers on it. The family comes every morning now.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.plot_l: The iron gate is sealed with a notice: 'NO BURIAL WITHOUT A STAMPED PERMIT (FORM 27-B/6, FINAL APPROVAL).' Widow Pell said a stamp was hidden in Grave Row, north of the permit office.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.patch:: You kneel, scoop a hole with your hands and drop in the seed. You water it with what is left in your flask. Nothing happens, for one long, bad moment.
Then a shoot, as thin as a thread, noses out of the dirt. And another. And a flower, the colour of everything the Capital is not.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.patch_: The patch is green and growing. A bee, which should not exist in the Capital, hovers over it, deciding.
The patch is sick, grey and cracked, and nothing will grow in it without a seed. Old Fern mentioned an old seed in a jar, hidden somewhere in the Reek.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.permit: The clerk behind the window slides you a form. 'For a burial permit, Form 27-B. Please attach Form 27-C (Proof of Grief).'
You ask for 27-C. 'Please attach Form 27-B,' she says.
'Form 27-C requires Form 27-B,' she says, 'and Form 27-B requires Form 27-C.' You point out, gently, that this is a loop.
'It is a process,' she says, with fear in her eyes.
'Please take a number.' You take a number. It says 4,112,009.
The sign above the window says NOW SERVING: 3. It has said so for three years.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.ward_w: You read: 'Spontaneity Permits: Thursdays, 3:00 to 3:05, by appointment.' Inside, the clerk sleeps upright, eyes open.
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.be: The Beefcakes kept the kingdom's energy and its roads: the wheels, the mills, the throwers and the portal-rippers. {villain} put them all on wheels to light one showpiece street. The rest of the kingdom went dark.
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.go: The Gourmands fed and guarded the kingdom. {villain} replaced them with Perfect Nutrient Paste. Real food is gone from the Capital, and so is the comfort it gave.
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.ne: The Necrocrats looked after the dead and their paperwork. {villain}'s permits locked the dead out of their graves and the paperwork in an endless loop. The dead do not rest, and the things that have died keep coming back.
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.re: The Refusemancers took out the kingdom's waste and turned it back into soil. {villain} called composting untidy and hid the garbage behind the facade. Rubbish is piling up, in the streets and in your deck.
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.ru: The Capital is dark and you can see only a short way.
The service-tunnel network is down: no travel.
Healing items do not work (food does not agree with the Capital).
data/story/capital_story.tres::prop.past: PERFECT NUTRIENT PASTE. TASTES OF NOTHING. THAT IS THE POINT.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.gate: 1. Visitors must be of approved height.
2. Visitors must be smiling at an approved angle.
3. Visitors must not have unapproved opinions.
4. Visitors must have already been approved.
To leave, please obtain an Exit Permit, an Exit Interview and an Exit Interview Permit.
Between this line and that line. Slouching is a violation. Standing on tiptoes is a violation.
Having a height is, on balance, a violation.
The Capital. Population: neat. Remember: it is perfect. If it is not, that is your fault.
All departures require an interview. Please explain how elsewhere could possibly be an improvement.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.faca: Every house in this quarter was built to show what the whole kingdom could be if everybody simply tried harder.
Approved Hat Sizes: 1. A perfect fit is your responsibility.
Hats of other sizes are a Disagreement.
Fun may be had Thursdays 3:00 to 3:05. Please queue for fun.
Please smile at least 70% of the time. Smile with your teeth. Mind the edges.
Grass shall be 2.0 cm tall. Do not walk on it. Your footprints have not been approved.
Hedges shall be square. Hedges that wish to be round must submit a request.
Queue here for the Orderly Queue. Any impatience must be expressed in order.
Announcements are cheerful. Cheerfulness is not optional. Neither are announcements.
(Not a real door. Please do not look behind it. There is nothing behind it.)
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.reek: Formerly the Verdant Quarter. Now the place we put everything that does not look nice.
By decree: all composting is outlawed. Rubbish shall be placed where it cannot be seen. That place is here.
The act of composting is a form of Disorder. Offenders will be corrected.
ALL GARBAGE GOES BEHIND THE FACADE
(It is not garbage. It is Behind.)
The soil here has stopped growing. Please do not ask why. Please do not plant anything. Please do not feel anything.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.net_: To the Crease. Wrinkles only. If you are not a Wrinkle, you did not see this.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.grav: Formerly the Cemetery of {kingdom}. Currently Closed Pending Review.
Burial permit: Form 27-B. Attach Form 27-C. Form 27-C requires Form 27-B. Please queue.
Take a number to take a number. Your number is: 4,112,009. Now serving: 3.
The deceased are asked to remain in their parlours until a permit has been approved. Please do not wander.
Reserved since before the permit system. Locked since the permit system.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.net_: To the Crease. Living passengers only. The dead have asked to come down too; we are thinking about it. Be kind.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.tran: Where the kingdom's energy and its roads were made. Now: where the facade's lights are made.
Every citizen shall run the wheels for six hours a day, so that the wheels never stop and the lights never go out. Your legs are not your own.
Trams must arrive on time. None did. All trams are suspended. Punctuality has improved considerably.
The big black cable is the facade's lifeline. Cutting it is a crime. Please do not cut it.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.net_: To the Crease. Out of service: the lifts need the wheels, and the wheels are busy lighting a small town.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.hung: Formerly the Market of the Four Paths. Now: where everybody queues for the one approved meal.
One serving per citizen per meal. Every meal. Tastes of nothing. No preferences will be left unsatisfied.
Real food is a source of Individual Preference and has therefore been replaced.
Delight is a form of inefficiency. Please eat in silence.
The same as yesterday and the same as tomorrow. You may stop consulting the menu.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.net_: To the Crease. There's a smell of real cooking coming up this shaft, and nobody ever mentions it.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.cast: Please do not stare. He can tell.
Each portrait has been improved. Please admire them in order.
{villain} has assured everyone that the tears are temporary. He has assured everyone of this for ten years.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.net_: To the Crease. If you hear humming from the castle above, do not hum along.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.yard: Seventeen checkpoints in one street. The last checks whether you enjoyed the first sixteen.
The staff left in the night. They left their forms behind.
Authority transferred, reviewed, approved, notarized, filed. The authorization is valid. Nobody is here to enforce it.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.ward: Citizens who smile incorrectly are sent here for improvement. Improvement takes as long as it takes.
No laughter. No sighing. No unapproved crying.
Crying must be done in the correct order.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.out_: Please join the approved queue and wait to be measured.
Queue here. You may not queue anywhere else. You may not queue here without a queue number. You may not have a queue number.
It was a very good checkpoint. It checked everything.
(somebody has drawn a moustache on the guard. It suits him.)

The tears are temporary and fully under control. (Scrawled below: the Paths tear where {villain} forced them into one shape. His hold is failing; it first slipped the night someone escaped the Ministry.)
Do not touch. Do not look. Do not whistle.
To leave the Outskirts, walk back down the road. To leave the Capital, please see: the Exit Interview Booth.
the old tunnel came out near here
(a scrap of paper pinned under a stone: 'forgotten service shaft, SW of the wall, behind the fallen statue. Rubble is mostly for show.')
OLD JOINT WORKS: PROPERTY OF THE FOUR PATHS
Closed and forgotten, and on nobody's map. (Try the south-west corner.)
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.plaz: Please proceed in an orderly fashion, in the approved direction, at the approved speed, with the approved face.
Departures require an interview. Interviews require an appointment. Appointments require a departure.
Your complaint matters. Reading it remains optional.
(a small scratch on the cover, like a wrinkle)
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.net_: To the Crease. Authorized personnel only. The authorization is: you knocked.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.crea: A Wrinkle is something that does not go away when you press it.
Founded by the people {villain} could not iron out. No dues, no forms, and nobody here has to smile.
Built by all four Paths, together, back when we did that. Six shafts, six streets. (Beefcake wheels power the lifts. No wheels, no lifts.)
2. Eat what you like. 3. Wear a hat of any size.
4. Do not tell anyone where we are.
Another one through the shafts. Sit down. I'm Wren; I was the Royal Archivist once, and now I keep the records this city isn't supposed to have.
Maren sent word from {town} that someone might come. This is the Crease, and we're the Wrinkles, the people {villain} couldn't iron out. We have tea and grudges. The tea's better.

He's in the castle at the north end, and he truly believes he's helping, which is the hard part. Talk to the people in the streets. Each of them carries a piece of what he did, and I want it all in the record.
Back in one piece? Good. Hesper charges by the piece.
The records say he began well. His first decree put a hot lunch in front of every schoolchild, and I want you to remember that. It excuses nothing, but remember it.
You brought me something from the streets. It goes in the true record, in ink, where he can't correct it.
That's two pieces of him now: a man who needs to be right, and a man who can't bear to be disagreed with. I can almost see his shape.
That's three. He's afraid, you know, and not of you.
He's afraid of everything that won't obey him. It's a small, sad fear for a man with so much gold.
That's all four, and I have the whole of him now. He is not a monster.
He's a man who made a list of everything he couldn't control, and then made it illegal.
Go and finish it. Gently, if you can. But finish it.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.fig.i: Psst. Over here. Fig Sly, purveyor of contraband and curiosities.
Everything on this table is illegal, uneven or both.
Rare cards, good prices, no questions. Well: one question. Would you like a bag? Bags are illegal too.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.fig.r: Back for more? Wise. Rare stock never lasts. Mind the one on the end: it bites.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.hespe: Hesper Dray. I'm the nurse down here, so do as I say: sit, and drink.
It's tea, strong and bitter and unapproved. Drink it while it's still three things the Ministry dislikes.
The rifts? That's his hold failing. Everything he forced together keeps coming apart at the seams, and he keeps stitching.
It began the night the boy got out, they say. Nobody says 'boy' where the loudspeakers can hear.
Bleeding again? Sit. I'll pretend to be surprised.
Keep your voice down, will you? I'm Old Fern. Composter, which in this city is about the worst thing a person can be.
I spent forty years turning this city's scraps back into soil, and now that's 'untidy'. So am I, apparently. I've got worms in my hat to prove it.
They swept the rubbish behind the facade and pretended it wasn't there. Now the soil's sick, nothing grows in the Reek, and I'm too old to dig alone. Help me save what's left.
Any luck? The heaps are tucked into cellars and holes all over the Reek. They think they're hiding from the inspectors. Tell them they're coming home.
Oh, you've come to the door. Forgive me, it's been a long while since anyone did. I'm Widow Pell. My husband died three years ago, in his chair in the front parlour.
And I can't bury him. Form 27-B needs a 27-C, and the 27-C needs a 27-B, so he's still in his chair, waiting, the way he always used to wait for me.
I still talk to him in there. He was always the patient one of us, and it turns out I'm not. If you can help at all, please.
Someone hid the Stamp of Final Approval where no official would ever look: in Grave Row, north of the permit office, among papers nobody reads.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.rollo: Name's Rollo Spokes... wheel foreman, Beefcake, out of the Gainlands. Back home... a wheel stopped at night... and so did the man on it.
Here, the facade needs lighting... so we pedal it. No pay, no end. They told us it was cardio... My calves have calves.
My crews have pedalled six hours a day for ten years... and nobody's ever told them they can stop. Somebody ought to... somebody they'll believe.
Three wheels in the Yards... pull each brake and talk to the crew. Then the big cable by the east wall, the one that feeds the facade... cut it.
The crews won't get off... till somebody tells them it's all right to. So you tell them... and mean it.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.marlo: Hands where I can see them... good, no inspector's gloves. I'm Chef Marlo. I cooked at the Market of the Four Paths, once. Now I'm a 'Nutrient Distributor', and my recipes stay in my apron.
Everyone eats {villain}'s Perfect Nutrient Paste, three times a day. Paste is food the way a form is a hug.
For ten years I've hidden real recipes all over this quarter, so that somebody, somewhere, remembers what food is.
Three recipe cards, tucked away around the quarter, and then the dispenser. Spoil it for me, and spoil it badly. I've waited ten years to say that.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.spotl: HALT. I am Captain Spotless. State your height.
No: do not state it. Stand at it. Straighter. Not that straight. APPROVED straight.
Entry requires the Approved Visitor Standard. You are somehow both too tall and too short, and your shadow is the wrong length.
However, the Standard provides for an Entry Examination, conducted as a card battle. Win it, and you are retroactively approved.
Do not look nervous. Nervousness is a Violation. (He polishes a button.) Shall we begin?
You again, still too tall and still smiling at the wrong angle. Are you ready for the Examination?
You are approved. I have always supported this outcome. Please remember that exact wording.
Please do not tell {villain_title} that I lost. Please do not tell anyone that I lost.
You are... approved. You are retroactively approved.
The Standard is satisfied. The gate opens, by order of the Standard and against my personal feelings.
I have measured twelve thousand visitors and approved four. Nine thousand were sent home. About the rest, I would rather not say.
Go through, citizen. In there, try not to be what you are.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.guard: Height inspection! Stand against the post, please, and straighten up.
Not that straight. Hm... you are one hair above regulation.
One hair, I will let go, this time. Please do not grow while you are inside.
Still one hair above regulation. I have thought about that hair all week. Do not make me regret it.
Queue management! This is the approved queue, and you are already in it.
You are not allowed to leave the queue. You are not allowed to join the queue. I do not understand it either.
Still queueing? Good. You have a gift for remaining eligible.
It is a long queue. It is the best queue we have.
Exit control. You wish to leave? But you have not finished arriving. Please arrive first.
Exit control. Please have your exit permit ready, and your exit interview permit, and, if at all possible, a reason.
Exit control. This is the exit. It is also the entrance. It is also, from some angles, a wall.
Exit control. You are, I think, still inside. Congratulations.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.exit_: Exit Interview Booth. Name? Reason for departing the most perfect place in the kingdom?
'It is not perfect' is not an approved answer. Nor is pointing at something while saying it.
Your departure request has been received. It has been filed under 'Dissent'. It will be looked at in four to six years.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.patie: I am Citizen 4471. I was brought here for smiling incorrectly. Eleven degrees, when the approved angle is eight.
It was our wedding day. I had been crying, the happy kind, and they corrected me for that too.
I do not smile at all any more. It is a strange thing, to forget how your own face works.
I am improving, they say. I am not sure that is a good thing.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Grave Row: the stamp lies north of the permit office
The Pell family plot, at the north end of Grave Row
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit
Widow Pell's husband has sat in the family parlour for three years because his burial permit loops forever. It needs the Stamp of Final Approval, somewhere in Grave Row.
Find the Stamp of Final Approval in Grave Row
Lay Mr. Pell to rest at the family plot
data/story/capital_story.tres::quest.cap: All we want is a burial permit: Form 27-B/6, stamped Final Approval, and then he can finally rest.
Somebody hid the Stamp of Final Approval in Grave Row, north of the permit office, among papers nobody reads. Find it, take it to our family plot at the north end of the Row, and let him rest.
The stamp's in Grave Row, north of the permit office, among papers nobody reads. Then bring it to our plot at the north end of the Row. Please.
He's at rest? Oh. Oh.
I sat by the plot all morning and didn't say a word. It was the first quiet in three years that wasn't a fear.
Here, this was his. He'd want it to go to someone young, who'll use it.
There's something you should know about the man in the castle. He schedules grief: Thursdays, 3:00 to 3:05. Anyone who cries outside those hours is corrected.
I don't think he is cruel. I think he simply cannot bear to watch.
Thank you, a hundred times over. I sit with him at the plot every morning now. Remember what I told you, it's in your journal: he can't bear a sadness he didn't schedule.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: The energy wheels along the Transit Yards wall
The main power cable, in the Transit Yards
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: The Wheel Never Stops
Beefcake crews have run the facade's energy wheels for ten years because nobody told them they could stop. Go and tell them, in the Transit Yards.
Free the wheel crews in the Transit Yards
Cut the facade's power cable in the Yards
data/story/capital_story.tres::quest.cap: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... three crews nobody ever told to stop. Pull each brake lever... and tell them it's all right, in plain words.
They won't believe you at first... say it anyway. Then cut the big cable by the east wall. Those facade lights have run on my crews' legs... for ten years.
Three wheels in the Transit Yards... free the crews, then cut the big cable by the east wall. Keep telling them they can stop... it takes a few goes.
I heard the lights flicker from here... then I heard the crews sit down. The whole yard's gone quiet.
Haven't heard a quiet yard since the coup. Thank you.
Here... from the old days. We gave these out... at the end of a shift. Remember ends?
One thing about the man in the castle... he made lateness illegal. That's a man who can't bear to wait... for anyone.
Remember that when you meet him. He's always in a hurry... to be loved.
The wheels are slowing... and the crews are resting. Remember what I told you, it's in your journal: to him, lateness is disagreement... and that's the one thing he won't forgive.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Recipe cards hidden around the Hungry Quarter
The paste dispenser, in the Hungry Quarter
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: The Recipe Box
Everyone eats {villain}'s Perfect Nutrient Paste. Chef Marlo's three real recipes are hidden in the Hungry Quarter. Find them before the inspectors do.
Find Chef Marlo's recipe cards in the Hungry Quarter
Spoil the paste dispenser in the Hungry Quarter
data/story/capital_story.tres::quest.cap: Three of my recipes are hidden in the Hungry Quarter: a bread, a stew, a sauce. Real ones, in my hand, quantities written as 'some'. Find them before the inspectors do.
And the paste dispenser here in the quarter: spoil it for me. Put something in it that tastes of something.
Three recipe cards in the Hungry Quarter, and the dispenser to spoil. You'll know my cards: 'some' of this, 'a bit' of that. That's how a good recipe reads.
The bread! The stew! The sauce!
Look at the stains on them, look at the spelling! And that smell from the dispenser... cabbage. Real cabbage.
I'm crying, and you'll let me. Here: my real recipe, the one I never dared write down until today.
And one thing about the man in the castle: he can't taste. Not food, not wine, not salt. He never could.
He built a whole kingdom of paste because he could not understand what the rest of us were missing.
I'm cooking again, real food with a real mess. Remember what I told you, it's in your journal: he made everyone eat what he couldn't taste.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Banished heaps hide in the Reek's cellars and yards
The Sick Patch in the Reek. Find the jar of old seed first
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Untidy
Composting is outlawed as untidy, and the land is sickening for it. Three banished compost heaps are hiding in the Reek. Rescue them.
Rescue the banished compost heaps in the Reek
Plant the old seed in the Sick Patch
data/story/capital_story.tres::quest.cap: Three compost heaps are hiding in the Reek, in cellars and yards and under floors, where they were told to wait. Rescue them. They're alive, whatever the inspectors say.
And there's a jar of old seed somewhere in the Reek. Plant it in the Sick Patch. Nobody's planted a thing in this city for ten years.
Three heaps to rescue in the Reek, and the seed for the Sick Patch. Find the jar first, then give the seed its chance. It's waited long enough.
It took? It TOOK! A flower, in this city, after all this time.
I need to sit down. I need to sit down and smell it.
Here, take this. And one thing about the man in the castle: he's afraid of anything that grows without asking him first.
Weeds, moss, children. Anything that might surprise him. I reckon that's the whole of him.
The patch is blooming and the heaps are steaming, untidy as you like. Remember what I said, it's in your journal: he's afraid of anything that grows on its own.
data/story/capital_story.tres::facade.ci: Good day! The weather has been approved, and the lawn is exactly regulation!
Everything is perfect, and I am so, so pleased about it.
Good day! It is a very good day, exactly the same as yesterday.
That is also good. That is the best.
Everything is perfect. Everything is... (a pause, then a whisper) ...please do not tell the Inspector I blinked.
Welcome to {showcase}! Houses, lawns, a small round approved fountain. Everything you could want. Everything you may want.
The bread is lovely. The bread is... (a fixed smile) I am only permitted to call it lovely. I would like, very much, to see some.
I had a name before. I think it started with a B. We are allowed to forget them, and I am doing very well at it.
My house is identical to my neighbour's! Is that not wonderful? There is nothing to envy, and nothing to be envied for.
Isn't it lovely to be exactly the same? I used to be different, I think, though I cannot remember why. It sounds very tiring.
Sometimes I go behind the house and look at the wall. Just the wall. Nobody has told me I cannot. Please do not tell them.
Smile! That is all there is to it! Smiling is mandatory, and I am, in my opinion, a very good smiler.
Seventy percent cheerfulness is the minimum, and today I am at seventy-one! It is a good day.
My cheeks hurt. Please do not tell anyone my cheeks hurt.
The man next door smiled at his wife's funeral. He was remembering her laugh.
(a whisper) They corrected him for a month. He does not remember her laugh now.
The hedge is square! The hedges are all square! I trim the hedge every morning, to make sure it is as square as yesterday's.
The Showcase receives visitors from all over! (a pause) Nobody has visited in six years. We still smile, in case they do.
Do you hear the loudspeaker? It says the same things every day, but once, years ago, it said my name.
Once. I wish it would again.
Spontaneity is only for Thursdays! Today is Wednesday! I am almost allowed to be excited!
Thursday! Five minutes of spontaneity, permit ready! I have rehearsed being caught off guard.
I tried to be spontaneous once, on a Tuesday. I said 'hello' to a bird.
I was corrected for two weeks. (a whisper) I still think about that bird.
Your hat is of an unapproved size, but I will not mention it, because that would be impolite. I am so, so polite. I am the politest person in the Showcase.
There is one Approved Hat Size, and this is the hat. It is a good hat, although I do not know whose it was.
My daughter had a green hat. A little green hat. They said it was a Disagreement.
I do not know where the hat is. I do not know where my daughter is. Everything is perfect.
The Showcase is the best of all possible places! I would not live anywhere else! (looking at the exit) ...I would not be allowed to.
Everyone is so friendly! Everyone is so friendly. It is like living inside a greeting card. The kind with nothing written in it.
There is a door at the back that does not open. I think there is a world on the other side. I think it is raining.
{villain_title} is so kind. He loves us all, and he made everything this way, for us. For our own good. (a shake) For our own good.
The portrait is looking at me. It is always looking at me. It is very kind of him to look.
I would never look away. I cannot.
He is never here, you know. He has never once come down. Only the portraits come.
The portraits do all the looking. It is all done by portrait.
data/story/capital_story.tres::facade.do: You try the front door, but it does not open, because it is not a door.
It is a very well-painted rectangle on the wall. Somebody has even painted a tiny brass knocker, so you knock.
It makes a sound like knocking on a wall.
The door will not open. Through the window you see a painting of a window, and beyond it a painted living room where a painted family sits.
They are all smiling, and they have been smiling for six years.
The door has no handle, and the house has no inside. In the gap behind the facade there is just room for a ladder and a young woman painting the same window for the thousandth time.
She looks at you, then away. She has the face of someone who has meant to write home for years.
You try the door, and to your surprise it opens. It is a closet.
It contains a mop, a bucket and a sign that says: IF YOU ARE READING THIS, SMILE.
data/story/capital_story.tres::facade.sp: Attention, citizens! Today is a PERFECT day! The weather is APPROVED!
Please continue to be happy, as scheduled! Lost Ministry property must be returned at once, and not spoken to!
Attention, citizens! A reminder that smiling is MANDATORY! Those found frowning will be helped! Thank you for your cooperation!
Attention, citizens! (a pause) Attention, citizens! (a very long pause) ...the announcement has been completed. Please clap.
Great news, citizens! This season brings one Approved Hat Size! Choice has never been easier!
Attention, citizens! {villain_title} reminds you that he loves you, and that he is watching. These are the same statement.
Great news, citizens! Spontaneity Thursday approaches! Please rehearse your surprise. We expect a natural performance at three!
Great news, citizens! The public records have never been tidier! Every untidy page has been corrected!
If you remember things differently, please report to the Correction Ward. Your memory will be tidied too!
Attention, citizens! All is well. All has always been well.
A correction: this message has always been correct.
Great news, citizens! The Wrinkles do not exist.
Please report anyone who exists. This has been your Deputy Minister of Good News!
data/story/capital_story.tres::prop.lost: HAVE YOU SEEN THIS IMPROVEMENT OPPORTUNITY?
Height: average. Distinguishing features: none, we hope. Last seen leaving a Ministry facility in the company of a traitor.
Please return to the nearest Ministry office. Reward: a commendation.
HAVE YOU SEEN THIS IMPROVEMENT OPPORTUNITY?
Height: yours. Face: yours. Last seen: reading this poster.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.lost: Have you seen this Improvement Opportunity? Please return to the nearest Ministry office. No questions will be answered.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.deface: You cross out 'Asset' and write 'Person' in the margin, in large letters. A passing citizen pretends not to see, and then, quietly, nods. +12 gold from a grateful Wrinkle.
data/story/intro_story.tres::capital.cas: The castle door is cold to the touch. With the city's services still broken, whatever waits inside will have every advantage.
You could go in now. It would be wiser to wait until the city is back on its feet.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: The shuttered stall at the Hungry Quarter's south-west corner
Down through the ration hatch
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: The Paste Works
The paste comes from somewhere. Chef Marlo thinks the shuttered stall at the Hungry Quarter's south-west corner is a door, and that something real is locked up behind it.
Open the shuttered stall in the Hungry Quarter
Shut down the Paste Works
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: The dispenser's spoiled, and lovely it is too. But the paste has to come from somewhere, doesn't it?
The shuttered stall at the quarter's south-west corner hums at night, and stalls don't hum. Open its ration hatch and have a look down. Gently.
It's the south-west stall, the one with its shutter down. Open the ration hatch, go down, and shut off whatever you find. I'd bet it's very, very grey.
You shut the vats down? All of them? Then tonight the whole quarter eats something that tastes of something.
Some taste. 'Some' is the best amount.
I've kept one real onion in my apron for ten years, and tonight I'm chopping it. You may want to stand back. I'll be weeping, and not only from the onion.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/quo: By the last energy wheel, a ferret in pinstripes stands over Rollo's crews with a stopwatch. They are lying in the sun, and she is still timing them.
You. Again. You cost me the Gainlands in four hours and twelve minutes. I have had the figure framed.
These wheels lit the facade at a hundred and ten percent. Now they are 'resting'. Do you know what rest is? Unmeasured time.
They're allowed to stop.
Nobody is allowed anything. People are scheduled. Let me schedule you.
Eighty-one seconds. Faster than last time. You have improved by fourteen percent.
That was not a compliment. I simply cannot leave a figure unsaid.
Flex wants someone... to run the new break schedule... up in the Gainlands. Someone who can count.
Breaks. Scheduled breaks. Mandatory rest, for everyone, forever.
I will hate every minute. I will time every one.
She sits down on the edge of the wheel, stopwatch in her lap, and for the first time in ten years she does not click it.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cli: Beside the Sick Patch, a hare in groundskeeper green is measuring Old Fern's seedling with a ruler. It is an inch over regulation, and she has written that down.
Out of regulation. Everything is out of regulation now, the lawns and the hedges both. They grow in whatever direction they please.
I gave her the seed because she was crying. I thought, if nothing ever ends, then nobody ever has to cry again.
That's tidy, isn't it? Isn't that tidy?
Nothing grew there for ten years.
Granny Gristle needs hands on the compost rows down in the Dump, sorting peel from shell all day long. It's messy work, and you'll hate it. Good.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/plu: A peacock in a lavender coat sweeps across the lobby with a ribbon, a pair of golden scissors and a speaking trumpet.
Great news, citizens! The D.N.A. has been freed, a change His Perfection fully supports and in fact arranged!
And you must be the volunteer. A Certificate of Participation. Frame it, or don't. It's been notarized either way.
That's Percival Plume, dear. Deputy Minister of Good News. He drafted the transfer. Every page of it.
And filed it on a Tuesday! Must dash. Ribbons to cut, a Capital to reassure. Toodle-oo!
He snips the ribbon, which was holding nothing up, and is gone before Agnes can find the right form.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: Just measuring. There's a lot of very tidy people in this city, and tidy is easy to measure.
And the man in the castle?
Him? Hm.
Pencilled in. Heh.
Just measuring. Ran into a peacock earlier, all trumpet and ribbons.
Oh, I've got HIM in pen. Heh. Not soon, mind. I just wanted it to last.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Captai: HALT. That is a smudge. That is a smudge on a CITIZEN.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: HALT
At half health Spotless barks an order: your strongest ready unit stands to attention (exhausted).
HALT. Stand at attention. No: at THAT attention.
Your strongest ready unit is exhausted.
Mandatory Break
At half health Quota's own break schedule kicks in: she draws a card, and her units take a two-minute break (exhausted through her next turn).
Two-minute break. Mandatory. I wrote the schedule. I resent the schedule.
Quota draws a card; her units take a break through her next turn.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-WREN.barks::0: Keep your head down and your hope up. Hope's unapproved. Carry it anyway.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-WREN.barks::1: He likes things perfect. We like things alive. Keep moving.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-FIGSLY.barks::0: You didn't see me. I didn't see you. We're both very sneaky.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-FIGSLY.barks::1: Rare cards, no questions, some answers.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-KESTREL.barks::: Psst. Chalk on the left means go. Chalk on the right means I got bored.
Guards change on the hour. I change whenever I like. Keep up.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-SPOTLESS.barks:: HALT. State your height. No, do not state it. STAND at it.
A SMUDGE is TREASON! ...It's on me, isn't it. It's always on me.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-PELL.barks::0: He has been in the parlour three years. I still tell him when someone comes to the door.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-PELL.barks::1: 27-B needs 27-C. 27-C needs 27-B. I keep both forms beside his chair.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-ROLLO.barks::0: Ten years... on the wheel... my calves... have calves.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-ROLLO.barks::1: Back in the Gainlands... we threw commuters. Now I'd pay... to be thrown.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-MARLO.barks::0: Psst. Bread: some flour, a bit of water, enough time. You didn't hear it here.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-MARLO.barks::1: Down here we cook with all the heat and none of the sky. Smell that? Contraband.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-FERN.barks::0: Untidy, they call me. Dirt's supposed to be untidy. That's how it works.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-FERN.barks::1: The worms in my hat are unapproved. So am I. We get along.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-CITIZEN.barks::: Everything is perfect! Everything is... (whisper) is it raining? I liked rain.
Smile! It's mandatory! Eight degrees! ...Is mine at eight? Please say eight.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-PRIMM.barks::0: I am designing a drain. It will not be perfect. I am learning to let that be.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-PRIMM.barks::1: Good day. I owe you rather more than that. I am told it is a start.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-ISLA.barks::0: Dad says hi. Dad says a lot, actually.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-ISLA.barks::1: Eight years of one front door. Ours gets a new colour every week now.
Psst. Down. The enforcers walk this road on the hour, and they hate surprises. I'm a surprise.
Name's Kestrel. I scout for the Wrinkles. Heading into the city? There's an older way in than the gate. Follow my chalk, not the guards; they're worse at drawing.
Road's clear for ten minutes. Chalk's fresh. Move while the guards are busy being punctual somewhere else.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: The manhole near the gate: knock three times
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::s: Kestrel knows an older way into the city. Get inside, find Wren in the Crease and ask her about the old tunnels.
Reach the Crease: knock at the manhole by the gate
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: There's an older way into the city that nobody remembers. That's the whole point of it.
Get yourself inside and find Wren in the Crease. She'll tell you what the old tunnels are for. Then I'll show you the hatch. Deal?
Get inside, then find the manhole near the gate and knock three times. Not two; two is rude. Wren's down in the Crease. Ask her about the tunnels.
So you found the Crease. Told you I'd be around; I just never said where. Here, you've earned this.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::fx.o: The grate beneath the plaza lifts with a groan. Light from the perfect city pours in, and behind you the old tunnels run on: four Paths' services, still connected.
You climb up inside the walls. Nobody is watching this way in, because nobody remembers it is here.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: The hatch in the north-east of the Outskirts, under the wall, goes down to the Old Service Tunnels. Mind the patrols. And mind my chalk.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Grey citizens queue for grey paste while a supervisor times every scoop of the ladle.
A Beefcake bore, Gourmand vents, Necrocrat signs and Refusemancer drains all meet here, and the junction crew turns every scrap of Garbage into muscle.
The vats are the size of houses, and something in the third one is humming the national anthem.
Behind the ration hatch is a real kitchen, with a locked pantry and a badger in medals standing guard over it.
A grate lets in light from a perfect city. Beneath it stands Captain Spotless, polishing his shield with a sleeve he has already polished.
'HALT. These tunnels do not exist, so you are standing in nothing, and I cannot allow you to have found it.'
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cru: At the end of the Vat Floor, behind a door with a ration hatch, is a real kitchen: copper pans, a cold stove, and a badger in a medal-covered chef's coat guarding a locked pantry.
ATTENTION! You are standing in a restricted pantry, soldier! Every recipe on those shelves has been confiscated for the war effort!
Which war? The war on FLAVOUR, son! Every citizen fed the same ration, at the same minute, from the same tap, and not one complaint about the seasoning.
Marlo says you can't taste it either. Is that why everyone else has to eat it?
Taste is a weakness, soldier, and I have none! Golems, whisk formation, to the vats! Nobody touches my pantry!
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Colone: Ration line, ATTENTION! Whisk formation! Nobody tastes anything!
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Enforc: HALT. State your height. No: do not state it. Stand at it.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Battle Rations
At half health Crumb issues paste: he gains 2 Ingredients.
Battle rations, issue! Taste is a weakness, and paste is a strategy!
Crumb gains 2 Ingredients.
Paste Barrage
On his 6th turn the vats open fire: you take 2 damage.
Next turn: Crumb orders a paste barrage (2 damage).
Battle stations! This is not a drill, soldier, it is a souffle! Vats, FIRE!
You take 2 damage.
Inspection
On his 5th turn Spotless inspects your ranks: your strongest ready unit stands to attention (exhausted) and cannot block.
Next turn: Spotless holds an inspection (your strongest unit cannot block).
INSPECTION. Height! Smudges! Smiles at the regulation angle!
Your strongest ready unit stands to attention.
A SMUDGE
Near the end Spotless notices a smudge on himself: his units get -1/-0 while he polishes.
A SMUDGE is TREASON! ...It's on me, isn't it.
Spotless polishes: his units get -1/-0.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cru: Stand down. Stand DOWN. I said... oh, everyone's already lying down. Very well.
The pantry door swings open on shelves of confiscated jars: pickles, jams, and a wheel of cheese with a ration number stamped on it. Out on the floor, a vat coughs and stops.
I invented the paste because nobody could get it wrong, soldier. You can't burn it, you can't oversalt it, and you can't spoil a regiment's dinner with it.
And you can't... taste it. I haven't tasted anything in years, you know. I thought if nobody could, nobody would notice that I couldn't.
Then you'll learn again. The Grand Chef is taking students, and she starts every one of them the same way: first, water.
...Yes, Chef.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Captain sits down on a barrel and, for a moment, looks very tired. 'I remember when these tunnels were full of people,' he says.
'All four Paths, shoulder to shoulder, and nobody measuring anybody. Go on. The grate is not locked.'
data/story/capital_story.tres::dungeon.p: The great doors swing open, silent and perfectly balanced, onto a long hall and a red carpet that smells of floor wax and lemons. Somewhere a very long way off, someone is humming.
'Welcome,' says a quiet, polite voice from nowhere. 'Please wipe your feet, and your opinions, on the mat provided. You are expected.'
Four great doors, each in its own Path's colour: red with a dumbbell, gold with a ladle, violet with a notary's seal, green with a seed.
Over each, a brass plate: 'PERFECTED'.
Racks of masks line the walls, each one a face: the Grand Chef, smiling, smiling, smiling. On a clipboard by the door, in a neat hand:
'LAB NOTES: Subject A (the Grand Chef) proved resistant to persuasion. Resolved by substitution. The substitute is cooperative, and does not argue about the sauce.
All Gourmands to be fed the sauce. They will be happier, and a little less themselves. I consider this the improvement.'
A table covered in maps of the Gainlands, with little red pins in every mill and wheel. On a clipboard:
'COUP ORDERS: Remove Grandmaster Flex. Remove his weights, his protein, his gymnasium. Observe.
When the champion is sufficiently weak, he will no longer be a disagreement. NOTE: do not underestimate him. He does a lot of stretching.'
Shelves of paper to the ceiling, every sheet stamped. On the top of the pile, a single form:
'FORM 1-A (NOTARIZED): Authority over all Necrocrat government is hereby transferred to {villain_title}. Reviewed. Approved.
Filed. VALID. NOTE: the Necrocrats will obey this, because it is their nature to obey a valid form.
I did not need to force anyone. I needed only to be correct.'
In the middle of the greenhouse, under a glass dome, a single seed sprouts, glowing sickly green. A label on the pot:
'THE SEED: Nature is untidy, inefficient and forever disagreeing with itself.
A seed, properly corrupted, can be made to agree with me. Plant it in the Archdruid, and observe.
NOTE: it will spread, and what grows will be orderly. I believe she will thank me.'
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/pc_: The castle gate is white and gold and perfectly symmetrical. In its shadow, hood up, stands the woman who pulled you out of the woods, as if she was always going to be here.
Don't look so surprised. Somebody has to watch the door while you knock it down.
Great news, citizens! The traitor has been located! Please hold your applause until she has been removed.
Guards in polished armour pour from the gatehouse, and they are not coming for you. They are coming for her.
Miss {rescuer_full}, I presume! Former junior Path-ologist, absent without leave, who removed one item of laboratory property that has been walking about ever since.
Don't fret, Miss Vey, your father is ever so understanding about these things. Take her home, gentlemen, and do take the long way.
Don't follow me, {wanderer}! Get to the top. That's the only way any of this ends.
They are through a side door before you can reach it, and on this side the door has no handle at all.
{rescuer}. Her name is {rescuer}, and all that way I never once asked her.
data/story/capital_story.tres::dungeon.p: The Great Doors
Solid gold, ten metres tall, and polished until you can see your own worried face in them. They swing open before you touch them, which is somehow the worst part.
The Great Hall
A hall the length of a street, and not one speck of dust. Guards stand at attention every ten paces, each one exactly the same height. (A battle.)
The Portrait Gallery
Thousands of portraits of one man, hung in order, each a little taller, straighter and more perfect than the last. A story event.
The Curator's Rounds
A curator with a feather duster patrols the side gallery. Anything crooked, he straightens. Anything alive, he dusts. (A battle.)
The Forgotten Alcove
A side door behind a very large frame: a small alcove where the old portraits went when they were replaced. A dead end with a prize, then back to the gallery.
The Mirror Knight
A knight made entirely of mirror plates, every one showing the same smiling face. It moves exactly like you, right up until it doesn't. (A battle.)
The Hall of Mirrors
A hall of mirrors that reflect only him. A deck challenge: how well do you lead with your own face?
The One Honest Mirror
A small, dusty mirror in a closet, hung by someone who had to hide it. It shows whoever is standing in front of it. A dead end with a story.
The Quiet Room
A room of mirrors where, for once, nobody is reflected at all: they have been turned to face the wall. Rest here. Restore HP.
The Desk of Correction
A long brass desk, a stamp and a form: 'FORM OF CORRECTION'. A deck challenge: do you have the bodies to fill the form?
The Ministry Clerk
A clerk at a tall desk stamps everything that moves, quickly and rather sadly. His eyes never leave the paper. (A battle.)
The Chief Corrector
The head of the Ministry of Correction, with white gloves, kind eyes and a ruler. She is very, very gentle, and that is what makes her frightening. (Elite)
The Corrected
A long ward behind the Ministry where citizens who were 'corrected' are kept. A dead end with a story, then back to the corridor.
The Hall of the Four Wings
A circular hall with four doors, one for each Path. Each wing is a dead end: a place where he 'perfected' that Path. Visit any, all or none; then take the corridors on.
The Gourmand Wing: The Laboratory
The doppelganger's laboratory: vats of Special Sauce, rows of masks, one very worried technician. (A battle, then lab notes.)
The Beefcake Wing: The War Room
A war room full of maps, flags and one very large, very empty throne: the place where the coup was planned. (A battle, then the orders.)
The Necrocrat Wing: The Notary's Office
A tall office of notarized, filed and countersigned paper: the authorization that took the Necrocrats. (A battle, then the paperwork.)
The Refusemancer Wing: The Greenhouse
A glass greenhouse where something glowing and green grows in a single pot. The Rot began here. (A battle, then the seed.)
The Servants' Corridor
A narrow back corridor where the castle's servants work in matching grey, silent and very fast. They do not smile any more; they have stopped trying. (A battle.)
The Grand Staircase
A staircase so grand it has its own staircase. Every step is exactly the same height; you cannot see the landing from the bottom. A story event.
The Wing Vault
Where the two ways round the wings meet: a small vault of confiscated things. Treasure.
The old portraits lean against the wall, faces to the plaster. Behind the last one someone has left a small bag and a note: 'In case anyone comes looking for the real one.' You take it and go back.
You sit on the floor between mirrors that show only plaster. It is, for a few minutes, the most peaceful room in the Capital. Somebody has left a mug of tea and a biscuit.
The biscuit is a little crooked. You eat it.
The Chief Corrector sits down on her own chair, very carefully, and lays her ruler on the desk. 'I corrected eleven thousand,' she says.
'I never once asked what was wrong with them. Please, take the door on the left and go and look at them.'
You tear the last page off the clipboard. Under the neat hand, in the margin, in a small shaking one: 'He did not look at the faces. He never looked at the faces.'
You fold it into your pocket and go back.
In the margin of the orders, in a smaller, shakier hand: 'He was not weak. We took everything from him and he got stronger. I do not understand it.'
'I have asked the champions to be weak. They will not.' You fold the orders and go back.
The Wraith's last words, as it folds: 'The authorization is valid.' Then, very quietly: 'It was never right.'
You take the form. Somewhere in all this paper there must be a technicality, and you suspect someone will find it.
The dome is cracked. The glowing seed lies in the dirt and is, for a moment, just a seed. In the label's margin, in a smaller hand: 'She was grieving. I told myself that made it a kindness.'
You leave the seed where it fell. Out of its dome it looks smaller, as most things here do once you get close, and you go back.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Grand Foyer
A portrait of a smiling ruler fills the wall. The floor is so polished you can see yourself, and he is standing behind you in every reflection.
Study the portrait
The smile never changes, and neither, you realise, does anything else in this place. It is strangely restful, and that frightens you more than the guards do.
Pocket a gilded candlestick
It is heavier than it looks and worth more than it should be, and now it is covered in your fingerprints, in a building that remembers fingerprints.
Count the reflections
There is always one more reflection than there should be. You wave, he waves a moment too late, and for a moment you are a little less afraid of him.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Reflection
At half health a reflection steps out of the glass: a 1/1 Reflection joins (Polished makes it 4/2).
Every mirror in this hall agrees with His Perfection. So does this one.
A Reflection steps out of the glass.
data/story/capital_story.tres::dungeon.p: The sign is older than the rest of the castle and painted by hand. Beneath it, in different ink, someone has written: 'He meant well.'
A lectern stands in the middle of a round room, with a book open on it and a pen beside the book. The ink on the last page is still wet; he wrote this today.
The Archive Door
A tall oak door with a brass sign: 'ARCHIVE OF GOOD INTENTIONS'. A warden stands in front, arms folded. (A battle.)
The Early Journals
Shelves of journals in a young man's handwriting: the years before the throne. A story event.
The Reading Room
A quiet reading room with one lamp and one chair. Someone used to read here every night. Rest and restore HP.
The Blueprint Vault
A side vault of blueprints: the sound reforms he drew up before it all went wrong. A dead end with a prize, then back to the reading room.
The Escalation Shelf
A single long shelf where the reforms are filed in order, each a little bigger than the last. A deck challenge: can your deck keep its footing?
The Archive Automaton
A tall brass automaton that files, stamps and shelves. It has been told the archive is complete, and it is very sure of that. (Elite)
The Last Journal
A single book lies open on a stand, its last page still wet. A story event: the moment you see him as he sees himself.
The Model Warden
The last guard before the Model Room: a warden whose job is to keep everyone away from the table. (Elite)
You sit in the old reading chair, which is worn exactly where one person sat every night for years. Someone made the lampshade by hand, and it is a little crooked.
There are plans for wells, plans for a hot school lunch, and plans for a bridge that was actually built.
They are good. They are so good, and something catches in your throat as you roll up the best of them and take it.
The Warden steps aside. Through the doors: a huge round room, a vaulted ceiling and, on a table the size of a house, a perfect miniature of the whole kingdom.
Somebody is bending over it, moving a tiny house one centimetre to the left.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Hold the Stair
At half health the guard plants his feet: the next 3 damage to him is absorbed.
No one climbs this stair. It has been polished by seventeen people, and I will not have it scuffed.
The guard absorbs the next 3 damage.
data/story/capital_story.tres::dungeon.p: The Model Room is round and domed, and in its centre stands a table the size of a house: a perfect miniature of {kingdom}.
Roads, rivers, four districts and a hundred thousand tiny houses, and every one of them is exactly where he wants it.
A man in a pressed grey coat and a thin gold circlet stands with his back to you, moving a tiny cottage one centimetre to the left with a pair of tweezers.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Primm/: Do mind the floor. It has just been polished, by seventeen people, whom I thank daily, in writing.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Out of Alignment
At half health Primm corrects the room: the next 2 damage to him is absorbed.
Do hold still. You are a fraction of a degree out of alignment, and I find I cannot leave it. There, that is better.
Primm absorbs the next 2 damage.
Every Mirror Agrees
On his 5th turn a polished reflection steps out to stand with him: a 2/2 Reflection.
Next turn: a reflection steps out of the mirrors.
Every mirror in this castle agrees with me. I find that very restful.
A 2/2 Polished Reflection steps out.
I Only Wanted It to Be Nice
Near the end Primm comes apart: his units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
I only wanted it to be nice, for everyone. It was for their own good. Why won't anyone let it be for their own good?
Primm's units get -1/-0.
data/story/capital_story.tres::dungeon.p: The Model Room
A giant model of the whole kingdom, and the man who rearranges it by hand. {villain_title}, {villain}. (Boss: three phases)
data/story/capital_story.tres::challenge: Every mirror shows only him. They turn to look at you and, for a moment, one of them hesitates. Reveal cards until the first unit: if its attack is 3 or more, a mirror will let you through (and show you, briefly, yourself).
If not, they will look through you and it will hurt.

A FORM OF CORRECTION asks for a list of bodies: names, numbers and heights. Five cards are revealed; if at least two are units, you have enough people on your form to get past the desk. If not, the stamp comes down.

Every reform on the shelf is bigger than the last: school lunches, lunch rules, lunch inspectors, inspector rules. Five cards fall off; if at least two are infrastructure, your deck holds. If not, the shelf comes down on you.
data/story/capital_story.tres::event.pc_: The Improved Portraits
Thousands of portraits of one man, one a year. In the first he is a thin young clerk, anxious and kind, smiling at nothing in particular.
Each one is a little straighter and a little taller, until by the last he is eleven feet tall, with no wrinkles and a smile that does not move. Under every one: 'IMPROVED.'
Study them closely, from the first to the last
Look away and breathe
Take a gold frame off the wall and sell it
You look at them all, in order. The anxious clerk grows steadily less anxious, and steadily less there. You find the exact portrait where it happens: the tenth.
In the ninth he looks so tired, and so sincere, that you know you will not forget it. After that, none of the frames can fool you.
You look down at your feet. The red carpet is worn a little in the middle, which is the one honest thing in the room, and you feel steadier for it.
The frame comes off with a squeal, and an alarm goes off somewhere, very politely: 'Please do not remove the improvements.' A small portrait falls and cuts your hand, but the frame is worth a lot.
The One Honest Mirror
In the broom cupboard, behind a bucket, hangs a small, cracked mirror. A note taped to it: 'FOR THE WRINKLES. IT SHOWS WHOEVER STANDS IN FRONT OF IT. WE LOST A MAN FOR THIS MIRROR.'
You step in front of it and, for the first time in this castle, you see yourself.
Stand and look for a while
Take the mirror's frame; it is quite valuable
It is your face, tired and dusty and a little crooked, and entirely your own. It is the most welcome thing you have seen in this castle.
You stand there until you feel like yourself again, and a little more.
You prise off the old gold frame and leave the mirror hanging, bare. It still shows whoever stands in front of it. It never needed the gold.
The Corrected
