A long white ward holds fifty beds, and in each lies a citizen in a grey gown with a small, fixed smile, looking at nothing.
A nurse moves among them, adjusting each smile by a few degrees. One man has been smiling at the ceiling for three years. A woman in the corner has forgotten the name of her own daughter.
One of them whispers to you as you pass: 'I smiled at a funeral.'
Sit with them and listen
Free the nearest bed and help them out
Take the ward's record book as proof
You sit by the beds and listen for as long as it takes, which is a long time, and one by one they tell you their names.
You listen to what they smiled at: a funeral, a wedding, a bird. When you rise, you repeat their names to yourself.
You undo the straps and help a man to his feet. He weeps and laughs and falls over, and cannot remember how to frown. A nurse hits an alarm.
You carry him out through a window. He is heavier than you expected, and it costs you something, though it has cost him far more.
He says: 'Thank you.' It is the first thing he has said in three years.
The record book lists every citizen corrected, their offence and the angle of their smile on admission. It is eleven thousand pages long. You will not need to read it all.
The first page is enough. Somebody will pay well for this book, and somebody, one day, will read it aloud.
The Hall of the Four Wings
Four great doors in four Path colours, and over each a brass plate: PERFECTED. Behind each, you can hear nothing at all. A fifth and sixth way lead on: the servants' corridor and the grand staircase.
You could visit all four wings, or none. Each wing is a dead end, and each one will tell you how he did it.
Rest on the bench in the hall
Take the coins from the collection plate by the door
You sit on a long bench under a brass plate and breathe. The doors do not open. Nothing in the hall moves, and everything in it seems to be listening. After a time you feel steadier.
A little brass plate for donations to {villain_title}, bolted to the wall. It is quite full. You take the lot.
It is, after all, other people's money. They would want it back.
The Grand Staircase
A staircase of five hundred steps, every one exactly the same height, and at the top a very large clock.
Halfway up, a servants' door stands ajar: through it, a narrow plain stair with worn steps. Nobody has ever climbed the grand staircase for pleasure.
Climb the grand staircase, step by identical step
Sit on a step and rest
Take the servants' stair
Five hundred identical steps. By the three hundredth you are trembling; by the four hundredth you want to scream.
At the top, a pot of coins sits on the landing: a tip left by the last person who made it. You rub your legs and pocket the coins.
You sit on step two hundred and fifty and look up at the very large clock. It has no hands, only a brass plate that says 'ON TIME'.
You sit there for as long as you like. Nobody comes to correct you.
The servants' stair is steep and narrow and wonderfully uneven. Every step is a different height. A cook has left a little shelf of bread and a pipe.
You eat and climb and feel, curiously, much better about the whole world.
The Early Journals
A wall of journals in a young man's neat handwriting, each one dated. 'Year 1: Wells. Half the lower city has to walk two miles for clean water.
I have drawn up plans for six new ones, and the Council has approved every one. I did not sleep at all. It was wonderful.'
'Year 3: School lunches. A child asked me why the soup was warm. I said, so that you can eat it.
She said, that is the best idea anyone has ever had. I put it in a frame.'
It goes on like that for years, and they are good. They are so good.
Read the first journals, all the way through
Close the book and sit with it for a moment
You read until the light changes. Wells, schools, bridges, lamps: he built a hundred good things, and he loved every one.
Once, he was exactly the person you would want running a kingdom. You close the last journal very gently.
You close the book and rest your hand on the cover. It is warm, as if someone had just put it down. You breathe, and wait until your hands are steady.
The Last Journal
The last page, in a neat hand, the ink still wet: 'Today I corrected eleven more. They cried, which is understandable. They do not yet see it.
In ten years' time they will thank me. In a hundred, they will not remember there was anything to thank me for. That is the point. That is how you know it has worked.
I am so tired. I do not think anyone has ever tried so hard to be kind. I only wish somebody would say so.'
Read it all again, and let it settle
Close the journal and steady yourself
You read it twice. He believes every word: that each portrait and each rule is a gift, that nobody has ever tried so hard to be kind.
He is not lying, and that is the worst of it. You understand him a little now, and you understand exactly what you will have to do.
You close the book softly. Whatever is in the next room, it is not a monster. It is a man who needed to be right, and made the whole world pay for it.
You breathe in, and out, and you go on.
Ah, a visitor. Do come in; I so rarely receive anyone who has not been summoned.
Mind the floor: it has just been polished, by seventeen people, whom I thank daily, in writing.
I am {villain_title}, {villain}: Minister of Improvements, Steward of the Throne, Protector of {kingdom}.
You have walked the whole length of my castle. You have, I notice, scuffed it.
Sorry, that's forest mud. I've walked a long way to get here, and everyone I met on the road was afraid of you.
Afraid? Of order, perhaps, or of comfort, or of the dreadful burden of being safe?
I have given them roofs, and hats, and rules, and I have given each of them exactly the same amount of each, which is more than anyone before me ever managed.
Every one of them has a number, so that nobody is ever overlooked. Do you know how few kingdoms can say that? I do. I counted.
Ten years I have been mending this kingdom. Ten years, and still you come, with your different hats and your different opinions, to undo the only good thing anyone has ever done.
I am afraid I shall have to correct you.
This will not hurt. It will, however, be Standard.
Why... why will they not all be three? It is a perfectly good number.
Every unit was to be equal, in every way. Why must some of them be five? Why must anything ever be five?
Because some things are five. Some people are.
You took ten years from me, and whatever you took, it was not the part that matters. Strength is what you do with what's left, and strength is not control.
Because some things are five. Some people are.
You took ten years from me. I don't know everything you took, but I know it wasn't the part that matters.
Then they must be made the same, for their own good. I had rather hoped that you, of all people, would see that.
You are not listening; nobody ever listens. (a breath) Very well. If you will not follow my rules, I shall simply have to use yours.
Everything you can do, I can do. I have had ten years of practice with it.
Let us see how you like fighting yourself.
Your cards, your plays, your very own deck, held in my hands and played rather more tidily than you ever played it.
And still you beat me. I should very much like to know how.
You copied my cards, but what I do with them is mine. A name is a blank page until you sign it.
And nobody files me under 'subject' ever again. No order you could write outranks treating people with respect.
You copied my cards. You can't copy what I do with them.
My name is mine to sign. You don't get to decide who I am.
You copied my cards, but what I do with them is mine. A name is a blank page until you sign it.
Copying a face never made anyone a cook. You don't get to decide who I am.
You copied my cards. You can't copy what I do with them.
Nobody files me under 'subject' ever again. No order you could write outranks treating people with respect.
That is simply not true. I made the wells, and I made the roads.
I made... (he stops.) I made a list of things other people had already built, and I put my name on it.
No. No, no, no. The rules are perfect. I checked every one of them myself, twice.
The rules are perfect. They have to be, because if they aren't, then I have been... then all this time I have been...
Everything is coming apart, and I don't understand why. I only wanted it to be nice.
data/story/capital_story.tres::boss.phas: Every unit, yours and his, starts as a 3/3; buffs and debuffs still change it. You may play at most two non-infrastructure cards a turn. (Two is the perfect number.)
His deck is a copy of yours, and he draws an extra card each turn. He can only imitate; he has never created anything.
His units get +1/+1 and he draws an extra card each turn, but he loses 1 HP at the start of each of his turns. The rules he wrote are breaking down.
data/story/capital_story.tres::boon.beef: Grandmaster Flex steps out from behind a pillar, unwinding a very small bandage from a very large arm. 'Breathe in. Hold.'
'Strength is the heart and the mind, son, and you brought both. We're with you.' (Grandmaster Flex's Heart: Beefcake units get +1 power, and you gain 2 max HP.)
data/story/capital_story.tres::boon.gour: The Grand Chef, in a clean apron, ladle in hand. 'Have you eaten? No, of course you haven't. Here. Eat first, fight after.'
'Ten years of sauce that tasted of nothing. Let's feed this kingdom something real again.' (The Grand Chef's Feast: Gourmand units get +1 defense, life gain is stronger, and you gain 2 max HP.)
data/story/capital_story.tres::boon.necr: Agnes Overdue floats forward with her enormous ribboned stack of denied appeals. 'I have found a technicality, dear,' she says, and stamps it with the department seal.
'It applies to him, dear. It applies to him very well.' (Agnes's Appeal: Necrocrat cards cost 1 less, and you gain 2 max HP.)
data/story/capital_story.tres::boon.refu: Archdruid Compostella kneels and presses a palm to the marble. A small green shoot pushes up through the polish.
'To grow, you have to let things go, child. Even him. Especially him.' (Compostella's Roots: Refusemancer units get +2 defense, and you gain 2 max HP.)
data/story/capital_story.tres::boon.none: Nobody stands beside you. The Paths are not free yet, and their leaders are still held behind wheels and sauce and paperwork and thorns, so you step into the chamber alone.
(Free the Paths and their leaders will stand with you.)
data/story/capital_story.tres::dungeon.p: The model lies in pieces, a hundred thousand tiny houses scattered across the floor in all the wrong places, and somehow they look better.
{villain} sits among them, small, in his pressed grey coat, and does not move for a long time.
...So it is over. I wrote such good rules, and they were not enough.
I did it for them, for the people. You do see that, don't you?
You must see that. Every rule, every portrait, every hat: so that nobody would ever be afraid again. So that nobody would ever be wrong.
You kept every face and every house. Nothing grows if you refuse to let anything go.
You took my mother and father, and I can't even remember their faces. I'm not going to keep that under glass the way you keep everything. I'm letting it go.
You kept every face and every house. Nothing grows if you refuse to let anything go.
You took my mother and father, and I can't even remember their faces. I'm letting it go anyway. Watch me.
...(a long silence)... I made them smile. I made them all smile.
And they smiled, and they smiled, and I looked at their faces, and I thought: they look like me. And I was so happy.
It was the mirrors, wasn't it? I wanted a world where nothing could ever surprise me.
And I forgot that a world where nothing surprises you is a world with nobody else in it.
I'm not going to correct you; that was always your way. Start smaller than that. Say sorry to one person.
One? I corrected eleven thousand. Where would I even begin? I cannot remember a single one of their names.
Take the crown. No: leave it. No: take it.
It is very heavy. It was always very heavy. And tell the Wrinkles... tell them I am sorry about the hats.
data/story/intro_story.tres::still.primm: The mirrors crack one by one, and for the first time in ten years {villain} sees himself in them.
There is no crown and no perfect smile, only a tired man kneeling above a very small kingdom.
Light pours in through the broken glass. It does not feel like winning. It feels like the end of a long, quiet lie.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Doppelganger's Lab Notes
A lab table of food notes: a shapeshifter's recipe for becoming a Grand Chef, with an entire page on how to smile like her. The margins are full of practice smiles.
Read the notes
It explains everything, including why the sauce tastes of nothing. There is no Grand Chef in here, only a very good understudy.
Take the samples
Somebody downstairs will pay for them and nobody upstairs will miss them, which is as much of a plan as you need.
Practise the smile in the mirror
The smile comes out perfect, which is horrifying, and your face stays like that for a while. The guards leave you alone.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/pc_: The Necrocrat wing's archive is paper from floor to ceiling. On the desk, under a paperweight shaped like a peacock, lies a memo, the ink still wet.
MEMO. To: His Perfection. From: P. Plume. Re: the leak in the lab. The junior Path-ologist has been returned to the Path-ology Lab beneath the forest, to her father. Handled. Promotion?
Ah! You found my memo. Isn't it well written? I used the active voice.
Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News. I drafted the transfer of the D.N.A., notarized it, filed it, and read it out on every loudspeaker in the land.
Where is this Lab? Where did you take her?
Beneath the forest where you... oh, I shouldn't have said that. Never mind. Great news: your visit is being declined!
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Perciv: Smile, please! This fight is being broadcast, and you are losing it beautifully.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Positive Spin
At half health Plume announces that he is fine: he heals 2.
Great news, citizens! I have been approved to feel fine!
Plume heals 2.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/pc_: This is a setback. A temporary, fully reversible, not-at-all-my-fault setback.
I'll draft a statement. 'Minister Plume bravely withdrew.' Yes. Bravely.
He withdraws, bravely, at a run. You fold the memo into your pocket, and two phrases go with it: beneath the forest, and her father.
data/story/capital_story.tres::dungeon.p: The Path-ologists' records are pinned to every door. 'SUBJECT 1, the Royal Asset. Drain cycle 3,114.
Power stable, routed to the Throne. {villain}'s hold depends on it. Do not allow the Subject to leave.'
You read the word Subject until it stops being a word.
The oldest notes, at the far end, are in a different hand: careful, rounded, familiar. 'Observation, Year 1. The child is not a specimen. He asks for his mother. I am leaving the lab. M.'
You have seen that handwriting on a pie recipe.
The Correction Ward
A long ward of white cells. Free the prisoners for a boon, and read what the Path-ologists wrote.
A single portrait hangs in a gilt frame, lit like a shrine: a royal family of three.
The king and the queen have been painted over in white, so carefully that every brushstroke runs the same way. Only the boy between them was left untouched.
A small card on the frame, in a neat hand: 'KEPT FOR REFERENCE.' The boy has your face.
You stand there a long time. Your throat has closed, and you cannot say why.
{villain}'s Private Gallery
A small gallery behind a mirror, which nobody is allowed to clean. A dead end with a prize.
Behind the frame, a hidden hatch holds a small bag. You take it, and you do not look back at the portrait, because if you do you will not be able to leave.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: The Hour Strikes
On its 4th turn the clock strikes: your two strongest ready units are exhausted and cannot block that turn.
Next turn: the hour strikes (your two strongest units cannot block).
BONG. The hour has been standardized. All movement will now cease.
The hour strikes: your two strongest ready units are exhausted.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Garden of Uniform Flowers
A thousand identical flowers stand in identical rows. You count them twice. One of them is, very slightly, a different shade of yellow.
Pick the odd one out
It tastes of dandelion. It feels like the first honest thing in the castle.
Pick a handful of the rest
They wilt in your hand and leave behind a few coins, which is more than they should have been able to do.
Plant something crooked
You press a bent stem into the soil. The gardener will find it tomorrow and have to rethink everything. You walk on, lighter.
data/story/capital_story.tres::hud.objec: The Capital is free. The facade is down, the rifts are closed and the citizens are saying whatever they like, mostly to each other. The Crease is open to everybody.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ui.exit.b: Leaving the Capital ends this visit, and Town heals you fully. Nobody will ask for an exit permit on the way out; the road is just a road again.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.main_d: The doors of {villain}'s Castle stand open, and the gold is flaking off them. A pigeon has built a nest in the crown above the lintel, and nobody has asked it for a permit.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.wake.f: You wake on a cot in the Crease. Nurse Hesper Dray looks up from her clipboard as if she has been expecting you for some time.
'You fell over, so we rolled you in. The fee's still yours, mind. The tea isn't free just because the kingdom is.'
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.be: The lights are back on: the street lamps burn, the lifts run, the tunnels are open again, and the Beefcakes' wheels, free at last, turn for everyone.
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.go: The food stalls have reopened: awnings, steam, lanterns, real food. Healing items work again, and the stomachs of the Capital are not quite so empty.
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.ne: The cemetery is calm: graves are tended, the permit loop has been broken, and the dead are finally allowed to lie down.
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.re: The heaps are smaller and greener. Things are being composted again and the Reek smells, very faintly, of flowers.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.gate: Everybody is welcome. Conditions: none. Please do not feed the pigeons.
1. Be of whatever height you are.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.faca: Now: some houses, a very tidy lawn and a lot of citizens who would like to go home.
Somebody has crossed out BY PERMIT and written BY SURPRISE.
(somebody has written 'when you feel like it' underneath, in small neat letters)
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.cast: Under new management. The new management is: all of us, arguing.
The tears are sealed. The pigeons have moved in, and they are staying.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.plaz: Proceed however you like. There is a very large statue; it is lying down.
You did it. Sit down a moment. I'm Wren, Royal Archivist, and for ten years I kept the only honest record in this city.
The Crease is just a cellar now, but we're keeping it. Too many true things were written down there to let it go.
Thank you. I mean that more than I have ever meant a footnote.
The kingdom is mending one argument at a time, and it's dreadfully inefficient. I've never been happier. Take your time.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.fig.i: Fig Sly, formerly purveyor of contraband. Now: purveyor of things. It is a much less exciting job.
The margins are better. Take a look.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.fig.r: Still selling. Nobody arrests me. It is horrible. I miss the thrill.
Old Fern, composter, and I'm allowed to say so out loud now.
The patch came in, the heaps are steaming, and nobody's thumped me for it in a week. I'm untidy, and I'm proud of it.
Smell that? Honest compost. I could cry, but it'd be a waste of good water. Come back any time.
I'm Widow Pell. My husband is finally at rest, and I visit him every morning, the way I always meant to.
Thank you. I will never say it enough, so I keep saying it.
We're well. My husband would have said you were late. He'd have meant it fondly.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.rollo: Rollo Spokes. The wheels are slow, and the crews are sitting in the sun, lifting nothing. Best I've ever seen them look.
We're lifting again, real things and on purpose this time. Come and watch the crews, and bring a snack.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.marlo: Chef Marlo. Chef. Say it with me. The stalls are open and the food is real.
And chaotic, I'll grant you. There's flour on the ceiling, and I've never been so happy to see a mess.
Come and eat. 'Some' of everything. If you ask how much, I shall have to demonstrate.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.spotl: I don't measure anyone any more; I simply stand here. Yesterday a man walked by at exactly the approved height, and I wept, and I could not tell you why.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.patie: Citizen... no. My name is Aldous.
I smile now, when I want to. It comes out crooked, and my wife says it's the best thing she's ever seen.
It's Aldous. Still crooked, but I'm practising.
data/story/capital_story.tres::facade.ci: Good day! A good day! The weather is whatever it wants!
I don't know the approved hat size and I don't care! It's wonderful to be alive.
I am going to wear a hat of any size. Maybe two at once.
I blinked twice just now, and nobody came to write it down.
The bakery's only painted on, but there's going to be a real one as soon as someone learns to bake. I have a recipe. It says: try.
My name is Berta! I'd forgotten it. It was on the tip of my tongue for ten years.
Berta. Berta. Berta. It is a very good name.
My house is different from my neighbour's now, because he's painted his purple. I'm furious about it, and I'm so happy to be furious.
I painted my door green. Do you like it? Please say no, so I can have an argument.
I still go round the back and look at the wall sometimes. It's a good wall, and it's only a wall.
I smiled at a funeral yesterday, and nobody corrected me. It was a good funeral.
I cried and smiled and it was exactly right.
My cheeks do not hurt any more. My cheeks are mine.
I'm not going to smile at all today unless I want to, and I'm enjoying it enormously.
The hedge is round because it wanted to be round. I asked it myself, and I didn't have to submit a form.
Visitors come! Real ones! They are mostly confused, but they come.
The loudspeaker's gone quiet. I stood under it for an hour and said my own name out loud, just because I could.
Spontaneity every day! I am exhausted! I am not sure I like it! I love it!
I said hello to the bird again. I have named the bird Thursday.
Now that every day is Spontaneity Thursday, I don't know what to do with any of them.
My daughter came home in her little green hat. I've never loved a hat more in my life.
Every hat size! All of them! Come and see the hats!
I'm not going to be polite today, I'm going to be honest: your hat is awful, and I love it.
I opened the back door and it was raining, so I stood out in it for an hour.
The Showcase isn't the best of all places any more. It's just a place, and it's mine, and it's a good one.
I'm going to go somewhere else, just to see what it's like. Then I'll come back, if I want to.
He wasn't kind, he was afraid, and for ten years none of us could tell the difference.
I'm not sure I forgive him, and I'm not sure I need to.
The portraits are coming down. There is a lot of wall behind them. Nobody knows what to put there.
He's gone, so I looked away from his portrait for a whole minute. It was a very long minute.
data/story/capital_story.tres::facade.do: The front door is still painted on. Someone has written under the knocker: 'Come round the back, we have a kettle.'
The painted window now has a real curtain, hung over it by a citizen who wanted one. The family in the painting has acquired a moustache.
The door has a handle now, and the house has an inside: two chairs, a table, a tea tray. The paintbrush has been left on the ladder, for good.
The closet is just a closet now. A sign inside says: IF YOU ARE READING THIS, YOU DO NOT HAVE TO SMILE.
data/story/capital_story.tres::facade.sp: Attention, citizens. (a cough) The weather is no longer approved; it is just weather, and it seems to be managing on its own.
Please do whatever you like. That is all.
Attention, citizens. A reminder: you do not have to smile. (a pause) Also: you may smile. We are very easy.
Attention, citizens. A pigeon is using the loudspeaker. Please stand by.
Attention, citizens! Hats of any size are now permitted. Hats of negative size remain under review.
Attention, citizens. He was afraid, and we were afraid of him. Please be gentle with yourselves.
Attention, citizens! Spontaneity Thursday is now every day. You may stop rehearsing your surprise.
Attention, citizens. The exits are open, and so, it turns out, are the entrances.
The walls are still walls. Please do not run into them.
Attention, citizens. All is not well yet, but it will be.
It is a lot of work. Thank you for helping.
Attention, citizens. The Wrinkles were real all along, and they kept the true record. Please thank them.
They are in the cellar. There is tea.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.guard: I used to measure people. Now I just look at them. A man walked past yesterday who was nine feet tall and I said 'good morning'.
I am not myself. I am much better.
Come in, come in. Bring any height.
Queue management. There's no queue any more, so I'm only standing here out of habit.
Nobody's told me where else to stand, so I thought I might go for a walk. If that's... no. I'm not asking permission, I'm telling you. I think.
Still no queue. I am doing very well.
Exit control. You may leave whenever you like; I'm only standing here. It's a very open exit.
Exit control. Goodbye. Come back. Goodbye.
Exit control. This is an exit. It is also an entrance. It is, from every angle, a door.
A door. A good door.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.exit_: Exit Interview Booth. Name? Reason for leaving?
...I was never going to read the answers. Please go and have a nice day.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.hespe: My tea's still unapproved, but then nothing's approved any more. Best thing that ever happened to it.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/mar: Sit down, dearie. Word came from the Capital this morning, and you won't like it.
Plume's men took a girl at the castle gate, the one who carried you out of the woods. {rescuer_full}, they called her.
I knew whose girl she was the day she brought you to my door. Her father worked in my laboratory once, and I never trusted her for a minute because of it.
I've been wrong about people before. Once, in 1987. It seems I've gone and done it twice.
Back where she came from, I expect: somewhere with glass walls and no windows. That's a door I can't open for you. Not yet.
Eat. You'll want your strength for when it opens.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/wre: We saw them take her at the gate: four guards and a peacock with a speaking trumpet. We couldn't get anywhere near her.
The Wrinkles are watching every door out of that castle. If they move her again, we'll know.
Her name goes in the true record, whatever else happens.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ending.be: The Model Falls
The scale model cracks in half, and then the table under it, and then, with the sound of a very large drawer being pulled from a very large cabinet, the castle walls begin to come down.
In the gallery a portrait slips off its hook and lands face-up. For the first time in ten years, nobody picks it up.
The Facade Falls
In {showcase}, a painted door falls flat, and a very surprised citizen steps through it onto a very real street.
Shopfronts topple, hedges slump back into their own shapes, and the loudspeakers cough once and go quiet.
Behind the facade are houses, lawns and people, all of them a little crooked. At the gate, a child paints the new sign: PATHORDIA.
The Rifts Close
Across the Capital the rifts fold up like letters. In the Reek, the Sick Patch is a flower bed.
In Grave Row, a family walks slowly to a quiet plot and stays. In the Transit Yards the wheels slow, and slow, and stop, and the crews lie in the sun.
In the Hungry Quarter, somebody lights a stove.
The Wrinkles
The Wrinkles climb up out of the Crease, blinking, into a light they had forgotten. Wren carries the true records under her arm. Nurse Hesper has brought the tea.
Fig Sly comes up out of the Crease already selling something, to somebody, for some reason. Nobody stops him.
The Paths Meet
And the Paths come home. Grandmaster Flex, the Grand Chef, Agnes Overdue and Archdruid Compostella meet in the plaza and look at one another for the first time in ten years.
The Beefcakes are late, the Necrocrats have brought a form, the Gourmands are overdressed, and the Refusemancers smell faintly of compost.
Nobody agrees on anything. It is the happiest sound the Capital has ever heard.
Together
{villain} demanded one way for everyone. It was never what made the kingdom strong.
Muscle and stoves, records and soil: each was good alone. Together they ran a kingdom, argued about it every day, and it worked.
The point was never to be the same; the point was the argument. Different Paths, working together.
The New Decree
A new decree appears on the plaza wall of {pathordia}, in four different handwritings. It reads: DIFFERENT PATHS MAY MIX AGAIN.
Somebody has crossed out MAY and written SHOULD. Somebody else has crossed out SHOULD and written WILL, IF THEY FEEL LIKE IT. A pigeon sits on the full stop.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ending.cr: A game about a kingdom that was strong because it was not the same.
Art: Kenney, KayKit, game-icons.net and friends (see CREDITS.md)
{villain}'s rule is over. The voices of the kingdom remain.
In memory of Form 27-B, Form 27-C and Form 27-B
No hats were harmed. Several were enlarged.
The Paths will be back, in some other order.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ending.re: You are back in {pathordia}. The streets are mostly the same, but they sound quite different now: people are shouting at each other cheerfully, in every direction.
Wren sits on the edge of the fountain with a ledger on her knee, writing the title of the first honest page: THE TRUE RECORD, VOLUME ONE.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.ending: The Capital is free. The postgame begins: decks of three or more Paths are now allowed.
data/story/capital_story.tres::freed_npc: Breathe in. Hold. ...Feel that? That is a city with nowhere it has to be.
Rollo's crews are lying in the sun, because I told them rest is a rep and they believed me. You used heart and mind both, son. That's the whole lift.
The sauce is gone from every stove in the kingdom, and I'm cooking with real onions again. I haven't cried this much since I was a girl.
Sit. Eat. You did something worth putting your name to, and you look as if you haven't had a proper meal since.
I have filed a Form of Gratitude, dear. It was approved on the first attempt. Irregular.
I think I'm going to cry, dear. I've wanted to for a very long time.
Look at this crack in the marble, child. Something's growing out of it.
I'm going to let it. It's earned the right, and so have you.
...You do not even know, do you? Look at you. You have walked my castle for hours and you have not once asked why my portraits stop at eleven.
...What do you mean?
I kept your face. I kept it for ten years, in the one gallery I never let anyone clean. It is the only face I could not improve.
You are the Royal Asset. You are the boy who got out. You are {prince_full}, and you have been so very hard to find.
...That's not possible. I would remember.
Your power has kept this kingdom lit for ten years, and I have only ever looked after it. Surely you can see that.
Come. You may as well see it used properly.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ending.be: The Pathwork Throne
The castle does not fall; it opens. Where the Model Room floor was, a stair of four colours winds down into the old heart of the Capital.
At the bottom stands the Pathwork Throne: four seats grown into one, four colours woven as a single thread. It was never {villain}'s.
You sit, and the Throne answers. It knows you.
Everything comes back at once: the lullaby, the glass, the throne room, the name. {prince_full}. And the Paths, all four, as they were always meant to be carried.
{villain} Sees
{villain} sits among the pieces of his model. As the Paths settle, he sees the kingdom as it is, and not as his reflection.
Cracked streets, real faces, and a boy he kept in a cell.
Slowly, he understands how much he broke. The wells were good, and so were the schools, but he made one choice for everyone, and nobody will trust him with another.
File Complete
Agnes Overdue floats up to the old transfer file, finds the heir clause and, with great ceremony, brings down her stamp: HEIR: ALIVE. FILE COMPLETE.
Maren pushes through the crowd, tortoise-slow, and stops in front of you. There is flour on her sleeve.
'{prince},' she says. It is the first time anyone has said it aloud and meant it. 'Welcome home.'
data/story/capital_story.tres::freed_npc: Do not look so alarmed. The guard is very kind, and the workshop has a very nice window.
I am designing a water main. A real one: pipes, a pump and nothing clever. It is the first thing I have made in ten years that nobody had to agree to.
I am not permitted to speak of the Paths, or to touch one. I find that I do not miss it. I find that I miss the wells.
He is allowed visitors, one at a time, ten minutes, no mirrors. Those are the rules. I did not write them, and I find I do not mind them.
He designs very good drains, it turns out. Do not tell him I said so.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: Ah. You did it, then, the castle and all.
Then I've two graves to finish properly, up in Grave Row in the city. Come by when you're ready. No rush; there never is, with me.
Back again! Walked them all the way home, I did. Lovely evening for it.
What are you writing?
Appointments. Let's see now... you're not down for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/isl: Someone is walking down the imperial road in faded pastel regulation clothes, a bedroll over one shoulder. Brannoch has stopped writing in his notebook.
Hi, Dad. I know. I should have written.
Eight years. Kept the gate open every night, in case.
They had us painting the same front door for eight years. Every time I asked to leave, the form came back "pending".
...You've got your mother's curls. Still can't keep a ribbon in them.
And your nose. Mum always said that was the unlucky part.
Wrote you in the book. Every day. "Isla. Not yet."
You're the one who knocked the castle over? That 'Hm' was Dad saying thank you. Thank you from me, too.
I keep walking to the gate and back. Nobody stops me. I keep expecting somebody to stop me.
Dad oiled the hinges this morning. It doesn't even lock. He just likes the sound of it opening now.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/roy: Grave Row, at dusk. At the end of the identical rows stand two new headstones, and they are not identical. Someone has carved them by hand: a crown, a harp, four colours in a ring.
Half the city has come, and nobody told them to. Wren holds the true record; Maren holds a pie she has forgotten she is carrying.
Ten years I've been digging these two. Slowly. I didn't want to finish before they could be visited properly.
Two forms, filed ten years ago, stamped by me. And a third, for a little boy, that I never had the heart to file.
I'm tearing that one up now, dear. With great pleasure.
He used to say the Paths argued like family. She used to say that was the point.
A warm wind comes up the row, out of season. Two figures stand by the headstones, the way people stand in a doorway when they are leaving and not sorry to.
Look at you. You came home.
Carry them gently, love. All four of them.
She hums the first bars of the lullaby, and does not need to finish it. You know the rest.
Right then, Your Majesties. Mind the step. It's a long one, but it's downhill all the way.
And you, Agnes. I've had you down for this a very long time.
One more week, Hob. Prudence needs a proper handover, and somebody has to explain the new handbook to Mortimer.
When you look again there are two headstones, a top hat bobbing away down the row, and a great deal of warm wind.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/bra: Notebook's full of her name, so I've started a new one. First page says yours. Spelled it right, this time.
data/story/intro_story.tres::still.reuni: In the Capital's square the leaders of the four Paths clasp hands, and several people in the crowd begin to cry.
Four banners fly from the same pole. It is a little crowded, and nobody minds.
At the edge of the crowd, a hooded traveler smiles, leaves still in their hair. There is always another path.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ending.po: With {villain} gone, the Paths are free to mix again. Your decks may now combine cards from ALL Paths, and the Alchemist's tri-Path crafting is open. What made the kingdom strong was never sameness.
Decks may now use 3 or more Paths.
The Alchemist's cauldron now takes three Paths at once: brew their essence into a tri-Path card.
{pathordia} is open to everyone: the facade is down, the rifts are sealed, and {villain} works under guard on wells and pipes, kept away from every Path.
{villain} is gone, and the Paths are shouting at each other in the street again. I have never been so glad to be annoyed.
The Capital is open to everyone now, and your decks may mix any Paths you like. Go and see what you can make of it, dearie. Then come home and eat.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.object: {villain} has fallen and the Paths are free to mix. Build decks from three or four Paths at once, try the Alchemist's tri-Path crafting, test yourself in the Undercroft and visit the changed Capital.
data/story/intro_story.tres::postgame.re: You came back for me. Down there, on purpose. I'm going to need a while to stop being cross about it.
Finish it, Tess. I'll be here. I've had a lot of practice waiting in this forest.
The Lab is quiet. For the first time in ten years I can hear the trees from down there.
Dad is in {town}, listening to Maren. She let him have one slice of pie. One. I've never seen him so frightened.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: Only the worthy reach the top, they say. The worthy also bring water, if they've any sense.

There's a mountain behind the station... and a barbell on top older than the regime. Older than me, nearly. Bring me a protein shake from the stand and I'll show you the way. Can't climb on an empty cup.
Water, friend. A protein shake from the stand will do. Don't spill it. I spilled one, the Festival year... where was I.
That's the best water I've ever seen. Thank you. Rule one: never lift alone. Rule two... rule two was water.
Mount Swolympus is open at last. Take the trail behind the station, and mind the thin air up top... never gets enough credit, thin air.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The mirror at the castle door, cracked from the inside. Beyond it the air is cold and smells of polish.
An Echo of Vivienne Quota, timing you to the second. Enemy units here enter with +1 attack.
A stone colossus sits at the summit with its palms turned up, waiting for a barbell. It has been spotting for a thousand years, and it is very, very ready.
'Lift,' it rumbles. 'I will catch it. I have always caught it.'
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::The An: One more rep. There is always one more rep.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: One More Rep
At half health the Spotter catches the weight: it heals 4.
Lift. I will catch it. I have always caught it.
The Ancient Spotter heals 4.
Young Spotters
On its 6th turn two 1/1 Young Spotters climb up to help it.
Next turn: two Young Spotters climb up the mountain.
Never lift alone. Not even me.
Two 1/1 Young Spotters arrive.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Weight of Glass
A barbell of solid mirror rests on a rack, and in every plate you see Clench at the height of his reign, lifting it easily. The rack has a little brass sign: FOR THE WORTHY.
Lift it anyway
It's heavier than anything you've lifted, because it's made of everything he wanted to be. Your arms shake, then hold. Something in the glass looks away first.
Leave it on the rack
You walk past. For the rest of the gallery, every reflection you pass is lifting it for you, slightly better.
Break it for the silver
The bar shatters into coins that are still warm. One of your cards goes with it, caught in the glass.
The Ancient Spotter lowers its hands and, for the first time in a thousand years, sets something down. The barbell on the altar is yours.
'One more rep,' it says. Then, quieter: '...That was the one. Thank you for coming up.'
An Echo of Chancellor Clench, at the height of his reign. He starts with Iron already in hand.
An Echo of Percival Plume, with perfectly good news. From here on the first card you play each turn costs 1 more.
The Valid Reflection
A mirror in a gilt frame holds a form already filled in with your name, your Path and a box marked 'Approved'. A pen waits on a chain. The ink is still wet.
Sign it
The mirror stamps you APPROVED. You feel sturdier and a little less like yourself.
Refuse to sign
The frame lets out a long, disappointed sigh, and the glass at your back cuts you on the way past.
Sign someone else's name
You sign 'Agnes Overdue'. The mirror has no answer to that and quietly pays you to leave.
An Echo of Mortimer Grimsby. The authorization, he says, is reflected.
The Quiet Frame
A frame with no glass in it, just a soft chair behind it and the sound of rain on a window that isn't there. It's the only quiet room in the gallery. A small plaque says RESTING IS A PRIVILEGE.
Rest (pay 250 gold)
You sit, and for a few minutes nothing reflects you at all. You stand up with steadier hands.
Rest, and leave a card as the fee
The chair keeps one of your cards in its cushion and lets you sleep.
Keep moving
You don't trust a quiet room in this place, and you're probably right.
An Echo of the Doppelganger, wearing a face it learned by heart. From here on the first unit you play each turn is copied for the enemy.
An Echo of Hortensia Clipwell, in a garden trimmed so neatly it hurts.
An Echo of the Rotheart, green glass that never stops growing.
Your Reflection
The last mirror before the end shows you as Primm would have made you: hair regulation length, posture perfect, smile approved. It's waiting to see what you'll do.
Look it in the eye
It looks back, and for a second you can't tell which of you blinked. You take some of its certainty with you, and it takes some of your strength.
Turn your back on it
You walk on without looking. The glass behind you cracks a little louder than it should.
Smash it
It breaks easily. Too easily. The pieces cut, and a shard of it goes on ahead of you to warn the room.
The Perfect Copy: your own deck, your own face, more HP and one extra card each turn.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/lab: The hatch opens on white light and a smell of disinfectant. A staircase of clean steel goes down through the roots of the forest where you woke up.
Everything about this place is familiar in the way a bruise is familiar. Your hands are shaking. You go down anyway.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Observation Deck
A glass gallery looks down on the cells: a kettle, a cracked mug, and a corkboard of notes about one subject. The newest notes are only a count of days.
Read the notes on the Subject
Drain cycles, power readings, a column labelled 'cooperative?' that someone has filled in with 'asks for his mother.' You put the notes down very carefully.
Drink the Path-ologists' tea
It is the first thing here that tastes like anything. You feel steadier.
Rifle the lockers
Keycards, a petty cash tin, and a half-written resignation letter.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Mutation
At half health the experiment sheds a piece of itself: a 1/1 Discarded Sample crawls out.
GRRRK. (The tag on its wrist reads: BATCH 12. DISCONTINUED.)
A 1/1 Discarded Sample crawls out.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Decontamination
Four nozzles hiss in four colors. A sensor asks whether your deck can carry more than one Path at a time.
The Draining Chamber
A round chamber, glass on every side, a chair at the center with straps worn pale. Cables run from the chair to four great tanks, each glowing a different colour. This is where it was done.
Put your hand on the glass
The four colors lean toward your palm like plants toward a window. They were yours. They remember.
Read the dials
Every cycle logged, every reading neat. You learn exactly how the machine works, which is how to break it.
Tear out the straps
They come away easily. They were only ever as strong as the people who buckled them.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/lab: A white room, three paces by four. Ten years of tally marks on the wall in rows of five, scratched with a spoon handle. Low down, where a child could reach, a drawing in four colors.
Someone is sitting under the drawing with her knees up and her hands bound, as if she has been keeping it company.
Took you long enough, Tess.
Tess?
That's what I called you, when we were small and you were too important to be called anything shorter.
They put me in your cell. My father calls it educational, and the worst of it is that he means it.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::even: Your old cell: ten years of tally marks, a child's drawing in four colors, and {rescuer} under it with her hands bound.
